### 1. pants. Personas tiesības uz tiesas aizsardzību

(1)	Katrai fiziskajai un juridiskajai personai (turpmāk — persona) ir tiesības uz savu aizskarto vai apstrīdēto civilo tiesību vai ar likumu aizsargāto interešu aizsardzību tiesā.  

(2)	Personai, kas griezusies tiesā, ir tiesības uz tās lietas izskatīšanu tiesā likumā noteiktajā procesuālajā kārtībā.

The Saeima has adopted and the President of State proclaims the following law:

Civil Procedure Law

Part A General Provisions

First Section
Basic Provisions of Civil Proceedings

Chapter 1 Principles of Civil Procedure

### Section 1. Right of a Person to Court Protection

(1)	Every natural and legal person (hereinafter — person) has the right to protection in court of their infringed or contested civil rights or interests protected by law.  

(2)	A person who has applied to a court has the right to have their case heard in court in the procedural manner prescribed by law.

### 2. pants. Tiesas spriešana civillietās

Civillietas tiesa izspriež kārtībā, kāda noteikta šajā likumā un likumā "Par tiesu varu".

### 3. pants. Tiesvedību civillietā regulējošo tiesību normu spēks laikā

Tiesvedību civillietā regulē civilprocesuālo tiesību normas, kas ir spēkā lietas izskatīšanas, atsevišķu procesuālo darbību izdarīšanas vai tiesas sprieduma izpildīšanas laikā.  
(07.04.2004. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.05.2004.)

### 4. pants. Tiesvedības instances civillietā

(1)	Civillietu pēc būtības izskata pirmās instances tiesa, bet pēc lietas dalībnieku sūdzības par šīs tiesas spriedumu — arī otrās instances tiesa apelācijas kārtībā, ja likumā nav noteikts citādi.  

(2)	Civillieta nav izskatāma pēc būtības augstākā tiesu instancē, iekams tā nav izskatīta zemākā tiesu instancē, ja šajā likumā nav noteikts citādi.  

(3)	Otrās instances tiesas spriedumu lietas dalībnieki var pārsūdzēt kasācijas kārtībā.  
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 08.09.2011. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 30.09.2011.)

### 5. pants. Tiesību normu piemērošana

(1)	A civil case is examined on the merits by a court of first instance, but upon complaint by the parties to the case against the judgment of this court — also by a court of second instance in appellate proceedings, unless otherwise provided by law.  

(2)	A civil case may not be examined on the merits in a higher court instance before it has been examined in a lower court instance, unless otherwise provided by this law.  

(3)	The parties to the case may appeal the judgment of a court of second instance in cassation proceedings.  
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 08.09.2011. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 30.09.2011.)

### 5. pants. Application of Legal Norms

(1)	The court adjudicates civil cases in accordance with laws and other normative acts, international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union legal norms.  

(2)	If an international agreement approved by the Saeima provides for provisions different from those in a Latvian law, the provisions of the international agreement shall apply.  

(3)	If the relevant legal issue is regulated by European Union legal norms that are directly applicable in Latvia, Latvian laws shall apply insofar as permitted by European Union legal norms.  

(4)	In cases prescribed by law or agreement, the court shall also apply the laws of other countries and international legal norms.  

(5)	If there is no law regulating the disputed relationship, the court shall apply a law that regulates similar legal relationships, but if there is no such law — shall be guided by the general principles and meaning of law.  

(6)	When applying legal norms, the court shall take into account case law.

(1)	Civil cases are examined in courts openly, except for cases concerning:

1)	determination of a child's origin;  

2)	approval and revocation of adoption;  

3)	dissolution or non-existence of marriage;  

4)	restriction of a person's legal capacity due to mental or other health disorders;  

41)	establishment of temporary guardianship;  

42)	suspension of the rights of a future representative;  

5)	unlawful removal of a child across the border to a foreign country or retention abroad and unlawful removal of a child across the border to Latvia or retention in Latvia;  

6)	custody and contact rights;  

7)	temporary protection against violence.  

(2)	Persons younger than 15 years of age who are not parties to the case or witnesses may be present at the court session only

with the permission of the court.  

(3)	Upon a reasoned request of a party to the case or at the court's discretion, the court session or part thereof may be declared closed:

1)	if it is necessary to protect state secrets or trade secrets;  

2)	if it is necessary to protect the private life and secrecy of correspondence of persons;  

3)	in the interests of minors;  

4)	if it is necessary to examine a person who has not reached 15 years of age;  

5)	in the interests of the administration of justice;  

6)	if it is necessary to protect information of limited access in cases concerning compensation for damages for competition law infringements.  

(31)	The court shall warn in writing persons who participate in the examination of a case whose materials include a state secret object or trade secret and who have the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials, of the obligation to keep the state secret or trade secret and of the liability provided for disclosure of a state secret or trade secret. (4)	Parties to the case participate in a closed court session, but if necessary — also experts and interpreters.  

(5)	If no party to the case objects, with the permission of the presiding judge of the court session, persons who have a special reason to do so may participate in a closed court session.  

(6)	A case in a closed court session shall be examined in compliance with all procedural rules.  

(7)	Court decisions in cases examined openly shall be announced publicly.  

(8)	In cases examined in a closed session, the operative part of the court decision shall be announced publicly. In cases concerning approval or revocation of adoption, the decision shall be announced in a closed court session.

### 13. Section. Language of Proceedings

(1)	Proceedings shall be conducted in the official language.  

(2)	Parties shall submit documents in foreign languages with a translation into the official language certified in the prescribed manner.  

(3)	The court may allow individual procedural actions also in another language if requested by one of the parties and if all parties agree thereto. The minutes of the court session and court decisions shall be written in the official language.  

(4)	For parties who receive state-provided legal aid in the case or are exempted from payment of court costs, the court shall ensure the right to familiarize themselves with the case materials and participate in procedural actions using

the assistance of an interpreter if they do not speak the language of proceedings.  
(With amendments made by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment concerning interpreters in part four enters into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision 114.)

### 14. Section. Immutability of Court Composition

(1)	Examination of a case on the merits shall take place with an immutable composition of the court.  

(2)	Replacement of a judge during the trial of a case shall be permitted only if he or she cannot complete the examination of the case due to transfer to another job, illness or other objective reasons.  

(3)	If during the trial of a case, until the preparation of the judgment in accordance with the content of the judgment specified in Section 193 of this Law, one of the judges is replaced by another judge, the trial of the case shall be commenced anew. The decision on replacement of a judge shall be made by the president of the court in the manner prescribed by the Law "On Judicial Power".  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The new wording of the first sentence of part three enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision 137.)

### 15. Section. Directness and Orality of Civil Case Examination

(1)	The court of first instance and the court of appeal, when examining a civil case, shall itself verify the evidence in the case.  

(2)	Persons invited and summoned to court shall give explanations and testimony orally. Testimony of previously questioned witnesses, written evidence and other materials shall be read out at the request of the parties. The court may not read out documents in the case if the parties agree thereto.  

(3)	In cases provided for in this Law or in European Union legal norms, the court shall examine applications, complaints and questions in written proceedings without holding a court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances that could be relevant to the resolution of the application, complaint or question, the court may examine it at a court session, having previously notified the parties of its time and place. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application, complaint or question.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 25.05.2006, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 2 Composition of the Court

### 16. Section. Judges

Cases in court shall be examined by judges appointed or confirmed in the manner prescribed by the Law "On Judicial Power".

### 17. Section. Resolution of Questions in Court

(1)	All questions that arise when examining a case collegially shall be decided by the judges by a majority of votes. None of the judges shall have the right to abstain from voting.  

(2)	In cases provided for in this Law, questions shall be decided by the judge individually.

### 18. Section. Inadmissibility of a Judge Participating in Repeated Examination of a Case

(1)	A judge who has participated in the examination of a case in the court of first instance may not participate in the examination of this case in the court of appeal or cassation, nor in a new examination of the case in the court of first instance if a judgment or decision on termination of proceedings or leaving a claim without examination has been set aside that was prepared with his or her participation.  

(2)	A judge who has participated in the examination of a case in the court of appeal or cassation may not participate in the examination of this case in the court of first instance or the court of appeal.

### 19. Section. Withdrawal or Recusal of a Judge

(1)	A judge shall not be entitled to participate in the examination of a case if he or she:

1)	in the previous examination of this case has been a party, witness, expert, interpreter or secretary of the court session;  

2)	is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with one of the parties;  

3)	is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with one of the judges who is in the composition of the court examining the case;  

4)	is personally directly or indirectly interested in the outcome of the case or there are other circumstances that give rise to justified doubts about his or her objectivity.  

(2)	If there are circumstances referred to in part one of this Section or in Section 18 of this Law, the judge shall withdraw himself or herself before the commencement of the trial of the case.  

(3)	If the judge discovers the circumstances referred to in part one of this Section during the trial of the case, the withdrawal shall be made at the court session, indicating the reasons for the withdrawal. In this case, the court shall postpone the examination of the case.  

(4)	If the judge has not withdrawn himself or herself, any party may, on the grounds referred to in this Section, file a recusal against the judge or several judges simultaneously, indicating the reasons for the withdrawal of each judge.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 20. Section. Filing of Recusal

(1)	A party may file a recusal in writing or orally, and an entry thereof shall be made in the minutes of the court session.  

(2)	A recusal shall be filed before the examination of the case on the merits has commenced. Later, a recusal may be filed if its grounds became known during the trial.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 21. Section. Procedure for Examination of a Filed Recusal

(1)	If a recusal is filed, the court shall hear the opinion of the other parties and shall hear the judge against whom the recusal is filed.  

(2)	A recusal filed at a court session shall be decided by the court in deliberation.  

(3)	In a case that a judge examines individually, the recusal filed shall be decided by the judge himself or herself.  

(4)	In a case examined collegially, the recusal filed shall be decided in the following manner:

1)	if a recusal is filed against one judge, it shall be decided by the remaining composition of the court. If the votes are equally divided, the judge is recused;  

2)	if a recusal is filed against several judges, it shall be decided by a majority of votes by the same court in full composition.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 22. Section. Consequences of Granting a Recusal

(1)	If a judge or several judges are recused, the case shall be examined by the same court in a different composition.  

(2)	If it is not possible to form a new composition of the court in the respective court, the case shall be sent to another district (city) court or

another regional court.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

Chapter 3
Jurisdiction and Venue of Civil Disputes

### 23. Section. Jurisdiction

(1) All civil disputes are subject to the jurisdiction of the court unless otherwise provided by law. This does not deprive the parties of the right, by mutual agreement, to refer the dispute for resolution to an arbitration court or to use mediation.  

(2)	The question of jurisdiction of a dispute shall be decided by the court or judge. If the court or judge finds that the dispute is not subject to the jurisdiction of the court, the decision shall indicate the institution within whose competence the resolution of this dispute falls.  

(3)	The court shall also examine applications of natural and legal persons that do not have the character of a civil dispute if so provided by law.  
(With amendments made by the law of 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 24. Section. Jurisdiction

(1) The district (city) court examines civil cases as a court of first instance. The Riga City Court examines cases whose materials include a state secret object, and cases concerning the protection of patent rights, plant varieties, topographies of semiconductor products, designs, trademarks, certification marks and geographical indications, cases concerning the protection of copyright and related rights, database makers' rights (sui generis) and cases concerning the protection of trade secrets against unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. If the case under examination includes a claim that is connected with a claim in a case that falls under the jurisdiction of both the Riga City Court and the district (city) court, or if a counterclaim that falls under the jurisdiction of the Riga City Court has been received in the district (city) court, the case shall be examined by the Riga City Court.

(11) The Court for Economic Cases as a court of first instance examines:

1) claims arising from reinsurance contracts;

2) claims arising from investment services or investment ancillary services contracts;

3) claims by investors from European Union Member States against the State of Latvia concerning investment protection;

4) claims arising from legal relations of groups of companies;

5) claims arising from mutual legal relations between participants (shareholders) of capital companies;

6) claims arising from financial collateral arrangements;

7) claims arising from transactions of capital companies with related parties within the meaning of the Commercial Law and the Financial Instrument Market Law;

8) claims arising from the transfer of undertakings and reorganisation of companies, excluding claims by employees;

9) claims arising from contractual obligations between participants in the construction process, including with subcontractors, in relation to the construction of such second and third group buildings for the realisation of which a building permit is required, excluding the construction of a separate one-dwelling or two-dwelling residential house and functionally related buildings;

10) claims concerning infringements of competition law;

11) claims concerning decisions of meetings of participants (shareholders) of capital companies;

12) applications for the liquidation and insolvency of credit institutions.

(12) If the case under examination includes a claim that is mutually connected with a claim in a case that falls under the jurisdiction of the Court for Economic Cases, or if a counterclaim that falls under the jurisdiction of the Court for Economic Cases has been received in the district (city) court, the case shall be examined by the Court for Economic Cases.

(13) If the case under examination includes a claim that is mutually connected with a claim in a case that falls under the jurisdiction of both the Court for Economic Cases and the Riga City Court in accordance with the jurisdiction specified in the third sentence of the first paragraph of this Section, or if a counterclaim that falls under the jurisdiction of the other court has been received in one of these courts, the case shall be examined by the Riga City Court.

(2) The regional court as an appellate instance examines cases by way of appeal.

(21) Decisions of the Court for Economic Cases appealed by way of appeal shall be examined by the Riga Regional Court.

(3) The Supreme Court as a cassation instance examines cases by way of cassation.
(In the wording of the law of 30.10.2014 with amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018., 25.10.2018., 28.02.2019., 01.10.2020.,
21.01.2021., 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 01.08.2022.)

### 25. Section. Jurisdiction of the regional court

(Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 26. Section

Bringing an action according to the defendant's declared place of residence or legal address

(1) An action against a natural person shall be brought in the court according to its declared place of residence.

(2) An action against a legal person shall be brought in the court according to its legal address.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 27. Section. Bringing an action if the defendant has no declared place of residence

(1) An action against a defendant who has no declared place of residence shall be brought according to his or her place of residence.

(2) An action against a defendant whose place of residence is not known or who has no permanent place of residence in Latvia shall be brought according to the location of his or her immovable property or according to his or her last known place of residence.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 28. Section. Jurisdiction at the plaintiff's choice

(1) An action arising in connection with the activities of a branch or representative office of a legal person may also be brought in the court according to the legal address of the branch or representative office.

(11) An action for the performance of obligations against a commercial company that has been reorganised by way of cross-border conversion to another Member State may, within two years from the entry into force of the reorganisation, also be brought according to the last legal address of the commercial company in Latvia.

(2) An action for the recovery of maintenance for a child or parent or for the establishment of paternity may also be brought by the plaintiff according to his or her declared place of residence.

(3) An action arising from personal injuries (Sections 1635, 2347–2353 of the Civil Law) may also be brought by the plaintiff according to his or her declared place of residence or according to the place where the injury was caused.

(4) An action for damage caused to the property of a natural or legal person may also be brought according to the place where it was caused.

(5) An action for the return of property or compensation for its value may also be brought by the plaintiff according to his or her declared place of residence.

(6) A maritime action may also be brought according to the place of arrest of the defendant's vessel.

(7) An action against several defendants who live or are located in different places may be brought according to the declared place of residence or legal address of one defendant.

(8) An action for divorce or nullity of marriage may be brought in the court at the plaintiff's choice in accordance with the provisions of Section 234 of this Law.

(9) An action arising from employment legal relations may also be brought by the plaintiff according to his or her declared place of residence or place of work.

(10) If the plaintiff in the cases referred to in this Section has no declared place of residence, he or she may bring the action according to his or her place of residence.
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 07.04.2004., 28.10.2010., 09.06.2011., 29.11.2012. and 16.03.2023.,
which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 29. Section. Exclusive jurisdiction

(1) An action concerning ownership rights and any other rights in rem to immovable property or its accessories, as well as an action for the registration of the said rights in the Land Register or for the deletion of these rights and for the exclusion of property from an inventory deed shall be brought according to the location of the property.

(2) Claims by creditors against an estate, where no heirs confirmed in inheritance rights or heirs who have accepted the inheritance are known, fall under the jurisdiction of the court according to the declared place of residence or place of residence of the testator, but if his or her declared place of residence or place of residence was not in Latvia or if it is not known — the court according to the location of the inherited property or parts thereof.

(3) Exclusive jurisdiction may also be established in other laws.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 30. Section. Contractual jurisdiction

(1) When concluding a contract, the parties to the contract may determine the court of first instance in which disputes that may arise between them concerning this contract or its performance are to be resolved.

(2) The exclusive jurisdiction established by law may not be modified by agreement of the parties.

If, in accordance with international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia and European Union legal norms, a case falls within the jurisdiction of a Latvian court, but the jurisdiction provisions of this law do not specify in which court the claim shall be brought, the claimant may bring the claim in any Latvian court of their choice, observing the provisions of Sections 23 and 24 of this law.

### 32. Section. Transfer of a Case Accepted in Proceedings to Another Court

(1)	A case which a court has accepted in its proceedings, observing the jurisdiction provisions, shall be examined by the court on the merits, even if during the examination of the case its jurisdiction has changed.  

(2)	A court may transfer a case for examination to another court if:

1)	when examining the case in court, it becomes apparent that it was accepted in violation of the jurisdiction provisions;  

2)	after the removal or challenge of one or more judges, their replacement in the same court is not possible;

(4)	Parties to the case may appeal the decision on the transfer of the case for examination to another court in the procedure specified in this law.  

(5)	The case shall be transferred for examination to another court when the time limit for appealing this decision has expired, but if the decision has been appealed — after the rejection of the complaint.  

(6)	A case that has been sent from one court to another court shall be accepted for examination by the court to which this case has been sent.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 29.11.2012. and 30.10.2014., which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

32.	Section 1. Transfer of a Case Accepted in Proceedings to Another Court to Ensure Faster Examination of the Case

(1)	A first instance court may initiate the transfer for examination to another court of the same instance of a claim proceedings case under its examination, except for a case whose jurisdiction is determined in accordance with Section 30 of this law, if the examination of the case on the merits has not been commenced and, by transferring the case to another court, its faster examination can be achieved. When initiating the transfer of a case for examination to another court of the same instance, preference shall be given to the transfer of a case to be examined in written proceedings.  

(2)	A regional court may initiate the transfer for examination to another regional court of an appeal case under its examination that has been initiated concerning a first instance court judgment (supplementary judgment), if the examination of the case on the merits has not been commenced and, by transferring the case to another court, its faster examination can be achieved.  

(3)	A case whose jurisdiction is determined in accordance with Section 28 or 29 of this law may be initiated for transfer by the instance court in whose examination the case is located for examination to another court of the same instance only upon a written request of the claimant.  

(4)	The decision on the transfer of a case from one court to another court upon the initiative of the chairperson of the court to which the case is subject to jurisdiction shall be adopted by the chairperson of a court one level higher. If a case in the proceedings of a district (city) court is to be transferred to a court located in another court district, the matter shall be decided by the chairperson of the regional court in whose territory of operation the court initiating the transfer of the case to another court is located. The decision shall be adopted in the form of a resolution and is not subject to appeal.  

(5)	The court that has initiated the transfer of the case to another court shall inform the parties to the case of the adoption of the decision referred to in paragraph four of this Section.  

(6)	If a case has been transferred for examination to another court in any of the proceedings instances to ensure its faster examination, repeated transfer of the case in the procedure specified in this Section is not permissible.  
(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015. with amendments made by the law of 21.01.2021., which enters into force on 01.03.2021.)

### 41. pants. Reimbursement of court costs

(1)	The court shall award to the party in whose favour the judgment is rendered all court costs paid by that party from the other party. If the claim is satisfied in part, the amounts specified in this Article shall be awarded to the claimant in proportion to the extent of the claims satisfied by the court, but to the defendant — in proportion to the part of the claims in which the claim was rejected. The state fee for an application for resumption of proceedings and re-examination of a case in which a default judgment has been rendered shall not be reimbursed.  

(2)	If the claimant withdraws the claim, he or she shall reimburse the defendant for the court costs incurred. In this case, the defendant shall not reimburse the court costs paid by the claimant. However, if the claimant does not maintain his or her claims because the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after the filing of the claim, the court shall, at the request of the claimant, award the court costs paid by the claimant from the defendant.  

(3)	If the claim is left without examination, the court shall, at the request of the defendant, award the court costs paid by the defendant from the claimant, except in the case specified in Paragraph 2 of the first part of Article 219 of this Law.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 08.09.2011. and 14.12.2017., which enter into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment in the first part regarding the deletion of the words "ancillary complaint against a court decision" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provisions paragraphs 139 and 140)

### 42. pants. Reimbursement of court costs to the state

(1)	Court costs, if the claimant has been exempted from their payment, shall be awarded from the defendant to state revenue in proportion to the part of the claim satisfied.  

(2)	If the claim is rejected, left without examination or if the claimant withdraws the claim, the court costs that have not been paid in advance shall be awarded from the claimant to state revenue. However, if the claimant does not maintain his or her claims because the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after the filing of the claim, the court costs shall be recovered to state revenue from the defendant.  

(3)	If the claim is satisfied in part, but the defendant is exempted from payment of court costs, they shall be recovered to state revenue from the claimant who is not exempted from payment of court costs, in proportion to the part of the claim that was rejected.  

(4)	If both parties are exempted from payment of court costs, the court costs shall be borne by the state.  

(5)	If the court approves a settlement and terminates the proceedings in the case, the court costs that have not been paid in advance shall be awarded from both parties to state revenue in equal amounts, unless otherwise provided in the settlement.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 23.04.2015., which enter into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 44. pants. Costs related to the conduct of a case and their reimbursement

(1)	Costs related to the conduct of a case are reimbursable in the following amounts:

1)	costs for payment of legal assistance:

a)	reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance in claims that are of a proprietary nature and in which the claim amount does not exceed 8500 euros, — in their actual amount, but not more than 30 percent of the satisfied part of the claims,

b)	reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance in claims that are of a proprietary nature and in which the claim amount is from 8501 euros to 57 000 euros, — in their actual amount, but not more than 2850 euros,

c)	reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance in claims that are of a proprietary nature and in which the claim amount exceeds 57 001 euros, — in their actual amount, but not more than 5 percent of the satisfied part of the claims,

d)	reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance in claims that are not of a proprietary nature, — in their actual amount, but not more than 2850 euros,

e)	reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance in claims that are not of a proprietary nature, and in cases which the court has recognised as complex, — in their actual amount, but not more than 4275 euros;  

2)	travel and subsistence costs in connection with appearance at a court hearing, as well as in connection with the presence or participation of parties or their representatives in the obtaining of evidence, at the request of Latvia when obtaining evidence abroad, — according to the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers for reimbursement of business trip expenses;  

3)	costs in connection with the obtaining of written evidence — in the actual amount of the costs;  

4)	interpreter costs in connection with the presence or participation of parties or their representatives in the obtaining of evidence, at the request of Latvia when obtaining evidence abroad, — in the actual amount of the costs, but not more than the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers;  

5)	interpreter costs in connection with the participation of parties in a court hearing — in the actual amount of the costs, but not more than the rates established by the Cabinet of Ministers.  

(11)	The actual amount of the reimbursable costs referred to in paragraph 1, clause 1 of this Article is considered to be both costs that have already been paid and costs for which an invoice has been issued in accordance with the agreement between the advocate and the party on the provision of legal assistance.  

(2)	Costs related to the conduct of a case are awarded from the defendant in favour of the plaintiff if his or her claim has been satisfied in full or in part, as well as when the plaintiff does not maintain his or her claims due to the fact that the defendant has voluntarily satisfied them after the filing of the claim.  

(3)	If the claim is rejected, costs related to the conduct of a case are awarded from the plaintiff in favour of the defendant.  

(4)	If the claim has been examined only in the court of first instance, reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance may not exceed 50 percent of the maximum reimbursement amount established in the first paragraph of this Article.  

(5)	The court may determine a smaller amount of reimbursable costs for payment of legal assistance, observing the principles of fairness and proportionality, as well as evaluating the objective circumstances related to the case, in particular — the degree of complexity and volume of the case, the number of court hearings during the examination of the case and the court instance in which the claim is being examined.

### 46. pants. Determination of procedural time limits

(1)	Procedural acts are performed within the time limits established by law. If procedural time limits are not established by law, they are determined by the court or judge. The duration of the time limit determined by the court or judge must be such that the procedural act can be performed.  

(2)	For the performance of a procedural act, a precise date or a time limit until a specified date, or a time period (in years, months, days or hours) is determined. If the procedural act does not have to be performed on a specified date, it may be performed throughout the entire specified time limit.  

(3)	A time limit may also be determined by indicating an event that must occur in any case.  

(4)	If the law establishes time limits for the court or judge for the examination of cases or the performance of other procedural acts and the performance of the relevant procedural act is notified to the participant in the case in accordance with Article 56.2 of this law, but the performance of the relevant procedural act within the time limit established by law is not possible, the court or judge is entitled to determine a more reasonable and longer time limit.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 47. pants. Commencement of the calculation of procedural time limits

(1)	A time limit that is calculated in years, months or days commences on the next day after the date or after the event that determines its commencement.  

(2)	A time limit that is calculated in hours commences in the next hour after the event that determines its commencement.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 48. pants. Expiry of procedural time limits

(1)	A time limit that is calculated in years expires on the corresponding month and date of the last year of the time limit. A time limit that is calculated in months expires on the corresponding date of the last month of the time limit. If a time limit calculated in months ends in a month that does not have a corresponding date, it expires on the last day of that month. A time limit that is determined until a specific date expires on that date.  

(2)	If the last day of the time limit is a Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday established by law, the next working day is considered to be the last day of the time limit.  

(3)	A procedural act for which the time limit expires may be performed on the last day of the time limit until twenty-four o'clock.  

(4)	If the procedural act is to be performed at the court, the time limit expires at the hour when the court finishes work. If a statement of claim, complaint or other postal items are submitted to a communications institution on the last day of the time limit until twenty-four o'clock, they are considered to have been submitted within the time limit.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 49. pants. Consequences of failure to observe procedural time limits

The right to perform procedural acts is lost upon the expiry of the time limit established by law or by the court. After the expiry of the procedural time limit, complaints and documents submitted are not accepted.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 50. pants. Suspension of Procedural Time Limits

Upon suspension of proceedings in a case, the calculation of the time limit is suspended. The calculation of the time limit stops at the moment when the circumstance that is the basis for suspension of proceedings has arisen. The calculation of the procedural time limit continues from the day when proceedings in the case are resumed.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 51. pants. Restoration of Procedural Time Limits

(1)	Missed procedural time limits shall be restored by the court upon application of a party to the case if it considers the reasons for missing the time limit to be justified.  

(2)	Upon restoring a missed time limit, the court simultaneously permits the performance of the missed procedural action.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 52. pants. Extension of Procedural Time Limits

Time limits set by the court or judge may be extended upon application of a party to the case.

### 53. pants. Procedure for Extension and Restoration of Procedural Time Limits

(1)	An application for extension of a time limit or restoration of a missed time limit shall be submitted to the court in which the missed action should have been performed, and it shall be examined in written proceedings. The parties to the case shall be notified in advance of the examination of the application in written proceedings, simultaneously sending them the application for extension of the time limit or restoration of the missed time limit.  

(2)	Documents necessary for the performance of the procedural action and justification for restoration of the time limit shall be attached to the application for restoration of a procedural time limit.  

(3)	A time limit set by a judge may be extended by the judge individually.  

(4)	An appeal may be filed against the refusal of the court or judge to extend or restore a time limit.  
(With amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 54. pants. Summoning to Court

(1)	Parties to a case shall be summoned to court by giving timely notice of the time and place of the court hearing or individual procedural action.  

(2)	Parties to a case shall be summoned to court by court summons. In cases provided for in this law, the defendant may be summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".  

(3)	Witnesses and experts shall be summoned to court by court summonses.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 04.02.2016., which enters into force on 29.02.2016. The amendment in the third part made in connection with interpreters enters into force on 31.07.2016. See transitional provision 114. point)

54.	1 pants. Determination of the Defendant's Place of Residence

(1)	If the defendant does not have a declared place of residence address in Latvia, the plaintiff has the obligation to indicate to the court the defendant's place of residence address if it is known to him or her.  

(2)	If the plaintiff has not succeeded in determining the defendant's place of residence, which is not in Latvia, for objective reasons, the court, upon a reasoned request of the plaintiff, may use the procedures provided for in international treaties binding on the Republic of Latvia or in European Union legal acts for determining the defendant's address.  
(In the wording of the law of 29.11.2012., which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 55. pants. Court Summons

The summons shall indicate:

1)	the name, surname, address of the natural person being summoned or called, or the name and legal address of the legal person;  

2)	the name and address of the court;  

3)	the time and place of appearance;  

4)	the name of the case in which the person is summoned or called;  

5)	an indication of the capacity in which the addressee is summoned or called;  

51)	an indication that videoconference will be used;  

6)	an indication that a person who has received the summons due to the absence of the addressee has the obligation to deliver it to the addressee;

(21)	Court documents shall be sent electronically, observing the following sequence:

1)	in the online system, if the addressee has notified the court that it consents to communication with the court using the online system;

2)	to the electronic mail address indicated by the addressee, if the addressee has notified the court that it consents to communication with the court using electronic mail;

3)	to the official electronic address of the addressee.

(22)	If it is not possible to send court documents to a natural person electronically in accordance with Paragraph 2.1 of this Section, they shall be sent to the address of the declared place of residence of the natural person, but in the case where an additional address is indicated in the declaration — to the additional address, unless the natural person has indicated another address for communication with the court. If the defendant does not have a declared place of residence address and has not indicated another address for communication with the court, court documents shall be delivered to the address indicated by the party to the case in accordance with the first part of Section 54.1 of this Law. Court documents may also be sent to the person's place of work.

(23)	A natural person has the obligation to be reachable in the online system, at the electronic mail address indicated by it or at the official electronic address, if the natural person has consented to electronic communication with the court, at the declared place of residence address, at the additional address indicated in the declaration or at another address indicated by this person for communication with the court.

(24)	If it is not possible to send court documents to a legal person electronically in accordance with Paragraph 2.1 of this Section, they shall be sent to its legal address.

(25)	A legal person has the obligation to be reachable in the online system, at the electronic mail address indicated by it or at the official electronic address, if the legal person has consented to electronic communication with the court.

(26)	When executing a foreign request for service of documents (Sections 672 and 681), documents shall be delivered to the addressee at the address indicated in the request, but if the addressee is not found at this address, they may be delivered in the manner prescribed in this Section.

(3)	Court documents may be delivered to the addressee personally against signature, if necessary, summoning the addressee by summons to appear at the court to receive the documents to be delivered.

(4)	A party to the case may, with the consent of the judge, receive court documents for delivery to another addressee in the case.

(5)	Court documents delivered by a courier or a party to the case shall be delivered to the addressee personally against signature. The time and date of delivery of the document shall be noted in the signature part and the signature part shall be returned to the court. If court documents are delivered by a bailiff or his or her assistant, an act drawn up by the bailiff or his or her assistant shall be submitted to the court.

Section 56.1 Date of Delivery and Service of Court Documents

(1)	If court documents have been delivered in the manner prescribed in Section 56 of this Law, except for the case provided for in the ninth part thereof, it shall be considered that the person has been notified of the time and place of the court hearing or procedural action or of the content of the relevant document and the court documents have been served:

1)	on the date when the addressee or another person has received them in accordance with the third, seventh or eighth part of Section 56 of this Law;

2)	on the date when the person has refused to receive them (Section 57);

3)	on the seventh day from the date of sending, if the documents have been sent by mail;

4)	on the third day from the date of sending, if the documents have been sent electronically;

5)	(deleted by law of 11.11.2021.).

(2)	The fact that court documents have been delivered to the address of the declared place of residence of a natural person, the additional address indicated in the declaration, the address indicated by the natural person for communication with the court or the legal address of a legal person and a certificate of delivery of the consignment has been received from the post office or the documents are sent back, does not in itself affect the fact of notification of the documents. The presumption that documents have been served on the seventh day from the date of their sending, if the documents have been sent by mail, or on the third day from the date of sending, if the documents have been sent electronically, may be rebutted by the addressee by indicating objective circumstances which, independently of his or her will, have been an obstacle to receiving the documents at the indicated address.
(As worded by law of 05.02.2009. with amendments made by laws of 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 23.11.2016. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 56.2 Delivery and Service of Court Documents to a Person Whose Place of Residence or Location is not in Latvia

(1)	Court documents shall be delivered to a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia and whose address is known:

1)	in the manner provided for in Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on the service in the Member States of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil or commercial matters (service of documents) (hereinafter — Regulation (EU) 2020/1784 of the European Parliament and of the Council) (Chapter 81);

2)	in the manner provided for in Article 13 of Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 July 2007 establishing a European Small Claims Procedure (hereinafter — Regulation No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council);

3)	in the manner provided for in international agreements binding on Latvia (Chapter 82);

4)	in the manner provided for in Chapter 83 of this Law;

5)	in the manner provided for in the Hague Convention of 15 November 1965 on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters (hereinafter — the Hague Convention of 1965) (Chapter 81.1).

(2)	If court documents have been delivered to a person in the manner prescribed in the first paragraph of this Section, it shall be considered that the person has been notified of the time and place of the court hearing or procedural action or of the content of the relevant document only if confirmation of service of the document has been received. Documents shall be considered served on the date indicated in the confirmation of service of documents.

(21) If court documents have been delivered to a person in the manner prescribed in the first paragraph of this Section and confirmation of their non-service has been received, the court shall evaluate the reasons for non-service of documents and shall determine the impact of non-service of documents on the proceedings in accordance with the provisions of this Law. After evaluating the reasons for non-service of documents, the court may deliver the documents again or use another method for service of documents. If it is not possible to serve the documents again, Section 59 of this Law shall apply.

(3)	This Section shall not apply if a person whose place of residence, location or legal address is not in Latvia conducts the case through an authorised representative in Latvia. In such a case, court documents shall be served in the general manner only to the representative.

(4)	This Section shall not apply if the declared place of residence or indicated address of the representative is outside Latvia. A summons, documents prepared by the court, as well as other electronically prepared documents shall be sent to a representative whose declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia by electronic mail, unless the representative has notified the court of the registration of his or her participation in the online system.
(As worded by law of 05.02.2009. with amendments made by laws of 29.11.2012., 01.06.2017., 31.05.2018., 11.11.2021. and
16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

(1)	A party to the case notifies the court of a change of email address, if he or she has consented to electronic communication with the court, or of a change of his or her address during case proceedings. (1)	A defendant whose address could not be ascertained in accordance with Section 54.1 of this law or to whom documents could not be delivered at the address indicated by a party to the case in accordance with the first paragraph of Section 54.1 of this law, or to whom court documents could not be delivered in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law, is summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(2)	Irrespective of the publication of the summons in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis", the plaintiff is entitled to publish the text of the court summons at his or her own expense in other newspapers.

(3)	The publication indicates the text of the summons corresponding to the content of the summons.

### 60. Section. Search for the Defendant if His or Her Whereabouts are Unknown

### 61. Section. Recording the Course of a Court Session

(1)	A court session protocol is written for each court session. The course of the court session is recorded in full using technical means.

(2)	The material obtained as a result of using sound recording or other technical means is attached to the case and stored together with it or entered and stored in the court information system.

(3)	In the cases provided for in this law, a protocol is also written for individual procedural actions performed outside the court session.

(4)	The course of the court session is not recorded using technical means if none of the parties to the case has appeared at the court session or if it is necessary for the court to verify information that is the subject of a state secret or commercial secret in order to ascertain the objective truth.

(5)	If the course of the court session has been recorded using sound recording, the relevant sound recording is available to persons who have the right to familiarise themselves with the case materials on the next working day after the day of the court session.

### 62. Section. Content of the Protocol

(1)	If the course of the court session is not recorded using technical means, the court session protocol indicates:

1)	the year, date, month and place of the court session;

2)	the name of the court examining the case, the composition of the court, the court session secretary, the advocate and the prosecutor participating in the case;

3)	that the course of the court session is recorded with technical means;

4)	the time of opening the court session;

5)	the name of the case;

6)	information about the arrival of the parties to the case, witnesses, experts and interpreters;

7)	information that the procedural rights and obligations have been explained to the parties to the case;

8)	information that witnesses, experts and interpreters have been warned of criminal liability;

9)	information about the examination of material and written evidence;

10)	court orders and decisions that have not been adopted in the form of separate procedural documents;

11)	information about the court's withdrawal to adopt a decision or render a judgment;

12)	information about the pronouncement of a judgment or a decision adopted in the form of a separate procedural document;

13)	information about the explanation of the content of the judgment or decision, the procedure and time limit for appeal;

14)	information about when the parties to the case may familiarise themselves with the court session protocol, the sound recording and the text of the judgment;

15)	the time of closing the court session;

16)	the time of signing the court session protocol.

(2)	A notation is made in the court session protocol about the plaintiff's withdrawal from the claim, as well as about the defendant having acknowledged the claim and the parties to the case having acknowledged legal facts.

(3)	The court session protocol is signed by the presiding judge of the court session and the court session secretary.

(4)	The protocol of individual procedural actions performed outside the court session must comply with the requirements of this Section.

### 65. Section. Types of Procedural Sanctions

In the cases specified in this law, the court may apply the following procedural sanctions:

1)	warning;

2)	removal from the courtroom;

3)	fine;

4)	compulsory bringing to court.

### 66. Section. Warning

The presiding judge of the court session issues a warning to a person who disturbs order during the trial of a case, and a notation thereof is made in the court session protocol.

### 67. Section. Removal from the Courtroom

If the parties to the case, witnesses, experts or interpreters repeatedly disturb order during the trial of a case, they may be removed from the courtroom by a court decision, but other persons present may be removed by an order of the presiding judge of the court session also without prior warning.

### 68. Section. Fine

(1)	The court imposes a fine in the cases and amounts specified in this law. If the court imposes a fine in a court session, the decision is entered in the court session protocol.

(2)	The court decision on the imposition of a fine is sent to the person on whom the fine has been imposed.

(3)	A person on whom a fine has been imposed may, within 10 days of the issuance of the court decision, request the court that imposed it to release this person from the fine or reduce its amount. This application is examined in a court session, having previously notified the person on whom the fine has been imposed of the session. The non-appearance of this person is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(4)	Fines imposed on officials are collected from their personal funds.

### 69. Section. Compulsory Bringing

(1)	In the cases specified in this law, the court may adopt a decision on the compulsory bringing of a person to court.

(2)	This decision is executed by the police institution indicated by the court.

### 70. Section. Administrative and Criminal Liability of Parties to the Case and Other Persons

Parties to the case and other persons who, by their action or inaction, obstruct the work of the court, in addition to the procedural sanctions provided for by law, may be held administratively or criminally liable in the cases specified by law.

### 71. pants. Civil Procedural Legal Capacity

(1)	Civil procedural legal capacity is the capacity to be vested with civil procedural rights and obligations.  

(2)	Civil procedural legal capacity is recognised equally for all natural and legal persons.

### 72. pants. Civil Procedural Active Capacity

(1)	The capacity to exercise civil procedural rights and fulfil obligations (civil procedural active capacity) belongs to adult natural persons insofar as it has not been restricted by a court, and to legal persons.  

(2)	For natural persons aged from 15 to 18 years, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives. For adult natural persons whose active capacity has been restricted by a court, cases in court are conducted by their representatives or — in cases provided by law — by representatives together with these persons. In cases conducted by the representatives of the aforementioned persons, the court also invites these persons themselves to participate.  

(3)	For natural persons who have not reached 15 years of age, cases in court are conducted by their legal representatives.  

(4)	In cases provided by law, minors are entitled to independently exercise their civil procedural rights and fulfil obligations. In such cases, at the court's discretion, the legal representatives of these persons may be invited to provide them with assistance in conducting the case.  

(5)	Adult natural persons whose active capacity has been restricted by a court nevertheless have full civil procedural active capacity in cases examining restrictions on their actions and freedom, as well as disputes between such person and their guardian. In such cases, the court invites a prosecutor and a representative of the orphan's court.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 73. pants. Concept of Participant in a Case

(1)	Participants in a case are the parties, third persons, representatives of the parties and third persons, the prosecutor and those state or local government institutions and persons to whom the law has granted the right to defend in court the rights of other persons and legally protected interests, institutions which are invited to give opinions in cases provided by law, as well as the representatives of these persons.  

(2)	A participant in a case may be a person who has civil procedural legal capacity and active capacity. State and local government institutions to whom the law has granted the right to defend in court the rights of other persons and legally protected interests may be participants in a case regardless of whether they are legal persons.  
(With amendments made by the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

73.1 pants. Bad Faith Use of Rights and Obligations or Contempt of Court

(1)	If a participant in a case uses their rights in bad faith or fulfils their obligations in bad faith, including provides the court with deliberately false information about facts and circumstances of the case or deliberately by action or inaction delays the examination of the case or matter, the judge issues a warning to the participant in the case or imposes a fine of up to 800 euros.  

(2)	For contempt of court — any conduct that demonstrates blatant disregard of the rules existing in a court session or in court — the court may impose a fine of up to 1000 euros on a participant in a case.  

(3)	For the submission of a deliberately false application, statement of claim or complaint, excluding ancillary complaints, appeals or cassation complaints, with the intention of achieving an unlawful objective or obstructing the protection of rights or legitimate interests, the court may impose a fine of up to 1200 euros on a party.  

(4)	The court imposes the fine referred to in paragraph three of this Article by a decision by which the case is decided on the merits or by which the application, claim or complaint is left without examination, or the proceedings are terminated. A person on whom a fine has been imposed may express objections to the imposition of the fine by submitting an appeal, cassation complaint or ancillary complaint, if the decision is appealable to a higher court instance. The imposition of a fine is not separately appealable from the decision by which it was imposed, when appealing the decision.  
(In the wording of the law of 23.04.2015 with amendments made by the law of 25.10.2018, which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

73.	2 pants. Restriction of Rights of Participants in a Case to Protect State Secrets

The court by a reasoned decision in the interests of protecting state secrets may restrict the rights of participants in a case who do not have the appropriate special authorisation for access to state secrets to familiarise themselves with the volume in which state secret objects are compiled, insofar as it does not affect the establishment of objective truth.  
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 74. pants. Parties, Their Rights and Obligations

(1)	In civil proceedings, any natural or legal person may be parties — the plaintiff and the defendant.  

(2)	Parties have the following civil procedural rights:

1)	to familiarise themselves with the case materials and make copies thereof;  

2)	to participate in a court session;  

3)	to file challenges;  

4)	to submit evidence;  

5)	to participate in the examination of evidence;  

6)	to file petitions;  

7)	to give oral and written explanations to the court;  

8)	to express their arguments and considerations;  

9)	to raise objections to the petitions, arguments and considerations of other participants in the case;  

10)	to appeal court judgments and decisions;  

11)	to receive the judgment, decisions and other documents in the case or copies thereof, as well as to exercise other procedural rights granted to them by this law.  

(3)	The plaintiff is additionally entitled to:

1)	renounce the claim in full or in part;  

2)	reduce the amount of the claim;  

3)	amend in writing the basis or subject matter of the claim or increase the amount of the claim before the examination of the case on the merits has commenced (Article 163 of this law).

(5)	The parties may agree on the use of mediation, as well as conclude a settlement or agree on the referral of the case for examination to an arbitral tribunal.  

(6)	Parties must exercise their rights and fulfil their obligations in good faith.  

(7)	Parties have the obligation to:

1)	appear at the court's invitation;  

2)	notify in writing in a timely manner of the reasons why they cannot appear at a court session, submitting evidence thereof;  

21) ensure the assistance of an interpreter if they do not speak the language of the proceedings, except in cases provided in this law, including ensuring the assistance of an interpreter also for experts or witnesses summoned at the request of the parties, if the expert or witness does not speak the language of the proceedings;  

3)	fulfil other procedural obligations imposed on them in accordance with this law.

### 77. Section. Succession of Procedural Rights of a Party

(1)	If one of the parties in a case withdraws (death of a natural person, a legal person ceases to exist, assignment of a claim, transfer of debt and other circumstances), the court shall allow this party to be replaced by its successor in rights.

(11)	An application for succession of procedural rights shall be examined in written proceedings, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session.

(12)	Before adopting a decision on succession of procedural rights, the court shall verify in the Court Information System whether the party that has assigned the claim is registered in the Register of Applicants and Debtors of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund. If it is established that the party is a maintenance debtor, the court shall adopt a decision rejecting the application for succession of the party's procedural rights.

(2)	Succession of rights is possible at any stage of the proceedings.

(21) An appeal may be filed against the court's decision.

(3)	All actions performed in the proceedings until the moment of entry of the successor in rights shall be equally binding on the successor in rights as they were on the person whose rights have been succeeded.

### 78. Section. Participation of Third Parties in Civil Proceedings

(1)	A third party in civil proceedings may be a natural or legal person whose rights or obligations towards one of the parties may be affected by the judgment in the case.

(2)	The provisions on procedural legal capacity and capacity to act of parties shall apply to third parties, they shall have the procedural rights and obligations of parties with the exceptions set out in Section 80 of this Law.

(3)	Third parties may enter the case before the examination of the case on the merits has been completed in the court of first instance. They may also be invited to participate in the case at the request of the parties or the prosecutor.

### 79. Section. Third Parties with Independent Claims

(1)	Third parties who assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case by submitting a statement of claim.

(2)	Third parties with independent claims shall have the rights and obligations of a claimant.

### 80. Section. Third Parties without Independent Claims

(1)	Third parties who do not assert independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute may enter the case on the side of the claimant or the defendant if the judgment in the case may affect the rights or obligations of these persons towards one of the parties.

(2)	Third parties who do not assert independent claims shall have the procedural rights and obligations of a party, except for the rights to amend the basis or subject matter of the claim, to increase or reduce the amount of the claim, to withdraw from the claim, to acknowledge the claim or to conclude a settlement, as well as to request enforcement of the court judgment.

(3)	Applications for inviting third parties and applications of third parties for entering the case on the side of the claimant or the defendant shall indicate the grounds on the basis of which the third parties are to be invited or allowed to participate in the case.

### 81. Section

Court Decision on Inviting or Allowing a Third Party to Participate in a Case

A third party shall be invited or allowed to participate in a case in accordance with a court decision. A decision granting or rejecting a request for inviting a third party or for entry into a case shall not be subject to appeal. The decision shall be sent to the third party to the official electronic address or by registered mail.

### 82. Section. Right to Representation in Civil Proceedings

(1)	Natural persons may conduct their cases in court themselves or through authorised representatives.

(2)	Cases of legal persons in court shall be conducted by their officials acting within the powers granted by law, statutes or regulations, or by other authorised representatives of legal persons.

(3)	Cases of state or local government institutions which have been granted by law the right to defend the rights of other persons or interests protected by law shall be conducted in court by the head of the institution or a representative authorised by him or her.

(4)	The participation of the participants in the case referred to in paragraphs one, two and three of this Section in civil proceedings shall not deprive them of the right to invite an advocate to their case for the provision of legal assistance. In this case, the scope of the advocate's powers shall be determined by Section 86 of this Law, he or she shall not provide explanations on the substance of the case.

### 84. pants. Persons who cannot be representatives in civil proceedings

(1)	The following persons cannot be representatives in civil proceedings:

1)	a person who has not reached the age of majority;  

2)	a person for whom guardianship has been established;  

3)	a person who has been deprived by court judgment of the right to conduct cases of other persons;  

4)	a person who is in a relationship of kinship up to the third degree or affinity up to the second degree with the judge who is to hear the case;  

5)	a person who has provided legal assistance to the other party to the dispute in this or another related case;  

6)	a mediator who has participated in mediation in this or another related case.  

(2)	Upon establishing the circumstances referred to in paragraph one of this Section, the court shall not admit such person to the hearing of the case.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 22.05.2014, which enter into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 85. pants. Formalisation of representation

(1)	Representation of natural persons shall be formalised by a notarially certified power of attorney. The represented person may express the authorisation of the representative orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  

(2)	Representation of legal persons shall be formalised by a written power of attorney or documents certifying the rights of an official to represent the legal person without special authorisation.  

(3)	The authorisation of an advocate to provide legal assistance shall be certified by a warrant. If an advocate appears as an authorised representative of a party, this authorisation shall be certified by a written power of attorney.  

(31)	The authorisation of a provider of state-ensured legal aid to provide legal assistance shall be certified by an assignment issued by the responsible state institution for the provision of legal aid.  

(32)	Representation by a professional patent attorney shall be formalised by a written power of attorney and a document certifying the status of the patent attorney.  

(4)	Parents, adoptive parents, guardians and curators shall present to the court documents certifying their rights.  

(5)	If the authorised representative is one of the procedural participants on behalf of other participants, the represented person may express his or her authorisation orally in court, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001, 12.02.2004, 17.02.2005, 10.12.2015 and 11.11.2021, which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 86. pants. Scope of powers of representatives

(1)	A representative has the right to perform all procedural acts on behalf of the represented person, except those for which special authorisation is required. If a natural person conducts a case through an authorised representative, court notifications and documents shall be sent only to the representative. If the authorised representative of a natural person whose declared place of residence or indicated address is outside Latvia does not indicate an e-mail address or does not notify of the registration of his or her participation in the online system, court notifications and documents may be sent only to the represented person.  

(2)	Full or partial withdrawal from a claim, amendment of the subject matter of a claim, filing of a counterclaim, full or partial acknowledgment of a claim, conclusion of a settlement, referral of a case to arbitration, appeal of court judgments in the procedure of appeal or cassation, submission of writs of execution for enforcement, receipt of adjudged property or money, termination of enforcement proceedings must be specifically indicated in the power of attorney issued by the represented person.  

(3)	All procedural acts performed by a representative in accordance with the power of attorney issued to him or her shall be binding on the represented person.  

(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003 and 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017.)

### 87. pants. Early termination of representation

(1)	The represented person may at any time revoke the authorisation given to the representative, immediately notifying the court thereof in writing. An oral notification of the revocation of authorisation may be given at a court session, and an entry thereof shall be made in the court session record.  

(2)	A representative has the right to refuse to conduct a case, notifying the represented person and the court thereof in writing in due time.  
(With amendments made by the law of 23.11.2016, which enters into force on 01.01.2017.)

Participation of state or local government institutions and individual persons in proceedings, defending the rights of other persons

### 90. pants. Participation of a prosecutor in civil proceedings

(1)	A prosecutor has the right to participate in the hearing of a case if he or she has brought a claim, submitted an application or his or her participation is mandatory.  

(2)	A prosecutor has the right to bring a claim or submit an application to a court if:

1)	it is necessary for the protection of state or local government rights and interests provided for by law;  

2)	the rights or legitimate interests of minors, persons under guardianship, persons with disabilities, prisoners or other such persons who have limited possibilities to defend their rights have been violated;  

3)	a violation of law has been established during a prosecutor's inspection.  

(3)	The participation of a prosecutor in the hearing of a case is mandatory if it is provided for by law or the court has deemed it necessary.  

(4)	A prosecutor who participates in the hearing of a case has the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, file challenges, submit evidence, participate in the examination of evidence, submit requests, give an opinion on issues that have arisen in the course of the trial and on the merits of the case as a whole, submit a protest against a court judgment or decision, receive a judgment, decision or other document in the case or a copy thereof, as well as perform other procedural acts provided for by law.  

(5)	If a prosecutor is a party to a case, he or she has the right to submit a protest against a court judgment or decision in all cases where other parties to the case have the right to appeal a judgment or decision.  

(6)	The withdrawal by a prosecutor from a claim or application he or she has submitted to a court shall not deprive the person for whose interests the prosecutor submitted the claim or application of the right to request that the court hear the case on the merits.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)
