### 91. Section. Recusal or Challenge of a Prosecutor

(1) A prosecutor may not give an opinion in a case if he or she has previously been a judge, party, third person, representative, witness, expert, interpreter or court session secretary in the examination of that case, as well as in the cases specified in Clauses 2,
3 and 4 of the first part of Section 19 of this Law.

(2) In the presence of the aforementioned circumstances, the prosecutor must recuse himself or herself before the commencement of the trial.

(3) If the prosecutor has not recused himself or herself, the participants in the case are entitled to file a challenge to the prosecutor on the grounds specified in this Section.

(4) A challenge to a prosecutor is filed and the court decides it in the procedure laid down in Sections 20 and 21 of this Law.

Part Three Evidence

Chapter 15
General Provisions on Evidence

### 92. Section. Evidence

Evidence is information on the basis of which the court determines the existence or non-existence of facts that are relevant to the adjudication of the case.
(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 93. Section. Duty to Prove and Submit Evidence

(1) Each party must prove the facts on which it bases its claims or objections. The plaintiff must prove the validity of his or her claims. The defendant must prove the validity of his or her objections.

(2) Evidence is submitted by the parties and other participants in the case. If it is not possible for the parties or other participants in the case to submit evidence, the court shall request it at their reasoned request.

(21) If the parties submit evidence or the court requests evidence that contains a state secret object, the court

shall request from the competent authority that has classified the information as a state secret object an opinion on the right of the participant in the case to become acquainted with it.

(3) Evidence shall be submitted to the court no later than 14 days before the court session, unless the judge has set a different time limit for the submission of evidence. The second sentence of the fourth part of Section 48 of this Law does not apply to this time limit.

(31) During the trial of a case, evidence may be submitted at the reasoned request of a party or other participants in the case if it does not delay the trial of the case or the court has recognised the reasons for failure to submit evidence in a timely manner as justified, or the evidence concerns facts that became known during the trial of the case.

(32) If a participant in a case submits evidence after the expiry of the time limit and the court does not recognise the reasons for failure to submit it in a timely manner as justified, it shall impose a fine of up to 750 euros on the participant in the case.

(33) A court decision to refuse to accept evidence is not subject to appeal, but objections to it may be expressed in an appeal or cassation complaint.

(4) If the court finds that no evidence has been submitted for any of the facts on which the party's claims or objections are based, it shall notify the parties thereof and, if necessary, set a time limit for the submission of evidence.
(In the wording of the Law of 31.10.2002, with amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003, 07.09.2006, 29.11.2012, 12.09.2013 and
11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 94. Section. Relevance of Evidence

The court shall accept only evidence that is relevant to the case.

### 95. Section. Admissibility of Evidence

(1) The court shall admit only the means of proof provided for by law.

(2) Facts which, in accordance with law, can be proved only by specific means of proof may not be proved by any other means of proof.

### 96. Section. Grounds for Exemption from Proof

(1) If the court recognises a fact as generally known, it need not be proved.

(2) Facts established by a judgment that has entered into legal force in one civil case need not be proved again when trying other civil cases in which the same parties participate.

(3) A court judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force, a prosecutor's order for punishment, as well as a decision to terminate criminal proceedings on non-rehabilitating grounds, is binding on the court examining a case concerning the civil liability of the person in respect of whom the relevant decision was adopted, only on the question of whether the criminal act or omission occurred or was committed or permitted by the same person.

(4) Facts which, in accordance with law, are considered to be established need not be proved. Such presumptions may be challenged in the general procedure.

(5) A party need not prove facts which the other party has not challenged in the procedure laid down in this Law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 31.10.2002 and 05.02.2009, which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 97. Section. Evaluation of Evidence

(1) The court shall evaluate evidence according to its inner conviction, which is based on evidence comprehensively, fully and objectively examined at the court session, guided by legal consciousness based on the laws of logic, scientific findings and observations gained in life.

(2) No evidence has a predetermined force that would bind the court.

(3) The court must indicate in the judgment why it gave preference to one piece of evidence over another and recognised some facts as proved and others as not proved.

Chapter 16 Securing of Evidence

### 98. Section. Admissibility of Securing Evidence

(1) If a person has grounds to believe that the submission of evidence necessary for him or her may later be impossible or difficult, he or she may request that this evidence be secured.

(2) Applications for securing evidence may be submitted at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

(3) Evidence before the initiation of a case in court shall be secured by the district (city) court in which the claim is to be filed. Evidence after the initiation of a case in court shall be secured by the court examining the case.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 14.12.2006 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

### 99. Section. Application for Securing Evidence

The application for securing evidence shall indicate:

1) the applicant's name, surname, the case for the examination of which it is necessary to secure evidence, or its possible participants;

2) the evidence that needs to be secured;

3) the facts for the proof of which this evidence is necessary;

4) the reasons for which the applicant requests the securing of evidence.

### 100. pants

Procedure for deciding an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim

(1) The court or judge shall decide on an application for preservation of evidence within 10 days from the date of its receipt.

(2) If the application for preservation of evidence is decided by the court, the applicant and possible parties to the case shall be summoned to the court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the submitted application.

(3) By decision of a judge, evidence may be preserved without summoning possible parties to the case only in urgent cases, including urgent cases of intellectual property rights infringement or possible infringement, or in cases where it is not possible to determine who will be the parties to the case.

(4) If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted without the presence of the possible defendant or other party to the case, he or she shall be notified of this decision no later than the moment of execution of the said decision.

(5) The examination of witnesses, as well as on-site inspection and expert examination, shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(6) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for submission of the statement of claim, not exceeding 30 days.

(7) When granting an application for preservation of evidence before filing a claim, the judge may require that the possible plaintiff, by depositing a specified sum of money into the bailiff's deposit account or by providing an equivalent guarantee, secure coverage of the losses that the defendant may incur in connection with the preservation of evidence.

(8) The minutes of the court hearing and the materials collected in preserving the evidence shall be kept until they are requested by the court examining the case.

(9) A secondary complaint may be filed against the judge's decision to refuse to accept an application for preservation of evidence or the decision referred to in paragraph three of this Section. If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for filing a secondary complaint shall be counted from the date of issue or dispatch of the decision.
(As worded by the Law of 14.12.2006 with amendments made by the Law of 20.12.2010, which enters into force on 01.01.2011.)

### 101. pants

Procedure for examining an application for preservation of evidence after initiation of a case in court

(1) An application for preservation of evidence shall be examined at a court hearing in accordance with the relevant provisions of this law.

(2) The submitter of the application and other parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the application for preservation of evidence.

### 102. pants. Court commissions

(1) If it is not possible for the court examining the case to collect evidence located in another city or district, the court or judge shall commission the relevant court to perform specific procedural actions.

(2) The decision on a court commission shall briefly set out the substance of the case being examined and indicate the circumstances to be clarified and the evidence to be collected by the court executing the commission. This decision shall be binding on the court to which it is addressed, and it must be executed within 15 days.
(With amendments made by the Law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 103. pants. Procedure for executing court commissions

(1) Court commissions shall be executed at a court hearing in the procedure established by this law. The parties to the case shall be notified of the time and place of the hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the execution of the commission.

(2) The minutes and other case materials collected in executing the commission shall be sent to the court examining the case within three days.

103.1 pants. Termination of preservation of evidence

If a decision on preservation of evidence has been adopted before filing a claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge shall, upon receipt of an application from the possible plaintiff or defendant, adopt a decision to cancel the preservation of evidence.
(As worded by the Law of 14.12.2006, which enters into force on 01.03.2007.)

103. 2 pants. Compensation for losses caused by preservation of evidence

The defendant shall be entitled to claim compensation for losses incurred in connection with the preservation of evidence if the preservation of evidence has been cancelled in the case provided for in Section 103.1 of this law, if the claim filed against him or her has been dismissed, left without examination, or the proceedings have been terminated in the cases provided for in points 2 and 4 of Section 223 of this law.

### 104. pants. Explanations of parties and third persons

(1) Explanations of parties and third persons that contain information about facts on which their claims or objections are based shall be recognised as evidence if they are confirmed by other evidence examined and evaluated at the court hearing.

(2) If one party acknowledges facts on which the other party bases its claims or objections, the court may recognise such

facts as proven if it has no doubt that the acknowledgement has not occurred under the influence of fraud, violence, threats or mistake, or in order to conceal the truth.

### 105. pants. Witness testimony

(1) A witness is a person who has knowledge of facts relating to the case and who has been summoned to the court hearing by the court.

(2) A party to the case, when requesting that a witness be examined, must indicate what circumstances relevant to the case the witness can confirm.

(3) No person summoned to court as a witness shall have the right to refuse to give testimony, except in the cases provided for in Sections 106 and 107 of this law.

(4) A witness may be examined only about facts to be clarified in this case.

(5) Witness testimony based on information whose source is not known or on information provided by other persons, if these persons have not been examined, cannot be evidence.

### 106. pants. Persons who cannot be witnesses

The following may not be summoned and examined as witnesses:

1) clergy — about circumstances that have become known to them while hearing confession, and persons who, by virtue of their office or profession, do not have the right to disclose information entrusted to them — about such information;

2) minors — about circumstances that testify against their parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters;

3) persons who, due to their physical or mental deficiencies, are unable to correctly perceive circumstances that are relevant to the case;

4) children up to seven years of age;

5) persons who have participated in mediation in this or another related case.
(With amendments made by the Law of 22.05.2014, which enters into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 107. pants. Persons who may refuse to testify

(1) The following may refuse the duty to testify:

1) relatives of the parties in the direct line and in the collateral line in the first and second degree, the spouse and first-degree in-laws, as well as family members of the parties;

2) guardians and trustees of the parties, as well as persons who are under the guardianship or trusteeship of the parties;

3) persons who are in litigation with one of the parties in another case.

(2) The court must explain to the said persons their right to refuse to testify.

### 108. pants. Duties of a witness

(1) A person summoned as a witness must appear in court and give truthful testimony about circumstances known to him or her. A witness may also be examined using videoconference in court at the witness's location or in a place specially equipped for this purpose.

(2) A witness must answer questions from the court and the parties to the case.

(3) The court may examine a witness at his or her location if he or she cannot appear following the court summons due to illness, age, disability or other justifiable reason.

(With amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 109. pants. Liability of a witness

(1) For refusal to testify for reasons that the court has recognised as unjustifiable, and for deliberately giving false testimony, a witness shall be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(2) If a witness fails to appear following a court or judge summons without justifiable reason, the court may impose a fine of up to 60 euros on him or her or have him or her brought to court by force.
(With amendments made by the Law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 110. Article. Written Evidence

Written evidence is information about facts that are significant to the case, and this information is recorded in documents, other writings, as well as in relevant recording systems (audio, video tapes, computer diskettes, etc.) by means of letters, numbers and other written signs or technical means.

### 111. Article. Procedure for Submitting Written Evidence

(1)	When submitting written evidence to the court or requesting that it be requested, the parties to the case must indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2)	Written evidence shall be submitted in the original or in the form of a copy certified in the prescribed manner. If a part of a written document or other writing is sufficient to clarify the facts that are significant to the case, an extract thereof may be submitted to the court.

(3)	Original documents, as well as written evidence certified in the prescribed manner, shall be submitted if laws or international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia provide that specific facts may be proved only with original documents or copies certified in the prescribed manner.

(4)	If written evidence has been submitted to the court in the form of a copy, the court, upon a reasoned request of the parties to the case or on its own initiative, shall be entitled to request that the original be submitted or produced if it is necessary to clarify the circumstances of the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 112. Article. Procedure for Requesting Written Evidence

(1)	The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, shall be entitled to request written evidence from state and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(2)	A party to the case who requests the court to request written evidence must describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she believes that it is in the possession of the said person.

(3)	State and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons who are unable to submit the requested written evidence or to submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge must notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.

(4)	If a party refuses to submit the requested written evidence to the court, without denying that this evidence is in its possession, the court may recognise as proven those facts for the confirmation of which the opposing party has referred to this written evidence.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 113. Article. Return of Written Evidence in the Case

The court shall return the originals of written evidence to the submitter after converting them into electronic form and attaching them to the case materials. If it is not possible to convert the originals of written evidence into electronic form, the court shall return them to the submitter after the court judgment has entered into legal force.

(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 114. Article. Inspection of Written Evidence at Its Place of Storage

If the submission of written evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the written evidence at their place of storage.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 115. Article. Material Evidence

Material evidence is physical objects which, by their properties, characteristics or very existence, may be useful in clarifying facts that are significant to the case.

### 116. Article. Submission and Requesting of Material Evidence

(1)	A party to the case who submits material evidence to the court or requests that it be requested must indicate what circumstances significant to the case this evidence may confirm.

(2)	A party to the case who requests the court to request material evidence must describe this evidence and give reasons why he or she believes that it is in the possession of the said person.

(3)	The court or judge, upon a reasoned request of a party to the case, shall be entitled to request material evidence from state and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons.

(4)	State and local government institutions, other natural and legal persons who cannot submit the requested material evidence or cannot submit it within the time limit set by the court or judge must notify the court thereof in writing, indicating the reasons.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 117. Article. Inspection of Material Evidence at Its Place of Storage

If the submission of material evidence to the court is impossible or difficult due to their number, volume or other reasons, the court may carry out an inspection and examination of the material evidence at their place of storage or instruct a bailiff to do so.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 118. Article. Storage of Material Evidence

(1)	Material evidence shall be attached to the case or stored in the court's material evidence repository.

(2)	Objects that cannot be brought to court shall be stored at their location. They shall be described and, if necessary, photographed or filmed. The descriptions and images shall be attached to the case.

(3)	The court shall inspect perishable material evidence immediately, notifying the parties to the case thereof. After the inspection, this material evidence shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received.

### 119. Article. Return of Material Evidence

(1)	Material evidence shall be returned to the persons from whom it was received or transferred to the persons to whom the court has recognised rights to these objects after the court judgment has entered into legal force.

(2)	Material evidence which, by law or court judgment, may not be returned to the parties to the case or to the persons from whom it was received, shall be transferred by the court to the relevant state institutions.

(3)	In individual cases, material evidence may be returned before the judgment has entered into legal force if this does not prejudice the examination of the case.

### 120. Article. Liability for Failure to Submit Written and Material Evidence

If the court has not been notified that it is not possible to submit the requested written or material evidence, or if it has not been submitted for reasons which the court has recognised as unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 40 euros on the guilty person. Payment of the fine does not release this person from the obligation to submit the evidence requested by the court.
(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 121. Article. Expert Examination

(1)	The court shall order an expert examination in the case upon a party's request in cases where special knowledge in science, technology, art or another field is necessary to clarify facts significant to the case. If necessary, the court shall order several expert examinations.

(2)	The expert examination shall be carried out by persons specified in the Law on Forensic Experts. The expert shall be chosen by the parties by mutual agreement, but if such agreement is not reached within the time limit set by the court, the expert shall be chosen by the court. If necessary, several experts may be chosen.

(3)	The parties to the case shall have the right to submit to the court questions on which, in their opinion, the expert should give an opinion. The court shall determine the questions on which an expert opinion is necessary. The court must give reasons for rejecting questions posed by the parties to the case.

(4)	The court decision on ordering an expert examination shall indicate on what questions an expert opinion is necessary and who is instructed to carry out the expert examination.

(5)	The expert examination shall be carried out in court or outside the court if carrying it out in court is not possible or is difficult.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 122. Section. Duties and Rights of an Expert

(1) A person appointed as an expert must appear upon summons by the court. An expert may also be examined using videoconference in court at the expert's location or at a specially equipped place for this purpose.

(2) If a summoned expert does not appear at a court hearing for reasons which the court has found to be unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 60 euros on him or her.

(3) An expert has the right to familiarise himself or herself with the case materials, to ask questions of the parties and witnesses, and also to request the court to obtain additional materials.

(4) An expert gives an objective opinion in his or her own name and is personally responsible for it.

(5) An expert may refuse to give an opinion if the materials provided to him or her for examination are insufficient or if the questions posed exceed the limits of his or her special knowledge. In such cases, the expert notifies the court in writing that it is not possible to give an opinion.

(6) For refusal without justified reason to perform his or her duties or for knowingly giving a false opinion, an expert is liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 12.09.2013, which enter into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 123. Section. Removal or Challenge of an Expert

(1) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case if he or she has previously been a judge, a party to the case in the examination of this case, or in the cases provided for in points 2, 3 and 4 of the first part of Section 19 of this Law.

(2) An expert may not participate in the examination of a case also if:

1) he or she is or has been dependent on a party or another participant in the case by official position or otherwise;

2) one of the parties in the case at hand has been connected with the performance of this expert's professional duties before the initiation of the case in court;

3) it is established that he or she is not competent.

(3) Where the said circumstances exist, the expert must remove himself or herself before the commencement of the trial of the case.

(4) If the expert has not removed himself or herself, the parties have the right to file a challenge against him or her on the grounds referred to in this Section.

(5) A challenge to an expert is filed and the court decides it in the procedure laid down in Sections 20 and 21 of this Law.

### 124. Section. Expert Opinion

(1) An expert opinion must be reasoned and substantiated.

(2) The opinion is expressed in writing and submitted to the court. An expert opinion must contain a precise description of the research carried out, the conclusions drawn as a result thereof, and reasoned answers to the questions posed by the court. If an expert, in carrying out an examination, establishes circumstances which are relevant to the case and about which questions have not been posed to him or her, he or she has the right to indicate these circumstances in his or her opinion.

(3) If several experts are appointed, they have the right to consult among themselves. If the experts reach a common opinion, it is signed by all the experts. If the opinions of the experts differ, each expert writes a separate opinion.

### 125. Section. Evaluation of an Expert Opinion

(1) The court evaluates an expert opinion in accordance with the provisions of Section 97 of this Law.

(2) If an expert opinion is not sufficiently clear or is incomplete, the court may order a supplementary examination, assigning its performance to the same expert.

(3) If an expert opinion is not substantiated, and also in the case where the opinions of several experts are contradictory, the court may order a repeated examination, assigning its performance to another expert or experts.

### 126. Section. Opinion of an Institution

The court evaluates the opinion of an institution invited in the procedure laid down in Section 89 of this Law as evidence. The court's non-adherence to the opinion must be reasoned in the decision adopted in the case.
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

Fourth Division Claim Proceedings

Chapter 18 Filing of a Claim

### 127. Section. Persons Who May File a Claim in Court

(1) Persons who have civil procedural capacity have the right to file a claim in court to defend their infringed or contested civil rights.

(2) On behalf of minors, a claim is filed by the legal representatives of these persons, but in the cases provided for in the fourth part of Section 72 of this Law, the claim may be filed by the minor himself or herself. On behalf of persons under guardianship, a claim is filed by the representatives of these persons together with the person under guardianship or by themselves alone in place of the respective person if so determined by the court, except for the case provided for in the fifth part of Section 72.

(3) A prosecutor, state or local government institutions or persons who have been granted rights by law to defend in court the rights of other persons or interests protected by law may file a claim to defend the infringed or contested civil rights of these persons.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012, which enters into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 132. Section. Grounds for Refusal to Accept a Statement of Claim

(1) The judge shall refuse to accept a statement of claim if:

1) the dispute is not subject to the court;

2) the claim has been brought by a person who does not have the right to bring a claim;

3) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to submit the dispute for consideration to an arbitral tribunal, except in cases where a statement of claim has been submitted to the court for recognition of the arbitration agreement as invalid;

31) the parties have agreed in the manner prescribed by law to resolve the dispute using mediation, and no evidence has been submitted that the proposal to resolve the dispute using mediation has been rejected or that a mediation agreement has not been concluded, or that mediation has been terminated without reaching an agreement in the manner prescribed by the Mediation Law;

4) proceedings are pending in the same or another court concerning a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds;

5) in a dispute between the same parties, on the same subject matter and on the same grounds, a court judgment that has entered into legal force or a decision to terminate proceedings due to the claimant's withdrawal from the claim or approval of a settlement between the parties exists;

6) the case does not fall within the jurisdiction of this court;

7) the claimant has not complied with the procedure for prior out-of-court examination of the case established for the relevant category of cases or has not taken the measures prescribed by law to settle the dispute with the defendant before bringing the claim;

8) the statement of claim has been submitted by a person who does not have civil procedural capacity;

9) the power of attorney or other document attached to the statement of claim does not show authorisation for the representative to bring such a claim;

10) no power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to bring a claim is attached to the statement of claim.

(2) The judge shall adopt a reasoned decision on the refusal to accept the statement of claim. The decision together with the submitted statement of claim shall be issued to the claimant.

(3) The decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this Law, except for a decision on refusal to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of point 10 of paragraph one of this Section.

(4) The judge's refusal to accept a statement of claim on the grounds of points 6 to 10 of paragraph one of this Section shall not be an obstacle to the submission of the same application to the court once the deficiencies have been remedied.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 29.11.2012., 22.05.2014., 23.04.2015. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force on 02.07.2015.)

### 133. Section. Leaving a Statement of Claim Without Progress

(1) The judge shall leave a statement of claim without progress if:

1) the statement of claim does not contain all the particulars specified in paragraph two, four or five of Section 128 of this Law;

2) the documents specified in Section 129 of this Law are not attached to the statement of claim;

3) the statement of claim in a simplified procedure case is not drawn up in accordance with the requirements of Section 250.20 of this Law.

(2) The judge shall adopt a reasoned decision on leaving the statement of claim without progress, send it to the claimant and set a time limit for remedying the deficiencies. This time limit may not be shorter than 20 days, counting from the date of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the manner prescribed by this Law. The appeal period shall be counted from the day the decision is issued to the claimant.

(3) If the claimant remedies the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed to have been submitted on the day it was first submitted to the court.

(4) If the claimant does not remedy the deficiencies within the specified time limit, the statement of claim shall be deemed not to have been submitted and shall be returned to the claimant.

(5) The return of the statement of claim to the claimant shall not be an obstacle to its repeated submission to the court, observing the general procedure for submission of statements of claim prescribed by this Law.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 23.04.2015., 14.12.2017. and 21.01.2021., which
enter into force on 01.03.2021.)

### 134. Section. Joinder of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) The claimant is entitled to join several interrelated claims in one statement of claim.

(2) If several similar cases in which the same parties participate are pending in court proceedings, or cases in which one claimant brings a claim against several defendants or several claimants against the same defendant, the court is entitled to join these cases in one proceeding if such joinder will facilitate faster and more correct examination of the cases.
(With amendments made by the Law of 08.09.2011., which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### 135. Section. Separation of Claims and Civil Cases

(1) The judge may instruct the claimant to separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate claim if it considers separate examination of the claims expedient.

(2) The court examining the case may, by decision, separate one claim or several claims from the joined claims into a separate case if their examination in one proceeding has become difficult or impossible.

### 136. Section. Bringing a Counterclaim

(1) The defendant is entitled, until the examination of the case on the merits is completed, to bring a counterclaim against the claimant in the court of first instance.

(2) A counterclaim shall be brought in accordance with the general rules for bringing a claim.

(3) The court or judge shall accept a counterclaim if:

1) mutual set-off is possible between the original claim and the counterclaim;

2) satisfaction of the counterclaim wholly or partially excludes satisfaction of the original claim;

3) the counterclaim and the original claim are interrelated and their joint examination will facilitate faster and more correct adjudication of the case.

(4) The counterclaim shall be examined together with the original claim.
(With amendments made by the Laws of 19.06.2003. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 139. pants. Prasības nodrošināšana un pagaidu aizsardzība pirms prasības celšanas

(1)	Iespējamais prasītājs var lūgt nodrošināt prasību pirms tās celšanas tiesā un pat pirms saistības termiņa iestāšanās, ja parādnieks, izvairoties no saistības izpildes, izved vai atsavina savu mantu, atstāj deklarēto dzīvesvietu vai dzīvesvietu, neinformējot kreditoru, vai veic citas darbības, kas liecina, ka viņš nav godprātīgs. Iesniedzot pieteikumu par prasības nodrošināšanu pirms prasības celšanas, iespējamais prasītājs sniedz pierādījumus, kas apliecina viņa prasības tiesību un nepieciešamību nodrošināt prasību.  

(11) Iespējamais prasītājs var lūgt pagaidu aizsardzību pirms prasības celšanas, ja pagaidu aizsardzība jāpiemēro nekavējoties būtiska kaitējuma novēršanai. Pieteikumā par pagaidu aizsardzību iespējamais prasītājs pamato tās piemērošanas neatliekamību. Pieteikumam pievieno pierādījumus, kas apliecina viņa prasības tiesību un nepieciešamību piemērot pagaidu aizsardzību.  

(2)	Pieteikumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību pirms prasības celšanas iesniedz tiesai, kurā ceļama prasība. Ja puses ir vienojušās par strīda nodošanu pastāvīgajai šķīrējtiesai, pieteikumu iesniedz tiesai pēc parādnieka vai tā mantas atrašanās vietas.  

(3)	Apmierinot pieteikumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību pirms prasības celšanas, tiesnesis prasītājam nosaka termiņu ne ilgāku par 30 dienām prasības pieteikuma iesniegšanai tiesā vai pastāvīgajā šķīrējtiesā.  
(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 29.11.2012., 11.09.2014. un 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

### 139. pants. Securing of a claim and interim protection before filing a claim

(1)	A potential plaintiff may request securing of a claim before filing it in court and even before the maturity date of the obligation, if the debtor, evading performance of the obligation, removes or alienates his or her property, leaves the declared place of residence or place of residence without informing the creditor, or performs other actions indicating that he or she is not acting in good faith. When submitting an application for securing a claim before filing a claim, the potential plaintiff shall provide evidence confirming his or her right to claim and the necessity to secure the claim.

(11) A potential plaintiff may request interim protection before filing a claim if interim protection must be applied immediately to prevent substantial harm. In the application for interim protection, the potential plaintiff shall substantiate the urgency of its application. Evidence confirming his or her right to claim and the necessity to apply interim protection shall be attached to the application.

(2)	An application for securing a claim or interim protection before filing a claim shall be submitted to the court in which the claim is to be filed. If the parties have agreed on submission of the dispute to a permanent arbitration court, the application shall be submitted to the court according to the location of the debtor or his or her property.

(3)	When granting an application for securing a claim or interim protection before filing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for the plaintiff not exceeding 30 days for submitting the statement of claim to the court or permanent arbitration court.
(07.09.2006. version of the law with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 11.09.2014. and 25.03.2021., which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 140. pants. Prasības nodrošinājuma jautājumu izskatīšana

(1)	Pieteikumu par prasības nodrošināšanu tiesa vai tiesnesis, iepriekš nepaziņojot lietas dalībniekiem, izlemj ne vēlāk kā nākamajā dienā pēc tā saņemšanas vai, ja pieteikums iesniegts vienlaikus ar prasības pieteikumu, — pēc lietas ierosināšanas. Apelācijas instancē pieteikumu izlemj trīs tiesneši koleģiāli. Izlemjot jautājumu par prasības nodrošināšanu, tiesa vai tiesnesis ņem vērā prasības pirmšķietamo (prima facie) formālo juridisko pamatojumu un samērīgumu starp pušu tiesiskajām interesēm.  

(2)	Apmierinot pieteikumu par prasības nodrošināšanu, tiesa vai tiesnesis var uzdot prasītājam nodrošināt zaudējumus, kas atbildētājam varētu rasties sakarā ar prasības nodrošināšanu, iemaksājot noteiktu naudas summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā.  

(21)	Lietās, kurās prasības priekšmets ir naudas prasījums un tiek piemērots šā likuma 138. panta pirmās daļas 1., 2., 4. vai 6. punktā noteiktais prasības nodrošinājuma līdzeklis, prasītājs nodrošina atbildētājam iespējamos zaudējumus, iemaksājot tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā piecus procentus no prasījuma summas. Tiesa vai tiesnesis, pieņemot lēmumu par prasības nodrošinājumu, var uzlikt prasītājam par pienākumu nodrošināt iespējamos zaudējumus lielākā apmērā. Zaudējumu nodrošināšanai tiesa nosaka termiņu, kas nedrīkst būt garāks par 20 dienām no lēmuma pieņemšanas dienas. Tiesa vai tiesnesis var pilnīgi vai daļēji atbrīvot no zaudējumu nodrošināšanas, ja, ņemot vērā lietas apstākļus, zaudējumu nodrošināšana nav taisnīga vai ir nesamērīga ar prasītāja mantisko stāvokli. Zaudējumu nodrošināšana neattiecas uz personām, kuras saskaņā ar likumu ir atbrīvotas no valsts nodevas.  

(22)	Ja saskaņā ar šā panta otro un 2.1 daļu tiesas vai tiesneša uzliktais pienākums nav izpildīts un prasītājs nav iesniedzis tiesā tiesu izpildītāja izsniegtu apliecinājumu par naudas summas iemaksu viņa depozīta kontā tiesas vai tiesneša noteiktajā termiņā, tiesa vai tiesnesis pieņem lēmumu par prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļa atcelšanu.  

(3)	Tiesa pēc lietas dalībnieka pieteikuma var aizstāt noteiktos prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļus ar citiem līdzekļiem.  

(31) Apmierinot pieteikumu par prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļu aizstāšanu ar citiem līdzekļiem, tiesa var atkārtoti lemt par prasītājam saskaņā ar šā panta otro un 5.1 daļu uzlikto pienākumu.  

(4)	Lietās, kurās prasības priekšmets ir naudas prasījums, atbildētājs var iemaksāt nodrošinātās prasības summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā. Iesniegumā tiesu izpildītājam atbildētājs norāda, kādā lietā piemērotā prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļa aizstāšanai šī summa tiek iemaksāta, kā arī iesniedz tiesu izpildītājam attiecīgo lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu. Tiesa vai tiesnesis, pamatojoties uz tiesu izpildītāja izsniegtu apliecinājumu par summas iemaksu depozīta kontā, aizstāj pieņemto prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekli ar iemaksāto naudas līdzekļu apķīlājumu. Apķīlātās kustamās mantas aizstāšana ar naudu, iemaksājot nodrošinātās prasības summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā, uzskatāma par prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļa aizstāšanu.  

(5)	Prasības nodrošinājumu pēc puses motivēta pieteikuma var atcelt tā pati tiesa, kura nodrošinājusi prasību, vai tiesa, kuras lietvedībā atrodas lieta izskatīšanai pēc būtības. Izlemjot jautājumu par prasības nodrošinājuma atcelšanu, tiesa izvērtē šā panta pirmajā daļā norādītos nosacījumus, ņemot vērā puses iesniegtos pierādījumus un pamatojumu. Atbildētājs pieteikumā var ietvert pamatojumu par zaudējumiem, kas tam radušies piemērotā prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļa dēļ vai varētu rasties, ja prasības nodrošinājuma līdzeklis netiks atcelts.  

(51) Noraidot pieteikumu par prasības nodrošinājuma atcelšanu, tiesa vai tiesnesis vienlaikus var uzlikt prasītājam par pienākumu nodrošināt šā panta piektajā daļā minētos zaudējumus, iemaksājot tiesas noteiktu naudas summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā 20 dienu laikā no lēmuma pieņemšanas dienas.  

(6)	Noraidot prasību, tiesa spriedumā atceļ prasības nodrošinājumu. Prasības nodrošinājums saglabājas līdz dienai, kad spriedums stājas likumīgā spēkā.  

(61) Ja prasītājam uzlikts par pienākumu nodrošināt atbildētājam zaudējumu atlīdzību, kas tam varētu rasties sakarā ar prasības nodrošināšanu, tiesa spriedumā vai lēmumā, ar kuru prasība atstāta bez izskatīšanas vai lieta izbeigta, vienlaikus izlemj jautājumu par zaudējumu atlīdzības nodrošināšanai iemaksātās summas izmaksu no zvērināta tiesu izpildītāja konta. Noraidot vai apmierinot prasību daļēji, tiesa jautājumu par zaudējumu nodrošinājuma pilnīgu vai daļēju izmaksu atbildētājam izlemj pēc atbildētāja lūguma, ja atbildētājs ir iesniedzis tiesai pierādījumus par faktisko zaudējumu apmēru. Ja lūgums un pierādījumi par faktisko zaudējumu apmēru tiesai nav iesniegti, nodrošinātie zaudējumi atmaksājami prasītājam. Atbildētājam ir tiesības prasīt nepiedzīto zaudējumu atlīdzināšanu šā likuma 143.panta kārtībā.  

(7)	Ja prasība atstāta bez izskatīšanas vai tiesvedība izbeigta, tiesa lēmumā atceļ prasības nodrošinājumu. Prasības nodrošinājums saglabājas līdz dienai, kad lēmums stājas likumīgā spēkā.  

(8)	Ja lēmums par prasības nodrošinājumu pieņemts pirms prasības celšanas un tiesas noteiktajā termiņā prasība nav celta, tiesnesis pēc iespējamā prasītāja vai atbildētāja pieteikuma saņemšanas pieņem lēmumu par nodrošinā juma atcelšanu.  

(9)	Šā panta trešajā un piektajā daļā minētos pieteikumus izlemj tiesas sēdē, iepriekš par to paziņojot lietas dalībniekiem. Šo personu neierašanās nav šķērslis pieteikuma izskatīšanai. Tiesas sēdes diena nosakāma ne vēlāk kā 30 dienu laikā pēc pieteikuma saņemšanas.  

(10)	Ja lēmumā, kas pieņemts par puses pieteikumu par prasības nodrošinājuma atcelšanu, prasītājam uzdots izpildīt šā panta 5.1 daļā uzlikto pienākumu, bet tas nav izpildīts un prasītājs nav iesniedzis tiesā tiesu izpildītāja izsniegtu apliecinājumu par summas iemaksu viņa depozīta kontā, tiesa vai tiesnesis pieņem lēmumu par prasības nodrošinājuma līdzekļa atcelšanu.  
(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009., 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011., 11.09.2014.,
23.04.2015., 28.05.2015., 25.03.2021. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

### 140. Section. Examination of the question of securing a claim

(1) The court or judge shall decide on an application for securing a claim, without prior notice to the parties, no later than the next day after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after the initiation of the case. In the appellate instance, the application shall be decided by three judges collegially. When deciding the question of securing a claim, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim and the proportionality between the legal interests of the parties.

(2) When granting an application for securing a claim, the court or judge may require the claimant to secure damages that may be caused to the defendant in connection with the securing of the claim by depositing a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff.

(21) In cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim and the measure for securing a claim specified in points 1, 2, 4 or 6 of the first paragraph of Section 138 of this Law is applied, the claimant shall secure possible damages to the defendant by depositing five percent of the claim amount into the deposit account of a bailiff. The court or judge, when adopting a decision on securing a claim, may impose on the claimant an obligation to secure possible damages in a larger amount. The court shall set a time limit for securing damages, which may not be longer than 20 days from the date of adoption of the decision. The court or judge may fully or partially release from securing damages if, taking into account the circumstances of the case, securing damages is not fair or is disproportionate to the claimant's financial situation. Securing damages does not apply to persons who are exempt from state fees in accordance with law.

(22) If the obligation imposed by the court or judge in accordance with the second and 2.1 parts of this Section has not been fulfilled and the claimant has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the deposit of the sum of money into his deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision to cancel the measure for securing the claim.

(3) The court, upon application of a party, may replace the specified measures for securing a claim with other measures.

(31) When granting an application for replacing measures for securing a claim with other measures, the court may decide again on the obligation imposed on the claimant in accordance with the second and 5.1 parts of this Section.

(4) In cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, the defendant may deposit the amount of the secured claim into the deposit account of a bailiff. In the application to the bailiff, the defendant shall indicate in which case this amount is being deposited to replace the measure for securing the claim applied, and shall also submit to the bailiff the relevant decision on securing the claim. The court or judge, based on a certificate issued by the bailiff confirming the deposit of the amount into the deposit account, shall replace the adopted measure for securing the claim with a pledge of the deposited monetary funds. The replacement of pledged movable property with money by depositing the amount of the secured claim into the deposit account of a bailiff shall be considered a replacement of the measure for securing the claim.

(5) The securing of a claim, upon a reasoned application of a party, may be cancelled by the same court that secured the claim or by the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. When deciding the question of cancelling the securing of a claim, the court shall evaluate the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Section, taking into account the evidence and reasoning submitted by the party. The defendant may include in the application reasoning about damages that have been caused to it due to the applied measure for securing the claim or could be caused if the measure for securing the claim is not cancelled.

(51) When rejecting an application for cancelling the securing of a claim, the court or judge may simultaneously impose on the claimant an obligation to secure the damages referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Section by depositing a sum of money determined by the court into the deposit account of a bailiff within 20 days from the date of adoption of the decision.

(6) When rejecting the claim, the court shall cancel the securing of the claim in the judgment. The securing of the claim shall remain in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(61) If the claimant has been imposed with an obligation to secure compensation for damages to the defendant that may be caused in connection with the securing of the claim, the court shall simultaneously decide in the judgment or decision by which the claim is left without examination or the case is terminated the question of payment of the amount deposited to secure compensation for damages from the account of a sworn bailiff. When rejecting or granting the claim in part, the court shall decide the question of full or partial payment of the secured damages to the defendant upon the defendant's request if the defendant has submitted to the court evidence of the actual amount of damages. If the request and evidence of the actual amount of damages have not been submitted to the court, the secured damages shall be refunded to the claimant. The defendant has the right to claim compensation for unrecovered damages in the manner provided for in Section 143 of this Law.

(7) If the claim is left without examination or the proceedings are terminated, the court shall cancel the securing of the claim in the decision. The securing of the claim shall remain in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(8) If a decision on securing a claim was adopted before filing the claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or defendant, shall adopt a decision to cancel the securing.

(9) The applications referred to in the third and fifth paragraphs of this Section shall be decided at a court session, with prior notice to the parties. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application. The date of the court session shall be set no later than 30 days after receipt of the application.

(10) If in the decision adopted on a party's application for cancelling the securing of a claim the claimant has been instructed to fulfil the obligation imposed in part 5.1 of this Section, but it has not been fulfilled and the claimant has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the deposit of the amount into his deposit account, the court or judge shall adopt a decision to cancel the measure for securing the claim.
(In the wording of the Law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 04.08.2011, 11.09.2014,
23.04.2015, 28.05.2015, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

140. 1 Section. Examination of questions of interim protection

(1) When deciding the question of interim protection, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim and the proportionality between the legal interests of the parties.

(2) The court or judge shall decide on an application for interim protection, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the parties, within 10 days after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after the initiation of the case. In the appellate instance, the application shall be decided by three judges collegially. If the court or judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided at a court session within 15 days after its receipt or, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the statement of claim, after the initiation of the case, summoning the parties, but if the application is submitted before filing the claim, the potential parties. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(3) If delay could cause irreversible harm and it is not necessary to request additional evidence, the court or judge shall decide on the application for interim protection no later than the next day after the initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, no later than the next day after receipt of the application, without prior notice to the defendant and other parties.

(4) When granting an application for interim protection, the court or judge may require the claimant to secure damages that may be caused to the defendant in connection with the application of interim protection and to deposit a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or to submit to the court an equivalent guarantee. If the claimant has not fulfilled the imposed obligation or has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the deposit of the sum of money into his deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision to cancel the measure of interim protection.

(5) The court, upon application of a party, may replace the applied measure of interim protection with another measure or modify it.

(6) When granting an application for replacing a measure of interim protection with another measure, the court may decide again on the obligation imposed on the claimant in accordance with the fourth and eighth parts of this Section.

(7) Interim protection, upon a reasoned application of a party, may be cancelled by the same court that applied the interim protection or by the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits. When deciding the question of cancelling interim protection, the court or judge shall evaluate the conditions specified in the first paragraph of this Section, taking into account the evidence and reasoning submitted by the party. The defendant may include in the application reasoning about damages that have been caused to it due to the applied measure of interim protection or could be caused if the measure of interim protection is not cancelled.

(8) When rejecting an application for cancelling interim protection, the court or judge may simultaneously impose on the claimant an obligation to secure the damages referred to in the seventh paragraph of this Section by depositing a sum of money determined by the court into the deposit account of a bailiff within 20 days from the date of adoption of the decision.

(9) When rejecting the claim, leaving the claim without examination or terminating the proceedings, the court shall cancel the interim protection in the respective decision. Interim protection shall be in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(10) When granting the claim, the court shall decide on the cancellation or continuation of the applied interim protection until the execution of the judgment.

(11) If a decision on interim protection was adopted before filing the claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the court or judge, upon receipt of an application from the potential claimant or potential party, shall adopt a decision to cancel the interim protection.

(12) An application for cancelling or replacing a measure of interim protection shall be decided at a court session, with prior notice to the parties. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.
(In the wording of the Law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

(2)	Ja lēmums par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību pieņemts bez lietas dalībnieka klātbūtnes, termiņu sūdzības iesniegšanai skaita no lēmuma izsniegšanas dienas.

(4)	Ja lēmums par pagaidu aizsardzības piemērošanu pieņemts bez atbildētāja vai citu lietas dalībnieku klātbūtnes, atbildētājam un citiem lietas dalībniekiem tiesa paziņo par šo lēmumu vienlaikus ar lēmuma paziņošanu prasītājam.

### 142. pants

Prasības nodrošinājuma un pagaidu aizsardzības jautājumos pieņemto lēmumu izpilde

(1)	Lēmums par prasības nodrošināšanu (140. panta pirmā daļa) un pagaidu aizsardzības piemērošanu (140.1 panta pirmā daļa) un lēmums par prasības nodrošinājuma atcelšanu (140. panta piektā un desmitā daļa) un pagaidu aizsardzības atcelšanu (140.1 panta septītā daļa) izpildāms nekavējoties pēc tā pieņemšanas.  

(2)	Lēmums par prasības nodrošināšanu un pagaidu aizsardzības piemērošanu, kas pieņemts ar šā likuma 140. panta otrajā daļā, 2.1 daļā vai 140.1 panta ceturtajā daļā noteikto nosacījumu, izpildāms pēc tam, kad prasītājs iemaksājis tiesas vai tiesneša noteikto summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā vai — 140.1 panta ceturtajā daļā minētajā gadījumā — iesniedzis līdzvērtīgu garantiju. Izpildu dokumentu vai šā panta trešajā daļā minēto lēmumu izsniedz pēc tiesas noteiktās summas iemaksas vai līdzvērtīgās garantijas saņemšanas.  

(3)	Ja prasība nodrošināta ar vai pagaidu aizsardzība piemērota attiecībā uz nekustamo īpašumu vai kuģi vai ar aizlieguma atzīmes vai citas atzīmes ierakstīšanu zemesgrāmatā, kustamas mantas reģistrā vai citā publiskā reģistrā, tiesa izsniedz prasītājam attiecīgo lēmumu ar uzrakstu, ka šis lēmums izsniegts atzīmes ierakstīšanai zemesgrāmatā, kustamas mantas reģistrā vai citā attiecīgā publiskā reģistrā, bet kuģa aresta gadījumā — kuģa aizturēšanai ostā.  

(4)	Lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzības piemērošanu, apķīlājot atbildētājam piederošu kustamu mantu vai skaidru naudu, kas atrodas pie atbildētāja vai trešajām personām, izpilda šā likuma 71.nodaļā noteiktajā kārtībā.  

(5)	Apķīlājot maksājumus, kuri atbildētājam pienākas no trešajām personām saskaņā ar līgumu (izņemot naudas līdzekļus kredītiestādēs vai pie citiem maksājumu pakalpojumu sniedzējiem), tiesu izpildītājs, pamatojoties uz izpildu dokumentu, nosūta šīm personām pieprasījumu paziņot, vai tām ir pienākums maksāt kādas summas atbildētājam, kādā apmērā un termiņā, kā arī paziņo, ka šīs summas tiek apķīlātas prasības summas apmērā, ievērojot šā likuma 1.pielikuma 3.punktā noteikto ierobežojumu attiecībā uz parādnieku, un dod rīkojumu ieskaitīt maksājumus (tajā skaitā pieprasījuma noguldījumus), kuriem iestājies termiņš, tiesu izpildītāja depozītu kontā. Naudas līdzekļus kredītiestādēs vai pie citiem maksājumu pakalpojumu sniedzējiem tiesu izpildītājs apķīlā šā likuma 599.1 pantā noteiktajā kārtībā. Apķīlātos maksājumus var izmaksāt citām personām tikai atbilstoši tā tiesu izpildītāja aprēķinam, kurš pirmais apķīlājis maksājumus.  

(6)	Lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzības piemērošanu, nosakot aizliegumu atbildētājam veikt noteiktas darbības vai pienākumu atbildētājam veikt noteiktas darbības, izpilda tiesu izpildītājs un šā likuma
555. pantā noteiktajā kārtībā paziņo par tiesas lēmumu atbildētājam vai attiecīgajai trešajai personai.  

(7)	Ja lietās, kurās prasības priekšmets ir naudas prasījums, atbildētājs iemaksājis prasības summu tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā, tiesu izpildītājs atbrīvo no apķīlājuma apķīlāto kustamo mantu.  

(8)	Ja piemērotais prasības nodrošinājums vai pagaidu aizsardzība atcelta, tad lēmumu par atcelšanu izpilda pēc tā tiesu izpildītāja rīkojuma, kurš izpildījis lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību.  

(9)	Lēmumu par prasības nodrošinājuma vai pagaidu aizsardzības līdzekļa aizstāšanu izpilda tiesu izpildītājs, vispirms nodrošinot prasību ar aizstājošo līdzekli un pēc tam atceļot aizstāto līdzekli. Summu, kura iemaksāta tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā kā prasības nodrošinājuma līdzeklis, tiesu izpildītājs atmaksā, tikai pamatojoties uz tiesas nolēmumu.  
(07.09.2006. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 25.03.2021. un
11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

142.	1 pants. Rīcība ar prasības nodrošinājuma vai pagaidu aizsardzības ietvaros apķīlātu kustamu mantu, kas ātri bojājas

(1)	Tiesu izpildītājs neapķīlā mantu, kura ātri bojājas un kuras pārdošana tās realizācijas termiņā var nebūt iespējama.  

(2)	Ja tiesu izpildītājs apķīlājis mantu, kura ātri bojājas, bet kuru tās realizācijas termiņā varētu būt iespējams pārdot, pēc tiesu izpildītāja lūguma tiesa, kas pieņēmusi lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību, vai tiesa, kurā tajā laikā atrodas lieta, lemj par atļauju pārdot apķīlāto mantu, bet pārdošanā iegūto naudu, no kuras atskaitīti pārdošanas izdevumi, apķīlāt prasības nodrošināšanai vai pagaidu aizsardzībai. Tiesu izpildītāja lūgumu tiesa izlemj rakstveida procesā ne vēlāk kā nākamajā dienā pēc tā saņemšanas. Lēmumu, ar kuru atļauts pārdot apķīlāto mantu, sastāda rezolūcijas veidā. Tiesas lēmums nav pārsūdzams.  

(3)	Pēc tam kad saņemts tiesas lēmums, ar kuru atļauts veikt apķīlātās mantas pārdošanu un pārdošanā iegūto naudas līdzekļu apķīlāšanu, tiesu izpildītājs apķīlāto mantu pārdod šā likuma 581. panta otrajā daļā paredzētajā kārtībā, bet pārdošanā iegūto naudu, no kuras atskaitīti pārdošanas izdevumi, ieskaita un glabā tiesu izpildītāja depozīta kontā. Šādā gadījumā pārdošanā iegūtie naudas līdzekļi kalpo lietā kā prasības nodrošinājuma vai pagaidu aizsardzības līdzeklis. Par prasības nodrošināšanai vai pagaidu aizsardzībai apķīlātās kustamās mantas pārdošanu un pārdošanas rezultātiem tiesu izpildītājs paziņo tiesai, prasītājam un atbildētājam.  

(4)	Ja tiesa noraida tiesu izpildītāja lūgumu atļaut apķīlāto mantu pārdot, tā vienlaikus izvērtē nepieciešamību atcelt piemēroto prasības nodrošinājumu vai pagaidu aizsardzību attiecībā uz konkrēto mantu.  
(01.03.2018. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 25.03.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 20.04.2021.)

### 141. pants

Notification and appeal of decisions adopted in matters of security for a claim and interim protection

(1) An appeal may be lodged against the decisions referred to in the third paragraph of Section 140 and the fifth paragraph of Section 140.1 of this Law, a decision rejecting an application for security for a claim or an application for interim protection, and a decision rejecting an application for cancellation of security for a claim or interim protection, as well as a court decision on security for damages that may be incurred by the defendant in connection with security for a claim or interim protection (Section 140, paragraphs two, 3.1 and 5.1 and Section 140.1, paragraphs four, six and eight).

(11) A decision adopted on security for damages that may be incurred by the defendant in connection with security for a claim or interim protection shall be notified to the defendant after the claimant has paid the amount determined by the court or judge into the bailiff's deposit account.

(2) If a decision on security for a claim or interim protection has been adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for lodging an appeal shall be calculated from the date of issue of the decision.

(3) If a decision on security for a claim has been adopted without the presence of the defendant or other participants in the case, the court shall notify the defendant and other participants in the case of this decision not earlier than on the third day after its adoption.

(4) If a decision on the application of interim protection has been adopted without the presence of the defendant or other participants in the case, the court shall notify the defendant and other participants in the case of this decision simultaneously with notification of the decision to the claimant.
(In the wording of the Law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the Laws of 14.12.2006, 05.02.2009, the Constitutional Court judgment of 30.03.2010, the Laws of 04.08.2011, 23.04.2015, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 142. pants

Execution of decisions adopted in matters of security for a claim and interim protection

(1) A decision on security for a claim (Section 140, paragraph one) and application of interim protection (Section 140.1, paragraph one) and a decision on cancellation of security for a claim (Section 140, paragraphs five and ten) and cancellation of interim protection (Section 140.1, paragraph seven) shall be executed immediately after its adoption.

(2) A decision on security for a claim and application of interim protection, adopted with the condition specified in the second paragraph, paragraph 2.1 of Section 140 or the fourth paragraph of Section 140.1 of this Law, shall be executed after the claimant has paid the amount determined by the court or judge into the bailiff's deposit account or — in the case referred to in the fourth paragraph of Section 140.1 — has submitted an equivalent guarantee. The writ of execution or the decision referred to in the third paragraph of this Section shall be issued after payment of the amount determined by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.

(3) If a claim has been secured by or interim protection has been applied in respect of immovable property or a ship or by entry of a prohibition note or other note in the Land Register, movable property register or other public register, the court shall issue to the claimant the relevant decision with an inscription that this decision has been issued for entry of a note in the Land Register, movable property register or other relevant public register, but in the case of arrest of a ship — for detention of the ship in port.

(4) A decision on security for a claim or application of interim protection by pledging movable property or cash belonging to the defendant that is in the possession of the defendant or third parties shall be executed in the procedure specified in Chapter 71 of this Law.

(5) When pledging payments that are due to the defendant from third parties under a contract (except for funds in credit institutions or with other payment service providers), the bailiff, on the basis of the writ of execution, shall send a request to these persons to notify whether they have an obligation to pay any amounts to the defendant, in what amount and time limit, and shall also notify that these amounts are being pledged in the amount of the claim, observing the restriction specified in point 3 of Annex 1 of this Law in respect of debtors, and shall give an order to pay the payments (including demand deposits) for which the time limit has arrived into the bailiff's deposit account. The bailiff shall pledge funds in credit institutions or with other payment service providers in the procedure specified in Section 599.1 of this Law. Pledged payments may be paid to other persons only in accordance with the calculation of the bailiff who first pledged the payments.

(6) A decision on security for a claim or application of interim protection by establishing a prohibition on the defendant to perform certain actions or an obligation on the defendant to perform certain actions shall be executed by the bailiff and the court decision shall be notified to the defendant or the relevant third party in the procedure specified in Section 555 of this Law.

(7) If in cases where the subject matter of the claim is a monetary claim, the defendant has paid the claim amount into the bailiff's deposit account, the bailiff shall release the pledged movable property from the pledge.

(8) If the applied security for a claim or interim protection has been cancelled, then the decision on cancellation shall be executed pursuant to an order of the bailiff who executed the decision on security for a claim or interim protection.

(9) A decision on replacement of a security for a claim or interim protection measure shall be executed by the bailiff, first securing the claim with the replacement measure and then cancelling the replaced measure. An amount that has been paid into the bailiff's deposit account as a security for a claim measure shall be refunded by the bailiff only on the basis of a court decision.
(In the wording of the Law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the Laws of 05.02.2009, 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Section 142.1 Handling of pledged movable property that perishes quickly within the framework of security for a claim or interim protection

(1) The bailiff shall not pledge property that perishes quickly and the sale of which during its realisation period may not be possible.

(2) If the bailiff has pledged property that perishes quickly but which it might be possible to sell during its realisation period, at the request of the bailiff, the court that adopted the decision on security for a claim or interim protection, or the court in which the case is located at that time, shall decide on permission to sell the pledged property, but to pledge the money obtained from the sale, from which the sale expenses have been deducted, for security for the claim or interim protection. The court shall decide on the bailiff's request in written proceedings not later than on the next day after its receipt. The decision by which permission is granted to sell the pledged property shall be drawn up in the form of a resolution. The court decision is not subject to appeal.

(3) After receipt of the court decision by which permission is granted to carry out the sale of the pledged property and the pledging of the funds obtained from the sale, the bailiff shall sell the pledged property in the procedure provided for in the second paragraph of Section 581 of this Law, but the money obtained from the sale, from which the sale expenses have been deducted, shall be paid in and kept in the bailiff's deposit account. In such a case, the funds obtained from the sale shall serve in the case as a security for a claim or interim protection measure. The bailiff shall notify the court, the claimant and the defendant of the sale of movable property pledged for security for a claim or interim protection and the results of the sale.

(4) If the court rejects the bailiff's request to permit the sale of the pledged property, it shall simultaneously assess the need to cancel the applied security for a claim or interim protection in respect of the specific property.
(In the wording of the Law of 01.03.2018 with amendments made by the Law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 147. pants. Preparation of Civil Cases for Trial

(1)	In order to ensure timely examination of a case, the judge prepares the case for trial after receiving the statement of claim.  

(2)	The duty of the participants in the case is to participate in the preparation of the case for trial: to respond within the time limits set by the judge to his or her requests, to submit written explanations, the necessary evidence and to appear in court at the invitation of the judge.

### 148. pants. Sending the Statement of Claim and the Documents Attached Thereto to the Defendant

(1)	After initiating the case, the statement of claim shall be sent to the defendant without delay to the official electronic address

or by registered mail and a time limit shall be set for the submission of a written explanation — 15–30 days from the date of sending the statement of claim, but in cases concerning a child — not longer than 15 days from the date of sending the statement of claim. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the statement of claim may also be sent to the defendant.  

(11)	If the statement of claim and the documents attached thereto (fourth part of Section 129) are to be sent to the defendant after initiating the case in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law, the time limit for submission of a written explanation is 30 days, counting from the day on which the statement of claim is issued to the defendant.  

(12)	The claimant shall be notified of the sending of the statement of claim and the documents attached thereto to the defendant.  

(13)	The court shall send to the claimant and the defendant information about the possibility of resolving the dispute using mediation and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified time limit if they agree to use mediation.  

(14)	The court shall send to the claimant and the defendant information about the court's proposal to transfer the case for examination to another court in accordance with Section 32.1 of this Law and about the obligation to notify the court within the specified time limit if the transfer of the case for examination to another court will create significant obstacles for the claimant or the defendant to appear at the court hearing.  

(2)	In the explanation, the defendant shall indicate:

1)	whether he or she acknowledges the claim in full or in any part thereof;  

2)	his or her objections to the claim and the grounds therefor;  

3)	evidence confirming his or her objections to the claim and the grounds therefor, as well as the law on which they are based;  

4)	requests for the admission of evidence or the obtaining thereof;  

5)	other circumstances which he or she considers significant in the examination of the case, and may also indicate his or her telephone number if he or she agrees to use the telephone for communication with the court;  

51)	an e-mail address for communication with the court and, if he or she has registered his or her participation in the online system, also includes an indication of registration if the defendant (or his or her representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia) agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the address of the defendant's representative is outside Latvia, he or she shall additionally indicate an e-mail address or notify of the registration of his or her participation in the online system;  

52)	the name of the credit institution and the account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;  

6)	whether he or she agrees to use mediation.  

(3)	Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the objections are based shall be attached to the explanation.  

(31) The defendant shall not indicate information containing state secrets in the explanations. Information containing state secrets shall be indicated in a separate document.  

(4)	After receiving the explanation, it shall be sent without delay to the claimant and third parties. If the judge considers it necessary, he or she is entitled to request a response from the claimant regarding the explanation.
