### 149. Section. Actions of the Judge in Preparing the Case for Trial

(1)	After receiving the statement or upon expiry of the time limit set for its submission, the judge decides on the actions for preparing the case so that it can be examined in a court session.

(2)	In preparing the case for trial, the judge attempts to reconcile the parties and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation.

(3)	In preparing the case for trial, the judge decides on the requests of the participants in the case concerning:

1)	the summoning or admission of third parties;

2)	the securing of evidence;

3)	the summoning of witnesses;

4)	the appointment of an expert examination;

5)	the acceptance or requesting of written and material evidence;

6)	the participation of persons in the trial of the case using videoconference.

(4)	The judge is entitled to request written statements from the participants in the case in order to clarify the circumstances of the case and the evidence. Statements and evidence shall be submitted within the time limit set by the judge.

(41) If the claimant and the defendant agree to the use of mediation, the judge, when adopting a decision on the use of mediation, shall set a time limit for the use of mediation, which shall not exceed six months, and the obligation of the parties to submit to the court evidence of the result of mediation no later than seven days after the termination of mediation. The judge's decision on the use of mediation is not subject to appeal.

(5)	The judge decides questions concerning the participation in the case of representatives of state and local government institutions and the prosecutor in cases provided for by law, concerning the sending of court instructions to other courts, concerning the participation of persons in the trial of the case using videoconference, and also performs other necessary procedural actions.

(6)	For the performance of the actions referred to in this Section, the judge may set a preparatory session to which the parties and third parties are invited.

(7)	If a preparatory session is not necessary, the judge shall set the day and time of the court session and the persons to be invited and summoned to court. When setting a time limit for the use of mediation, the judge shall simultaneously set the day of the court session no earlier than after the time limit referred to in Paragraph 4.1 of this Section.

(8)	In cases concerning the reinstatement of an employee at work and in cases concerning the recognition of an employer's notice as invalid, the day of the court session shall be set no later than within 15 days after receiving the statement or after the expiry of the time limit for its submission or after the preparatory session or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the result of mediation is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new day for the court session.

(9)	In cases concerning claims arising from the alienation of immovable property for the needs of society, the court session shall be set within 15 days after receiving the statements or after the expiry of the time limit for their submission, or after the preparatory session, or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the result of mediation is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new day for the court session.

(10)	In cases concerning claims by administrators on behalf of insolvent debtors in the cases provided for in Chapter XVII of the Insolvency Law and concerning the recovery of losses from members of management institutions of a legal person and participants (shareholders) of a capital company, based on their obligation to be liable for losses caused, as well as from personally liable members of a partnership, based on their obligation to be liable for the obligations of the partnership, the court session shall be set no later than within three months after receiving the statement or after the expiry of the time limit for its submission, or after the preparatory session, or after the expiry of the mediation time limit. If evidence of the result of mediation is received by the court before the time limit set by the judge, the judge may set a new day for the court session.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.04.2004., 09.06.2005., 30.09.2010., 08.09.2011., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021.  
which come into force on 01.12.2021.)

149. 1 Section. Preparatory Session

(1)	In the preparatory session, the judge questions the participants in the case about the substance of the case in order to clarify the subject matter and limits of the dispute, explains to the participants in the case their procedural rights and obligations, the consequences of performing or not performing procedural actions, decides the questions provided for in Paragraphs three, four and five of Section 149 of this Law, attempts to reconcile the parties and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation, if necessary, sets a time limit by which individual procedural actions must be performed.

(2)	If the court session has not been set in advance, in the preparatory session the judge shall set the day and time of the court session and notify the participants in the case who are present, and also determine the persons to be invited and summoned to the court session.

(3)	The preparatory session shall be recorded in minutes. The course of the preparatory session shall be recorded in full using technical means. The minutes shall record information about the course of the session, the substance of the statements of the participants in the case and the decisions adopted by the judge.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.12.2013., 22.05.2014. and 11.11.2021., which come into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 150. Section. Liability of Participants in the Case

(1)	If a participant in the case, without justifiable reason, does not submit a statement within the time limit set by the judge or does not respond to the judge's request, the judge may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on him or her.

(2)	If a participant in the case, without justifiable reason, does not appear at the preparatory session, the judge may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on him or her.

(3)	If the defendant has not submitted a statement, has not appeared at the preparatory session and has not notified the reason for his or her non-appearance, the court may issue a default judgment at the preparatory session.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 30.09.2010., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013. and 11.11.2021., which come into force on 01.12.2021.)

21. Chapter Trial of Civil Cases

### 151. Section. Court Session

(1)	Cases shall be tried in a court session presided over by a judge.

(2)	The judge shall conduct the trial of the case in such a way as to ensure equal opportunities for all participants in the case to participate in the clarification of the circumstances of the case.

(3)	During the course of the trial of the case, the judge attempts to reconcile the parties and also offers to resolve the dispute using mediation.  
(With amendments made by the law of 22.05.2014., which comes into force on 18.06.2014.)

### 152. Section. Order in the Court Session

(1)	Participants in the case, witnesses, experts and interpreters in the court session shall observe the order established in this Law and shall comply without objection with the instructions of the judge and the decisions of the court.

(2)	Persons present in the courtroom shall behave in such a way as not to disturb the course of the court session.

(3)	The course of the trial may be recorded or otherwise documented without disturbing the course of the court session. The use of photo, film and video equipment in the court session is permitted only with the permission of the court. Before deciding this question, the court shall hear the opinion of the participants in the case.

(4)	The number of persons admitted to the courtroom shall be determined by the court in accordance with the number of seats available in the room. Relatives of the parties and representatives of the mass media have priority rights to be present at the trial of the case.

(5)	When the court enters the courtroom and leaves it, all persons present in the courtroom shall stand.

(6)	Participants in the case, witnesses and experts shall provide the court with statements and opinions, submit requests and give testimony while standing. Deviation from this rule is permitted only with the permission of the judge.

(7)	All persons present in the courtroom shall hear the judgment of the court while standing.  
(With amendments made by the law of 19.06.2003., which comes into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 153. Section. Maintenance of order in court session

(1)	A person who disturbs order during the hearing of a case shall be given a warning by the judge.

(2)	If parties to the case, witnesses, experts or interpreters repeatedly disturb order, the court may impose a fine of up to 80 euros on these persons.

(3)	If a prosecutor or advocate repeatedly disturbs order, this shall be reported to a higher-ranking prosecutor or to the Latvian Sworn Advocates' Council.

(4)	If a person who is not a party to the case repeatedly disturbs order, the judge shall expel that person from the courtroom. This person may also be held liable as provided by law for contempt of court.
(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which comes into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 154. Section. Commencement of court session

At the time appointed for the hearing of the case, the court enters the courtroom, the presiding judge opens the court session and announces:

1)	the year, date, month and place of the court session;

2)	the name of the court hearing the case, the composition of the court, the secretary of the court session, the interpreter, the representative appointed by the court for the videoconference proceedings if a party to the case participates in the court session using videoconference at the court according to the location of the party to the case or at a specially equipped place for this purpose, the advocate and the prosecutor participating in the case;

3)	the time of opening of the court session;

4)	the name of the case.
(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 155. Section. Verification of appearance of participants in proceedings

(1)	The secretary of the court session reports to the court which persons invited and summoned in this case have appeared, as well as whether persons who have not appeared have been notified of the court session and what information has been received regarding the reasons for non-appearance of these persons.

(2)	The court verifies the identity of the persons who have appeared, the identity of those persons who participate in the court session using videoconference in an online system, and the powers of representatives. A representative appointed by the court verifies the identity of those persons who participate in the court session using videoconference at the court according to the location of the person or at a specially equipped place for this purpose.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 156. Section. Consequences of non-appearance of a party to the case, witness, expert or interpreter

(1)	If any of the parties to the case, a witness, an expert or an interpreter has not appeared at the court session, the court shall commence the examination of the case unless there are grounds to postpone it in accordance with Sections 209 or 210 of this law.

(2)	If a party to the case who has not appeared at the court session has not notified the court in due time of the reason for non-appearance, the court may impose a fine of up to 80 euros on this person.

(3)	If any of the parties to the case does not appear at court for reasons which the court considers unjustified, the court may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on this person.

(4)	The procedural sanctions provided for in Sections 109 and 122 of this law shall apply to a witness and an expert who have not appeared at the court session.
(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which comes into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 157. Section. Explanation of duties to interpreter

(1)	The court shall explain to the interpreter his or her duty to interpret the explanations, questions, testimonies, applications and requests of those persons who do not speak the language of the proceedings, and to these persons — the explanations, questions, testimonies, applications, requests of other parties to the case, the content of documents read out, the orders of the judge and the decisions of the court.

(2)	The court shall warn the interpreter that he or she is liable under the Criminal Law for refusal to interpret or for deliberately incorrect interpretation.

### 158. Section. Expulsion of witnesses from the courtroom

Witnesses shall be expelled from the courtroom until the commencement of their examination. The presiding judge shall ensure that witnesses examined by the court do not communicate with witnesses who have not been examined.

### 159. Section. Explanation of rights and duties to parties to the case

(1)	The court shall explain to the parties to the case their procedural rights and duties.

(2)	During the course of the examination of the case, the court shall explain to the parties and third persons the consequences of performance or non-performance of procedural actions.

### 160. Section. Deciding on challenges

(1)	The court shall ascertain whether the parties to the case have challenges to the judge, prosecutor, secretary of the court session, expert or interpreter.

(2)	The court shall decide on challenges filed in the procedure provided for in Section 21 of this law.

### 161. Section. Explanation of rights and duties to expert

If the person chosen as an expert is not a certified forensic expert in the procedure provided for in the Forensic Experts Law, the court shall explain to the expert his or her rights and duties and warn that the expert is liable under the Criminal Law for refusal to give an opinion or for deliberately giving a false opinion.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which comes into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 162. Section. Deciding on requests filed by parties to the case

The court shall ascertain whether the parties to the case have requests related to the hearing of the case and shall decide on them after hearing the opinion of the other parties to the case.

### 163. Section. Commencement of examination of the case on the merits

(1)	The examination of the case on the merits shall commence with the judge's report on the circumstances of the case.

(2)	After the judge's report, the court shall ascertain whether the plaintiff maintains the claim, whether the defendant acknowledges the claim and whether the parties wish to conclude a settlement or to refer the case for examination to an arbitration court.

### 164. Section

Withdrawal from claim, acknowledgement of claim, settlement, agreement on referral of case to arbitration court or use of mediation

(1)	Withdrawal from a claim or acknowledgement of a claim may be expressed orally at the court session.

(2)	If withdrawal from a claim or acknowledgement of a claim is expressed in written applications addressed to the court, they shall be attached to the case.

(3)	A settlement shall be submitted to the court in writing and shall be attached to the case.

(4)	An agreement on referral of the case to an arbitration court shall be drawn up in writing and attached to the case.

(5)	The court shall adopt a decision on the plaintiff's withdrawal from the claim, on the parties' agreement to refer the case for examination to an arbitration court, as well as on the parties' settlement, whereby it shall simultaneously terminate the proceedings in the case. The decision on approval of the settlement shall indicate the terms of the settlement.

(6)	The court shall adopt a reasoned decision on refusal to approve the settlement and shall continue to examine the case on the merits.

(7)	Before the examination of the case on the merits has been completed, it is possible to withdraw from the claim, acknowledge the claim, conclude a settlement or an agreement on referral of the dispute for examination to an arbitration court, as well as to agree on the use of mediation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.12.2013, 22.05.2014 and 11.11.2021, which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 165. Section. Explanations of parties to the case

(1)	Parties to the case shall give explanations at the court session in the following order: the plaintiff, the third person with independent claims and the defendant.

(2)	If a third person without independent claims participates in the case, he or she shall give explanations after the plaintiff or the defendant depending on which side this third person participates in the case.

(3)	If the claim has been brought by a prosecutor, a state or local government institution or a person who has been granted by law the right to defend in court the rights and legally protected interests of other persons, he or she shall give explanations at the court session first.

(4)	Representatives of parties to the case shall give explanations on behalf of those they represent.

(5)	In their explanations, parties to the case shall indicate all circumstances on which their claims or objections are based.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which comes into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 166. Section. Written explanations of parties to the case

(1)	Parties to the case are entitled to submit their explanations to the court in writing.

(2)	Written explanations of parties to the case shall be read out at the court session, observing the order provided for in Section 165 of this law, and shall be attached to the case.

### 167. Section. Procedure for Asking Questions

(1)	With the court's permission, parties may ask each other questions. The court may reject questions that do not relate to the case.  

(2)	A judge may ask a question to a party if they express themselves unclearly or indefinitely, as well as when it is not evident from the explanations that the party acknowledges or denies the circumstances on which the opposing party's claims or objections are based.  

(3)	If a party refuses to answer a question about disputed circumstances or evades giving explanations about them, the court may assume that the party does not dispute these circumstances.

### 168. Section. Determination of the Procedure for Examination of Evidence

The court, having heard the parties' explanations and listened to their opinion, determines the procedure for examination of witnesses and experts and other evidence.

### 169. Section. Warning of a Witness

(1)	Before examining a witness, the court establishes their identity and warns them about liability for refusal to testify

or for knowingly giving false testimony, as well as explains the content of Section 107 of this law.  

(2)	Before examination, the witness gives orally an affirmation of the following content:

"I, . . . (witness's name and surname), undertake to testify to the court about everything known to me in the case in which I am summoned as a witness. It has been explained to me that for refusal to testify or for knowingly giving false testimony I face criminal liability in accordance with the Criminal Law."

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(4)	A witness who has not reached 14 years of age is explained by the judge their duty to testify truthfully, to tell everything known to them in this case, but this witness is not warned about liability for refusal to testify or for knowingly giving false testimony.  
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 170. Section. Examination of Witnesses

(1)	Each witness is examined separately.  

(2)	First, witnesses indicated by the plaintiff are examined, then — witnesses indicated by the defendant. The sequence of examination of witnesses indicated by one party is determined by the court, taking into account the opinion of that party.  

(3)	A witness gives their testimony and answers questions orally.  

(4)	The court establishes the witness's relationship with the parties and third persons and invites them to tell the court everything personally known to the witness in the case, avoiding providing information whose source they cannot indicate, as well as expressing their assumptions and conclusions. The court may interrupt the witness's narrative if they speak about circumstances that do not relate to the case.  

(5)	With the court's permission, parties may ask questions to the witness. The first to ask questions is the party at whose request the witness was summoned, then — other parties.  

(6)	A judge may ask questions to a witness at any moment of their examination. During the examination of a witness, questions may also be asked to the parties.  

(7)	The court may examine a witness a second time in the same or another court session, as well as confront witnesses.  

(8)	If the circumstances for the clarification of which witnesses were summoned have been clarified, the court, with the consent of the parties, may not examine the witnesses who have appeared, adopting an appropriate decision on this.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.12.2013 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 171. Section. Right of a Witness to Use Written Notes

During testimony, a witness may use written notes if their testimony is related to calculations or other data that are difficult to remember. These notes must be shown to the court and the parties, and they may be attached to the case by court decision.

### 172. Section. Examination of a Minor Witness

(1)	Examination of a minor witness is carried out, at the court's discretion, in the presence of a legal representative or a pedagogue. These persons may ask questions to the minor witness.  

(2)	In cases where it is necessary for clarifying the circumstances of the case, during the examination of a minor witness, by court decision, any party or person present in the courtroom may be removed from the courtroom. After the party's return to the courtroom, they are familiarised with the minor witness's testimony and given the opportunity to ask questions to the witness.  

(3)	A witness who has not reached 15 years of age must be removed from the courtroom after examination, except in cases where the court considers the presence of this witness in the courtroom necessary.

### 173. Section. Reading of a Witness's Testimony

A witness's testimony obtained in the procedure of securing evidence or court assignment or in a previous court session is read or played back, if it is recorded using audio recording, in the court session in which the case is tried.  
(With amendments made by the law of 04.02.2016, which enters into force on 29.02.2016.)

### 174. Section. Duty of an Examined Witness

An examined witness must remain in the courtroom until the end of the trial of the case. They may leave the courtroom before the end of the trial only pursuant to a court decision adopted after hearing the parties' opinions.

### 175. Section. Examination of an Expert Opinion and Examination of an Expert

(1)	An expert opinion is read in the court session.  

(2)	The court and the parties may ask questions to the expert in the same procedure as to witnesses.  

(3)	In the cases referred to in Section 125 of this law, the court may order a supplementary or repeated expert examination.

### 176. Section. Attachment of Written Evidence to the Case

(1)	The question of attaching written evidence to the case is decided by the court after it has familiarised the parties with the content of this evidence and heard their opinion.  

(2)	State secret objects are compiled in a separate volume.  

(3)	Evidence containing commercial secrets, upon a reasoned request of a party, is compiled in a separate volume.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009 and 28.02.2019, which enters into force on 01.04.2019.)

### 177. Section. Examination of Written Evidence

(1)	Written evidence or protocols of their inspection are read in the court session or shown to the parties, and, if necessary, — also to experts and witnesses.  

(2)	Personal correspondence may be read in an open court session only with the consent of the persons involved in the correspondence. If there is no such consent or the persons are deceased, the said evidence is read and examined in a closed court session.

### 178. Section. Challenging Written Evidence

(1)	Parties may challenge the authenticity of written evidence.  

(2)	A person who has signed written evidence themselves cannot object to its authenticity. This person may challenge this evidence by bringing a separate action if the signature was given under the influence of violence, threats or fraud.  

(3)	The authenticity of land register, notarial and other acts certified in the procedure prescribed by law cannot be doubted. They may be challenged by bringing a separate action.  

(4)	The submitter of challenged written evidence must give explanations in the same court session as to whether they wish to use this written evidence or request its exclusion from evidence.  

(5)	If a party wishes to use the challenged evidence, the court, having compared this evidence with other evidence in the case, decides on the admissibility of its use.

### 179. Section. Application Regarding Forgery of Written Evidence

(1)	A party may submit a reasoned application regarding forgery of written evidence.  

(2)	The person who submitted this evidence may request the court to exclude it.  

(3)	To verify an application regarding forgery of written evidence, the court may order an expert examination or request other evidence.  

(4)	If the court finds that written evidence is forged, it excludes this evidence and notifies the prosecutor of the fact of forgery.  

(5)	If the court finds that a party has knowingly and without grounds initiated a dispute regarding forgery of written evidence, it may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on this party.  
(With amendments made by the law of 12.09.2013, which enters into force on 01.01.2014.)

### 183. pants. Completion of Examination of the Case on the Merits

(1)	After all submitted evidence has been examined, the court ascertains the opinion of the parties regarding the possibility of completing the examination of the case on the merits.

(2)	If it is not necessary to examine additional evidence, the court ascertains whether the plaintiff maintains the claim and whether the parties wish to conclude a settlement.

(3)	If the plaintiff does not withdraw the claim and the parties do not wish to conclude a settlement, the court declares the examination of the case on the merits completed and proceeds to court debates.

### 184. pants. Court Debates

(1)	In court debates, the plaintiff or his or her representative speaks first, followed by the defendant or his or her representative. A prosecutor, a representative of a state or local government institution and a person who has applied to court to defend the rights and legally protected interests of other persons speak first in court debates.

(2)	If a third party with independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute participates in the case, this person or his or her representative speaks after the parties.

(3)	A third party without independent claims regarding the subject matter of the dispute, or his or her representative, speaks after the plaintiff or defendant on whose side this third party participates in the case.

(4)	A participant in court debates is not entitled to refer in his or her speech to circumstances and evidence that have not been examined in the court session.

(5)	The court may interrupt a participant in the debates if he or she speaks about circumstances that are not relevant to the case.

### 185. pants. Rebuttals

(1)	After the parties referred to in Section 184 of this Law have spoken in the debates, each of them is entitled to one rebuttal.

(2)	The court may limit the duration of rebuttals.

### 186. pants. Opinion of the Prosecutor

If a prosecutor who has not brought the claim participates in the case, he or she gives an opinion on the merits of the claim after the court debates and rebuttals.

### 187. pants. Court Deliberation

(1)	After the court debates, as well as rebuttals and the prosecutor's opinion, the court retires for deliberation to render a judgment, having announced this to those present in the courtroom.

(2)	If the court considers that it is not possible to render a judgment in this court session, it sets a date when the judgment will be prepared and available in the online system.
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003., 14.12.2017. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

### 188. pants. Resumption of Examination of the Case on the Merits

(1)	If during deliberation the court considers it necessary to ascertain new circumstances that are significant to the case, or to additionally examine existing or new evidence, it resumes the examination of the case on the merits.

(2)	In such case, the court session continues in the procedure set out in this Chapter.

### 189. pants. General Provisions

(1)	The court's decision by which the case is adjudicated on the merits is rendered by the court in the form of a judgment and is pronounced in the name of the Republic of Latvia.

(2)	The judgment is rendered and pronounced after examination of the case.

(3)	The judgment must be lawful and well-founded.

(4)	No direct or indirect interference in the rendering of a judgment or influencing of the court is permissible.
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 24.07.2003.)

### 190. pants. Lawfulness and Well-Foundedness of a Judgment

(1)	When rendering a judgment, the court is guided by the norms of substantive and procedural law.

(2)	The court bases the judgment on circumstances established by evidence in the case. In the judgment, the court does not reflect information that is the subject of a state secret or a commercial secret, but indicates that it has reviewed and evaluated this information.
(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009. un 28.02.2019. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.04.2019.)

### 191. pants. Procedure for Rendering a Judgment

(1)	(Izslēgta ar 19.06.2003. likumu.)

(2)	Only judges who are part of the court composition in the case being examined may be present at the judges' deliberation.

(3)	If the judgment is rendered collegially, the presiding judge of the court session expresses his or her opinion last.

(4)	The court, when rendering a judgment, adopts all decisions by a majority of votes. The judgment is signed by all judges.

(5)	In a case that a judge examines individually, the judgment is signed by the judge.

(6)	After the judgment has been signed, it is not permitted to amend or change it.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 19.06.2003. un 11.11.2021. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.12.2021.)

### 192. pants. Observance of the Limits of the Claim

The court renders a judgment on the subject matter of the claim specified in the claim and on the basis indicated in the claim, without exceeding the limits of the claim.

### 193. pants. Form and Content of a Judgment

(1)	The judgment is prepared in writing.

(2)	The judgment consists of an introductory part, a descriptive part, a reasoning part and an operative part.

(3)	The introductory part indicates that the judgment has been rendered in the name of the Republic of Latvia, as well as the time of rendering the judgment, the name of the court that rendered the judgment, the composition of the court, the secretary of the court session, the parties and the subject matter of the dispute.

(4)	The descriptive part indicates the plaintiff's claims, the defendant's counterclaim, objections, as well as the substance of the explanations provided by the parties.

(5)	The reasoning part indicates the facts established in the case, the evidence on which the court's conclusions are based, and the arguments by which certain evidence has been rejected. This part also indicates the normative acts by which the court has been guided, and the legal assessment of the established circumstances of the case, as well as the court's conclusions on the merits or lack of merits of the claim.

(6)	The operative part indicates the court's decision on full or partial satisfaction of the claim or on its full or partial rejection, separately showing the claims that are satisfied and those that are rejected, and the substance of the judgment. In addition, it indicates to whom and in what amount litigation costs are payable, also mentioning the name of the credit institution and the account number to which payment is to be made, the time limit for voluntary execution of the judgment, if the court has set one, the time limit and procedure for appealing the judgment, as well as the date of preparation of the judgment, observing the exceptions provided for in this Law.

### 194. Section. Abbreviated judgment, its form and content

(1)	The court prepares an abbreviated judgment:

1)	if the defendant has fully acknowledged the claim and the court grants the claim;  

2)	in the case of a default judgment, if the court grants the claim in full;  

3)	in simplified procedure cases;  

4)	(deleted by law of 25.10.2018).  

(2)	The abbreviated judgment is prepared in accordance with the requirements of Section 193 of this law, except for the descriptive part, which indicates only the subject matter of the claim, the normative acts on which the party has relied, as well as the claim, and the reasoning part, which indicates only the normative acts on which the court has relied.  

(3)	The court prepares the abbreviated judgment within 14 days.  
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017 with amendments made by the law of 25.10.2018, which enters into force on 28.11.2018.)

### 195. Section. Judgment for recovery of a sum of money

(1)	When making a judgment for recovery of a sum of money, the court indicates in the operative part the type of claim and the sum to be recovered, separately showing the principal debt and interest, the period for which interest has been awarded, the claimant's right to receive interest for the period until execution of the judgment (the date of conclusion of the auction), also stating the amount thereof, as well as the name of the credit institution and the account number to which payment is to be made, if such is indicated in the statement of claim.  

(2)	When making a judgment for recovery of a sum of money for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management expenses), for payments for services necessary for the maintenance of the building (utility services) or payments to the accumulation fund of the community of apartment owners (accumulations), the court, in addition to what is mentioned in the first paragraph of this section, indicates separately in the operative part of the judgment these claims and the sum to be recovered separately for each claim, as well as the time period for which each claim is to be satisfied.  
(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011 with amendments made by the laws of 28.05.2015 and 21.01.2021, which enters into force on 01.03.2021. See transitional provisions points 162 and 163)

### 196. Section. Judgment for return of property in kind

When making a judgment for return of property in kind, the court indicates in the operative part the specific property, and also determines that in the event of absence of the property, its value is to be recovered from the defendant, stating a specific sum.

### 197. Section. Judgment imposing an obligation to perform specific acts

(1)	In a judgment imposing an obligation to perform specific acts, the court determines specifically who must perform what acts and within what time limit.  

(2)	When making a judgment imposing on the defendant an obligation to perform specific acts which are not connected with the transfer of property or a sum of money, the court may indicate in the judgment that if the defendant does not execute the judgment within the specified time limit, the claimant is entitled to perform these acts at the defendant's expense, subsequently recovering from him the necessary expenses.

### 198. Section. Judgment in favour of several claimants or against several defendants

(1)	In a judgment in favour of several claimants, the court indicates what part of the judgment relates to each of them, or that the rights of recovery are joint and several.  

(2)	In a judgment against several defendants, the court indicates what part of the judgment is to be executed by each of them, or that their liability is joint and several.

### 199. Section. Pronouncement of judgment

(1)	The judgment is pronounced at a court hearing by reading out its introductory part and operative part, but in the case mentioned in the second paragraph of Section 187 of this law, the court sets a date within the next 30 days when the judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the judgment is available in the online system is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment.  

(2)	If the judgment is pronounced at a court hearing, the judge explains the procedure and time limits for appealing it.  

(3)	If the case is heard at a court hearing, the abbreviated judgment is pronounced at the court hearing after its preparation by reading out its introductory part and operative part, but in the case mentioned in the second paragraph of Section 187 of this law, the court sets a date within the next 14 days when the abbreviated judgment will be available in the online system. The date when the abbreviated judgment is available in the online system is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment.  

(4)	If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of pronouncement, the judgment is available at the court registry on the same date. In such a case, the date when the judgment is available at the court registry is considered the date of pronouncement of the judgment.  
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 200. Section. Correction of clerical and mathematical calculation errors

(1)	The court may, on its own initiative or upon application of a party, correct clerical and mathematical calculation errors in the judgment. The question of correction of errors is examined in written proceedings. The parties are notified in advance of the examination of the said question in written proceedings. If the application has been submitted by a party, simultaneously with sending the notification, the court sends to the parties the application for correction of clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment.  

(2)	Clerical or mathematical calculation errors in the judgment are corrected by a court decision, which is sent to the parties within three days of its adoption.  

(3)	A party may submit an interlocutory appeal against a decision to make a correction of an error in the judgment.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 201. Section. Supplementary judgment

(1)	The court that has made a judgment in a case is entitled, on its own initiative or upon application of a party, to make a supplementary judgment if:

1)	no judgment has been made on one of the claims in respect of which the parties have submitted evidence and given explanations;  
2)	the court has not determined the amount of the sum awarded, the property to be transferred, the acts to be performed, or the reimbursement of litigation costs.  

(2)	The making of a supplementary judgment may be initiated within the time limit for appealing the judgment established by law.  

(3)	The court notifies the parties of the time and place of examination of this question. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to deciding the question of making a supplementary judgment.  

(4)	An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the court's decision to refuse to make a supplementary judgment.

### 202. Section. Clarification of judgment

(1)	The court that has made a judgment may, upon application of a party, clarify it by its decision without changing the content of the judgment.  

(2)	Clarification of a judgment is permissible if it has not yet been executed and the time limit for its compulsory execution has not expired.  

(3)	The question of clarification of a judgment is examined in written proceedings, with prior notification to the parties. Simultaneously with the notification, the court sends to the parties the application for clarification of the judgment.  

(4)	An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the court's decision on the question of clarification of the judgment.  
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 203. Section. Entry into Legal Force of a Judgment

(1) A court judgment enters into legal force after the time limit for appealing it has expired and no appeal has been filed. If the appellate court has left the appeal without consideration or has terminated the appellate proceedings, the judgment enters into force from the moment of the announcement of the respective decision.

(2) If a judgment has been appealed in part, the judgment enters into force in the part not appealed when the time limit for appealing it has expired.

(21) If, with respect to at least one party to the case, the time limit for filing an appeal against a first instance court judgment is determined in accordance with Section 415, Paragraph 2.2 of this Law, the court judgment enters into legal force after the time limit for appealing it has expired, counting the time limit from the later date of issuance of the judgment, if no appeal has been filed.

(22) If, in the cases referred to in Paragraph 2.1 of this Section, the relevant confirmation of the issuance of the judgment has not been received (Section 56.2), the judgment enters into legal force six months after its announcement.

(3) After a judgment has entered into legal force, the parties to the case, as well as their successors in title, are not entitled in other proceedings to contest the facts established by the court, or to bring a new action in court concerning the same subject matter on the same grounds, except in cases provided for in this Law.

(4) If, after a judgment has entered into legal force by which periodic payments have been awarded from the defendant, circumstances change that affect the determination of the amount or duration of payments, each party is entitled, by filing a new claim, to request a change in the amount or term of payments.

(5) A judgment that has entered into legal force has the force of law, it is binding and enforceable throughout the entire territory of the state, and it may be revoked only in cases and in the manner provided for by law.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 204. Section. Enforcement of a Judgment

A judgment shall be enforced after it has entered into legal force, except in cases where the judgment is immediately enforceable.

204. 1 Section. Voluntary Enforcement of a Judgment

(1) When rendering a judgment for the recovery of a sum of money, for the return of property in kind, for the eviction of persons and property from premises, and for the recovery of litigation costs, the court shall set a time limit for voluntary enforcement of the judgment, except in cases where the judgment is immediately enforceable.

(2) The time limit for voluntary enforcement of a judgment may not be longer than 10 days from the date the judgment enters into force.
(In the wording of the law of 17.02.2005., which enters into force on 10.03.2005.)

### 205. Section. Immediately Enforceable Judgments

(1) At the request of a party to the case, the court may determine in the judgment that the following judgments are immediately enforceable in whole or in a specified part:

1) for the recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;

2) for the recovery of wages;

3) for reinstatement in employment;

4) for compensation for mutilation or other injury to health;

5) for the recovery of maintenance in connection with the death of a person who had a duty to support someone;

6) in cases where the defendant has acknowledged the claim;

7) in cases where, due to special circumstances, delay in the enforcement of the judgment may cause significant losses to the creditor or the recovery itself may become impossible;

8) in cases arising from custody and contact rights.

(2) Immediate enforcement of a judgment in the case provided for in point 7 of the first paragraph of this Section is permissible only by requiring from the creditor adequate security in the event that the appellate court modifies the judgment.

(3) In the cases provided for in points 1 and 8 of the first paragraph of this Section, the court may also, on its own initiative, determine that the judgment is immediately enforceable in whole or in a specified part.
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2011., 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 206. Section

Postponement of Enforcement of a Judgment, Division into Instalments, Modification of its Method or Procedure of Enforcement

(1) The court that rendered the judgment in the case is entitled, at the request of a party to the case, taking into account the financial situation of the parties, the rights of children or other circumstances, to adopt a decision on postponing the enforcement of the judgment or dividing it into instalments, as well as on modifying its method and procedure of enforcement. A decision on postponing the enforcement of a judgment, dividing it into instalments or modifying the method and procedure of enforcement is immediately enforceable.

(2) The application shall be examined in written proceedings, with prior notice to the parties to the case. Simultaneously with the notice, the court, setting a time limit for the submission of an explanation, sends to the parties to the case the application for postponement of enforcement of the judgment, division into instalments, or modification of its method or procedure of enforcement.

(3) An ancillary appeal may be filed against the court's decision to postpone the enforcement of a judgment or to divide it into instalments, as well as to modify its method and procedure of enforcement. The filing of an ancillary appeal does not suspend the enforcement of the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 14.12.2006., 08.09.2011. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

206. 1 Section. Issues of Enforcement of a Judgment Rendered in the Procedure Provided for in Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council and of a European Payment Order Rendered in the Procedure Provided for in Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council

(1) The court that rendered a judgment in the procedure provided for in Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council or a European Payment Order in the procedure provided for in Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council is entitled, at the request of the debtor, in the cases provided for in Article 15(2) of Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council or in Article 23 of Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council:

1) to replace the enforcement of the judgment or European Payment Order with the measures provided for in Section 138 of this Law to secure the enforcement of this judgment or European Payment Order;

2) to modify the method or procedure of enforcement of the judgment or European Payment Order;

3) to suspend the enforcement of the judgment or European Payment Order.

(2) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Section shall be examined in written proceedings, with prior notice to the parties to the case. Simultaneously with the notice, the court, setting a time limit for the submission of an explanation, sends the application to the parties to the case.

(3) An ancillary appeal may be filed against the court's decision.

(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009. with amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011. and 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 207. Section. Security for Enforcement of a Judgment

At the request of the parties to the case, the court may determine in the judgment the measures provided for in Section 138 of this Law or in Chapter 77.3 to secure the enforcement of the judgment.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. Amendments to the Section in connection with the European Account Preservation Order enter into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision point 121)

### 208. Section. Sending of a Judgment to the Parties to the Case

(1) A judgment shall be sent to a party to the case who has not participated in the court hearing no later than within three days after the announcement of the judgment.

(2) (Deleted as of 01.03.2018. by the law of 14.12.2017. See transitional provision point 137)

(3) If, in the cases referred to in the first paragraph of this Section, a judgment is to be sent to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this Law and, in cases provided for in this Law, a translation is to be attached to the judgment, the court shall send the judgment together with the translation immediately after the preparation of the translation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

208.1 Article. Judgment by default

(1) A judgment by default is a judgment made by a first instance court in a case where the defendant has not provided an explanation regarding the claim and has not appeared following the court's summons, without notifying the reason for non-appearance.

(2) The court makes a judgment by default based on the plaintiff's explanations and the materials in the case, if the court considers them sufficient for resolving the dispute.

(3) A judgment by default cannot be made in cases:

1) which cannot be terminated by settlement;

2) where the defendant's declared place of residence, place of residence, location or legal address is not in the Republic of Latvia;

3) where the defendant is summoned to court by publication in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis";

4) where there are several defendants and at least one participates in the proceedings.

(4) The provisions on judgment by default do not apply to special proceedings.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.2 Article. Form and content of judgment by default

(1) The court makes and compiles a judgment by default in the procedure specified in Articles 189-198 of this law, observing the specificities established in this Article.

(2) The fact that the judgment is by default is indicated in its title.

(3) The descriptive part of a judgment by default indicates the plaintiff's claims, the essence of the plaintiff's explanation, the procedural basis for making this judgment, except in cases where the descriptive part of the judgment by default is made in accordance with the requirements of Article 194, paragraph 1, point 2 and paragraph 2 of this law.

(4) In the operative part of a judgment by default, in addition to that mentioned in Article 193, paragraph 6 of this law, the court indicates that the plaintiff is entitled to appeal the judgment by way of appeal, but the defendant within 20 days from the date of sending the judgment by default is entitled to submit to the court that made the judgment by default an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.3 Article. Sending of judgment by default to the defendant

A judgment by default is sent to the defendant to the official electronic address or by registered mail.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

208.4 Article. Appeal of judgment by default

(1) The plaintiff is entitled to appeal a judgment by default by way of appeal.

(2) The defendant is not entitled to appeal a judgment by default by way of appeal.

208.5 Article. Restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case

(1) The defendant is entitled within 20 days from the date of sending the judgment by default to submit to the court that made the judgment by default an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case.

(2) The application indicates:

1) the name of the court that made the judgment by default;

2) the defendant's name, surname, personal code, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the defendant agrees to electronic communication with the court, also indicates the email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also includes an indication of registration;

21) the name of the credit institution and account number to which litigation costs are to be reimbursed;

3) the date of making the judgment by default and its essence;

4) the reasons why the defendant did not take part in the case;

5) the defendant's objections to the claim and judgment, the basis for the objections;

6) evidence confirming the objections and their basis, the law on which they are based;

7) requests for acceptance of evidence or its procurement;

8) a request to restore proceedings in the case and re-examine the case.

(3) The following documents are attached to the application confirming:

1) payment of state fee and other court costs in the procedure and amount established by law, except in cases where the application is submitted and payment is made in the online system;

2) the basis for the objections.

(4) Evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based is attached to the application.

(5) An unsigned application is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015., 23.11.2016., 22.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.6 Article. Leaving application without movement

(1) The judge leaves the application without movement if:

1) the application does not contain all the requisites established in Article 208.5, paragraph 2 of this law;

2) the documents established in Article 208.5, paragraphs 3 and 4 of this law are not attached to the application.

(2) The judge adopts a reasoned decision on leaving the application without movement, which is sent to the defendant, and sets a time limit, not shorter than 20 days, for remedying deficiencies. The time limit is counted from the date of issuance of the decision. The judge's decision is appealable in the procedure established in this law. The appeal time limit is counted from the date of issuance of the decision.

(3) If the defendant has not remedied the deficiencies within the time limit set by the judge, the application is considered not submitted and is returned to the defendant. The decision on returning the application is not appealable.

(4) If the application is returned to the defendant, he or she does not have the right to repeatedly submit an application to the court.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force 01.12.2021.)

208.7 Article. Actions of the judge after acceptance of the application

(1) Having found that the application complies with the requirements of Article 208.5 of this law, the judge notifies the plaintiff and third parties about the application and sends them the application. Depending on the circumstances and nature of the case, the documents attached to the claim may also be sent to the plaintiff and third parties.

(2) The judge examines the application within seven days after its receipt and adopts one of the following decisions:

1) on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, if it finds that the examination of the case without the defendant's participation and verification of the evidence submitted by him or her has led or could have led to incorrect adjudication of the case;

2) on rejection of the application, if it finds that there is no basis specified in point 1 of paragraph 2 of this Article for re-examination of the case.

(3) In the decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case, the judge sets the day and time of the court session and the persons to be summoned and called to court.

(4) If a decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has been adopted and the plaintiff has submitted an appeal against the judgment by default, the appeal is returned to the plaintiff.

(5) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against a decision rejecting the application. A decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case is not appealable.
(With amendments made by the laws of 11.11.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force 07.07.2022.)

208.8 Article. Entry into legal force of judgment by default

(1) A judgment by default enters into legal force if an appeal has not been submitted within the time limit established by law and an application for restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has not been submitted.

(2) If an application for restoration of proceedings has been rejected and an appeal against the court judgment has not been submitted, the judgment by default enters into force after the time limit for appealing the judge's decision has expired.

(3) If the judge's decision on rejection of the application has been appealed and the appellate court has left it unchanged, the judgment by default enters into force from the moment of pronouncement of the appellate court's decision.

208.9 Article. Re-examination of the case

If a decision on restoration of proceedings and re-examination of the case has been adopted, the judgment by default does not enter into force and the case is re-examined in full in the procedure provided for in Chapter 21 of this law. The restriction established by law on a judge's participation in re-examination of a case does not apply to this case.

### 227. Section. Conclusion of a settlement

(1) The parties conclude the settlement in writing and submit it to the court.

(2) The settlement shall indicate:

1) the claimant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; if the claimant is a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address;

2) the defendant's name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if they are known, but if the defendant is a legal person — its name,

registration number and legal address;

3) the subject matter of the dispute;

4) the obligations of each party that it voluntarily undertakes to perform.

(3) The court may approve the settlement without the presence of a party at a court hearing or in written proceedings if the settlement has been made before a notary in the form of a notarial deed and contains a statement by the parties that they are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 04.02.2016., which enter into force on 29.02.2016.)

### 228. Section. Court decision on approval of settlement

(1) Upon receiving the parties' settlement, the court shall ascertain whether the parties have voluntarily agreed to the settlement, whether it complies with the requirements of Sections 226 and 227 of this law and whether the parties are aware of the procedural consequences of approving the settlement.

(2) If the court finds that the settlement complies with the requirements of this law, it shall adopt a decision approving the settlement and terminating the proceedings in the case.

(3) A settlement approved by a court decision shall be enforceable in accordance with the rules for enforcement of court judgments.

28. Chapter Court decision

### 229. Section. Adoption of a decision

(1) A court ruling by which a case is not decided on the merits shall be adopted in the form of a decision.

(2) A decision shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document or recorded in the minutes of the court hearing and announced after its adoption. In cases provided for in this law, a decision may be drawn up in the form of a resolution. In such a case, only the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, as well as the ruling of the court or judge shall be indicated.

(3) In the form of a separate procedural document, a court decision shall be drawn up in cases provided for in this law.

(4) A decision may be adopted regarding a judge's procedural action outside a court hearing, which shall be drawn up in the form of a separate procedural document.
(With amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012., 29.10.2015. and 25.10.2018., which enter into force on 28.11.2018.)

### 230. Section. Form and content of a decision

(1) A decision shall consist of an introductory part, a descriptive part, a reasoning part and an operative part.

(2) The introductory part shall indicate the time and place of adoption of the decision, the name and composition of the court, the parties to the case and the subject matter of the dispute.

(3) The descriptive part shall indicate the issues on which the decision has been adopted.

(4) The reasoning part shall indicate the established facts, the evidence on which the conclusions and arguments of the court or judge are based, as well as the normative acts by which the court has been guided.

(5) The operative part shall indicate the ruling of the court or judge and the procedure and time limits for appealing the decision.

(6) In decisions that are necessary for a bailiff, additional information shall be provided about the parties to the case [natural person
— claimant or applicant — name, surname, personal identity number (if known) and declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence; natural person — defendant — name, surname, personal identity number (if known), declared place of residence, additional address (addresses) indicated in the declaration and place of residence, if known; legal person — name, legal address and registration number].

(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015., which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

230.1 Section. Abbreviated decision

(1) The court shall draw up an abbreviated decision:

1) on granting an application for undisputed enforcement of obligations;

2) on granting or partially granting an application for enforcement of obligations in warning procedure
— with respect to the granted part;

3) on approving a settlement concluded by the parties.

(2) An abbreviated decision shall be drawn up in accordance with the requirements of Section 230 of this law, except for the reasoning part, which shall indicate only the normative acts by which the court has been guided.

(3) The abbreviated decision referred to in paragraph 3 of the first part of this section shall be announced and sent in accordance with Section 231 of this law.
(In the wording of the law of 14.12.2017. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 231. Section. Announcement and sending of a decision

(1) The court shall announce the decision at a court hearing by reading its introductory part and operative part or by setting a date within the next 14 days when the decision will be available in the online system. The date when the decision is available in the online system shall be considered the date of announcement of the decision. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be considered drawn up on the date when it is available in the online system. If for technical reasons it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the date of announcement or drawing up of the decision, the decision shall be available at the court registry on the same date. In such a case, the date when the decision is available at the court registry shall be considered the date of announcement or drawing up of the decision.

(2) A court decision shall be sent within three days after the announcement of the decision to a party to the case who has not participated in the court hearing and to a person to whom it relates. A decision adopted in written proceedings shall be sent within three days from the drawing up of the decision.

(3) If a court decision in the cases referred to in the first and second parts of this section has been sent to a person in accordance with Section 56.2 of this law and in cases provided for in this law a translation must be attached to the court decision, the court shall send the decision together with the translation immediately after the preparation of the translation.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 29.10.2015., 14.12.2017., 31.05.2018. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 232. Section. Supplementary decision of the court

(1) If, when examining a case, circumstances are established that indicate a possible violation of law, the court shall be entitled to adopt a supplementary decision, which shall be sent to the relevant institution.

(2) A supplementary decision of the court shall not be subject to appeal.

In the wording of the law of 06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.1 Section. Jurisdiction of the court over complaints about actions of a sworn notary and procedure for submission

A complaint about the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties, as well as a complaint about refusal to perform these duties, shall be submitted by a person whose rights have been affected to the district (city) court at the address of the sworn notary's place of practice within 30 days from the day when the sworn notary performed the action about which the complaint has been submitted or when he or she

refused to perform such an action.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232.2 Section. Procedure for examining complaints

(1) The court shall examine a complaint within 30 days from the date of receipt of the complaint.

(2) The court shall examine a complaint in written proceedings without holding a court hearing, except when it considers it necessary to examine the case at a court hearing or when the complainant, sworn notary or other interested persons request that the case be examined at a court hearing, substantiating their request. The complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons shall be invited to the court hearing. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to examining the matter.

(3) The court shall send a copy of the decision adopted after examining the complaint to the complainant, sworn notary and other interested persons.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

232. 3 Section. Appeal of decisions adopted on complaints

(1) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision within the time limit and in the manner prescribed by this law.

(2) A court decision by which a complaint about the actions of a sworn notary in performing official duties in a case on the discharge of a natural person from debt obligations has been examined shall not be subject to appeal.
(In the wording of the law of 15.06.2021., which enters into force on 01.01.2022.)

Cases concerning the nullity or dissolution of marriage shall be heard by the court in the procedure of a claim according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

### 234. Section. Jurisdiction of Cases

A claim concerning the nullity of marriage or dissolution of marriage may also be brought before a court according to the plaintiff's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the plaintiff's place of residence, if:

(With amendments made by the law of 29.11.2012., which comes into force on 01.01.2013.)

### 235. Section. Cases Concerning Dissolution of Marriage upon Application of Both Spouses

(Deleted by the law of 28.10.2010., which comes into force on 01.02.2011.)

235.	1 Section. Statement of Claim Concerning Dissolution of Marriage

In the statement of claim, in addition to that provided for in Section 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1)	from what time the parties have lived separately;  

2)	whether the other spouse consents to the dissolution of marriage;  

3)	whether the parties have agreed on the custody of the child, the procedure for exercising the other parent's contact rights, maintenance and the division of property acquired during the marriage, or submit respective claims.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 19.06.2003., which comes into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 236. Section. Participation of Parties in Court Session

(1)	A case concerning dissolution of marriage shall be heard with the participation of both parties.  

(11) Upon the request of one spouse, the court may hear each spouse in a separate court session if the dissolution of marriage is related to violence against the spouse who requests the dissolution of marriage, or against his or her child, or the spouses' common child.  

(2)	If the defendant fails to appear upon the court's summons without a valid reason, if it has been sent to the official electronic address or by registered mail, he or she may be brought to court by force.  

(3)	If one of the parties lives far away or for another reason cannot appear upon the court's summons, the court may recognise that written explanations of this party or the participation of its representative are sufficient for hearing the case.  

(4)	If the defendant's place of residence is unknown or it is not in Latvia, the case may be heard without the defendant's participation if he or she has been summoned to court in the procedure prescribed by law.  

(5)	In a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage, the representative of a party must be specially authorised to conduct this case. The authorisation for representation in a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage also extends to all other claims related thereto.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 29.11.2012., 23.11.2016. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 237. Section. Bringing a Claim Concerning Nullity of Marriage

A claim concerning the nullity of marriage may be brought by an interested person and the prosecutor.

### 238. Section. Prohibition of Division of Claim

(1)	In a case concerning dissolution or nullity of marriage, claims arising from family legal relations shall be adjudicated simultaneously. Such claims are disputes concerning:

1)	the establishment of custody;  

2)	the exercise of contact rights;  

3)	maintenance for a child, including maintenance in the minimum amount determined by the Cabinet of Ministers;  

4)	means for ensuring the previous standard of living of a spouse;  

5)	the common family dwelling and household or personal use items;  

6)	the division of spouses' property (also if it affects a third party).

238.	1 Section. Interim Decision in Certain Claims

(1)	Upon a party's request, the court or judge may adopt a decision by which, temporarily until the judgment is rendered concerning the dissolution of marriage or nullity of marriage, the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, maintenance for the child, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, means for ensuring the other spouse's previous standard of living, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling are determined, or one party is ordered to deliver household and personal use items to the other party.  

(2)	A request concerning maintenance for a child and means for ensuring a spouse's previous standard of living shall be heard in written proceedings.  

(3)	A request concerning the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country, the procedure for using the spouses' common dwelling, or an order for one party to deliver household and personal use items to the other party shall be heard in a court session.  

(4)	In claims affecting a child (concerning the child's place of residence, the procedure for the child's care, the procedure for exercising contact rights, a prohibition on the child's removal from the country), a representative of the orphan's court, upon the court's request, shall provide any information that is relevant in the case concerning:

1)	the living conditions of the parties;  

2)	the child's opinion, if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity;  

3)	the child's contact with the parties and other persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;  

4)	the child's health care and education;  

5)	the parties' cooperation with the social service;  

6)	persons who live or are known to be going to live with the child in one household;  

7)	the parties' violence against the child or the child's parent.  

(5)	The parties shall be notified of the court session, but in claims affecting a child — a representative of the orphan's court shall be summoned to the court session. If the court considers it necessary to clarify the information provided by the orphan's court, it shall ascertain the child's opinion if the child is capable of formulating it, taking into account his or her age and degree of maturity. The non-appearance of the other spouse is not an obstacle to hearing the claim.  

(6)	If in claims concerning the procedure for exercising contact rights the court, upon a participant's request or on its own initiative, establishes that contact rights are to be exercised in the presence of a contact person, the court shall invite the contact person to participate in the court session. The court shall ascertain whether the contact person consents to contact rights being exercised in its presence.  

(7)	The court or judge shall hear the party's request and adopt a decision within one month from the date of receipt of the request. The decision shall be enforceable immediately. The decision shall lose force when a judgment enters into force in the case or when another decision is adopted, except in cases when the decision is enforceable immediately.  

(8)	A judge's decision concerning the claims referred to in Paragraph two of this Section is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be filed against a court decision in a case concerning the claims referred to in Paragraph three of this Section.  

(9)	Upon a party's reasoned request, the court may review a decision concerning the request referred to in Paragraph three of this Section if circumstances have substantially changed and it is in the child's interests. Such a court decision is not subject to appeal.  

(10)	If the court does not establish grounds for reviewing the decision or adopting a new decision, or considers that it may commence hearing the case on the merits, it shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application. The court shall adopt the decision to refuse to accept the application in the form of a resolution, and it is not subject to appeal.  
(In the wording of the law of 29.10.2015. with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)
