## (Chapter 13

In the wording of the 02.2014 law, which enters into force on 31.03.2014.)

Article 250.43 Admissibility of Temporary Protection Against Violence in Claims

Temporary protection against violence is admissible in claims for nullity or dissolution of marriage, in claims for personal injury, in claims for recovery of maintenance, in claims for division of the parties' common dwelling in which they live in one household, or for determination of the procedure for use of the dwelling in which the parties live in one household, and in cases arising from custody and contact rights.

Article 250.44 Persons Who May Submit an Application for Temporary Protection Against Violence

An application for temporary protection against violence may be submitted by spouses or former spouses; persons between whom there exists a parent-child relationship, there exists or has existed a guardianship or other out-of-family care relationship; persons between whom there exists a relationship of kinship or affinity; persons who live or have lived in one household; persons who have or are expecting a common child, regardless of whether these persons have ever been married or have ever lived together; persons between whom there exists or has existed a close personal or intimate relationship.

Article 250.45 Grounds for Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) If a person is subjected to any physical, sexual, psychological or economic violence that occurs between former or current spouses or other mutually related persons regardless of whether the offender lives or has lived in one household with the injured person, the court or judge, upon a reasoned application of the person or an application submitted through police intermediation, may adopt a decision on temporary protection against violence.

(2) The first paragraph of this Article shall also apply in cases where a person is subjected to violent control — such action or set of actions that includes injury, sexual coercion, threats, humiliation, intimidation or other violent actions whose purpose is to harm, punish or intimidate the injured person.

(3) It is permissible to examine the question of temporary protection against violence at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before filing a claim in court.

Article 250.46 Content of an Application for Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) An application for temporary protection against violence shall be formatted in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(2) The application for temporary protection against violence shall indicate:

1) the name of the court to which the application is submitted;

2) the claimant's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. If the claimant consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration. The claimant may additionally also indicate another address for communication with the court;

3) the respondent's first name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence. The respondent's personal identity number shall be indicated if it is known;

4) the claimant's representative's (if the application is submitted by a representative) first name, surname, personal identity number and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and legal address. If the claimant's representative, whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia, consents to electronic communication with the court, the email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also include an indication of registration. If the claimant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of participation in the online system shall be provided;

5) the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law and how these circumstances manifest themselves;

6) evidence confirming the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law, if such is in the claimant's possession and if the person from whom the said evidence is obtainable is known, but it is not in the claimant's possession or the claimant cannot obtain it himself or herself for objective reasons;

7) the applicable temporary protection against violence measure or measures;

8) a list of documents attached to the application;

9) a confirmation that truthful information about facts has been provided to the court and the claimant or the claimant and representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed of liability in accordance with the Criminal Law for submission of a false application;

10) the time of preparation of the application and other information if it is necessary for examination of the case.

(3) If the applicable temporary protection measure is an obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and remain therein, an annex shall be attached to the application indicating the claimant's contact information (telephone, email address, address) so that the State Police, by contacting the claimant, can carry out control of execution of the relevant decision. This annex is information of limited access, which in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 250.62 of this Law is sent to the State Police and is not attached to the case materials.

(31) In the application, the claimant may request the court to send the decision on temporary protection against violence to the social service at the claimant's place of residence.

(4) If the application does not contain the confirmation referred to in point 9 of the second paragraph of this Article, the application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.

(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.47 Temporary Protection Against Violence Measures

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures are:

1) an obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and a prohibition to return and remain therein;

2) a prohibition for the respondent to be closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court decision on temporary protection against violence;

3) a prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places;

4) a prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her;

5) a prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way;

6) a prohibition for the respondent to arrange, through the intermediation of another person, a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant;

7) a prohibition for the respondent to use the claimant's personal data;

71) an obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, the scope, procedure for receipt, payment, execution, interruption and termination of which shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers;

8) other prohibitions and obligations that the court or judge has imposed on the respondent and whose purpose is to ensure the claimant's temporary protection against violence.

(2) The temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of this Article shall be imposed if the respondent has reached the age of majority.

(3) It is permissible to impose several temporary protection against violence measures simultaneously.

(With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021. Point 7.1 of the first paragraph enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.48 Obligation for the Respondent to Leave the Dwelling in Which the Claimant Permanently Resides, and Prohibition to Return and Remain Therein

(1) The obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and the prohibition to return and remain therein is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to stay and remain in this dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of this dwelling.

(2) If the respondent is subject to the restriction referred to in this Article, the respondent shall be ensured the right to take or shall be issued the necessary clothing, footwear, linen, books, instruments, tools, items necessary for health care and other items that the respondent needs on a daily basis located in the dwelling.

Article 250.49 Prohibition for the Respondent to Be Closer to the Dwelling in Which the Claimant Permanently Resides Than the Distance Specified in the Court Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

The prohibition for the respondent to be closer to the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides than the distance specified in the court or judge's decision on temporary protection against violence is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to visit the relevant dwelling and to be closer to it than the distance specified in the decision.

Article 250.50 Prohibition for the Respondent to Remain in Specified Places

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to visit the relevant place, which is not the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, or to be closer to this place than the distance specified in the decision.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to remain in specified places applies to the address of a specific place or places that correspond to certain characteristics, or to public or other specified events. The court or judge shall, as far as possible, take into account the respondent's obligations to appear at the workplace and other obligations of the respondent related to appearing in specified places.

Article 250.51 Prohibition for the Respondent to Meet with the Claimant and Maintain Physical or Visual Contact with Him or Her

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to deliberately approach or be closer to the claimant than the distance specified in the decision and to avoid physical or visual contact with the claimant.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to meet with the claimant and maintain physical or visual contact with him or her also applies to persons who are closely related to or dependent on the claimant.

Article 250.52 Prohibition for the Respondent to Communicate with the Claimant in Any Way

(1) The prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to use means of communication, including electronic means of communication, or any other methods of transmitting information to contact the claimant.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the restriction referred to in this Article, may indicate that the prohibition for the respondent to communicate with the claimant in any way also applies to persons who are closely related to or dependent on the claimant.

Article 250.53 Prohibition for the Respondent to Arrange, Through the Intermediation of Another Person, a Meeting or Any Kind of Communication with the Claimant

The prohibition for the respondent to arrange, through the intermediation of another person, a meeting or any kind of communication with the claimant is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to use the intermediation of another person to approach the claimant or arrange physical or visual contact with the claimant or to contact the claimant using any means of communication or any other methods of transmitting information.

Article 250.54 Prohibition for the Respondent to Use the Claimant's Personal Data

The prohibition for the respondent to use the claimant's personal data is a restriction provided by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to process, publish, make known or otherwise use the claimant's personal data in any way, except in procedural actions related to legal proceedings.

Article 250.54A Obligation for the Respondent to Complete a Social Rehabilitation Course for Reduction of Violent Behaviour

(1) The obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour is an obligation imposed by a court or judge's decision for the respondent to complete this course in order to prevent or reduce further risks of violence.

(2) The court or judge, when imposing on the respondent the obligation referred to in this Article, shall also impose on the respondent an obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent if the respondent begins to complete the course within six months, and in full if the respondent begins to complete the course after six months.

(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 01.07.2021. The Article enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.55 Temporary Protection Against Violence Before Filing a Claim

(1) A potential claimant may submit a reasoned application requesting the court to ensure temporary protection against violence before filing a claim in court if the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law exist.

(2) If the circumstances referred to in the first and second paragraphs of Article 250.45 of this Law relate to a child, the application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article may be submitted in the child's interests by one of the child's parents, a guardian, an orphan's court or a prosecutor.

(3) An application for temporary protection against violence before filing a claim shall be submitted to the court at the place where the injury was inflicted or the applicant's location.

(With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.56 Temporary Protection Against Violence Before Filing a Claim Upon an Application Submitted Through Police Intermediation

(1) If, before filing a claim, the police have adopted a decision that imposes an obligation on a potential respondent who poses a threat to leave the dwelling, not to return and not to remain therein or in its vicinity, or prohibits the potential respondent from contacting the potential claimant (police decision on separation), the police, at the request of the potential claimant, shall send to the court a copy of the police decision, the potential claimant's application indicating that the potential claimant wishes the court to examine the question of temporary protection against violence, as well as other information that is in the police's possession and relates to the question of temporary protection against violence.

(2) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall be formatted in accordance with the model approved by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(3) The application referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, as well as other information, shall be sent by the police to the court at the place where the injury was inflicted or the applicant's location.

(4) The potential claimant's application submitted through police intermediation need not contain authorisation for the police to submit the application on behalf of the applicant.

(5) The question of temporary protection against violence, based on the potential claimant's application submitted through police intermediation, shall be examined by the judge in accordance with the first paragraph of Article 250.58 of this Law.

(With amendments made by the law of 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

Article 250.57 Evidence in Cases of Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) In cases of temporary protection against violence, a party to the case shall confirm the circumstances significant to the case indicated in the application with a confirmation.

(2) If there is no other evidence or it is insufficient, the court on its own initiative may request in a court session that a party to the case confirm his or her explanations containing information about facts and circumstances on which his or her claims or objections are based.

(3) Before providing an explanation, a party to the case shall give orally a confirmation of the following content:

"I, (first name, surname), confirm that in good conscience I will tell only the truth and will not conceal anything. I confirm that the information I have provided to the court about facts and circumstances of the case is exhaustive and truthful. I have been warned that I may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law for deliberately providing false explanations and deliberately concealing facts and circumstances of the case known to me."

(4) (Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021)

(5) A party to the case may be held criminally liable in accordance with the Criminal Law for providing confirmed deliberately false explanations or an application to the court.

(6) Confirmation of explanations and an application as evidence is not admissible with respect to such circumstances that have been established by a court judgment that has entered into force, as well as for confirmation or refutation of generally known facts.

(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.58 Examination of the Question of Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) The court or judge shall decide on an application for temporary protection against violence no later than the next day after receipt of the application if it is not necessary to request additional evidence or delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights. The court or judge shall decide on the said application without prior notification to the parties to the case.

(2) If the evidence is insufficient or it must be requested from the state or local government institutions or other natural or legal persons indicated in the application, the court or judge, at the request of a party to the case or on its own initiative, shall request evidence or invite institutions to provide an opinion and shall decide on the application for temporary protection against violence within 20 days after its receipt.

(3) The court or judge shall decide on an application for temporary protection against violence even if the application does not indicate all the information referred to in Article 250.46 of this Law or documents are attached, provided that the lack of documents or necessary information does not substantially affect the possibility of deciding on the application.

(4) The court or judge, when deciding on an application for temporary protection against violence, shall take into account the proportionality between the infringement of rights or potential infringement and the temporary protection against violence measure to be applied. The court or judge may, at its discretion, also impose another temporary protection against violence measure that is not indicated in the application.

(5) If it appears prima facie from the application for temporary protection against violence that delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, the court or judge shall decide on this application in accordance with the first paragraph of this Article and may grant it based on the confirmation contained in the application even in cases where there is no other evidence or it is insufficient.

(6) If it does not appear prima facie from the application for temporary protection against violence that delay could cause substantial infringement of the claimant's rights, and it has not been possible to obtain other evidence in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article, the court or judge shall decide on this application in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article and may grant it based on the confirmation contained in the application and confirmation of explanations provided in accordance with the second and third paragraphs of Article 250.57 of this Law.

(7) When granting an application for temporary protection against violence before filing a claim, the court or judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a statement of claim to the court, not longer than one year, but when imposing temporary protection against violence measures referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant — not longer than 30 days.

(71) When examining a claim, the court or judge may, on its own initiative, apply the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law.

(8) When granting a claim, temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, which shall be in force until its execution.

(9) In individual cases, the court may determine in the judgment that temporary protection against violence shall also be in force after the judgment enters into legal force, but not longer than one year after the judgment enters into legal force. If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in points 1 and 2 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been imposed on a respondent who permanently resides in the dwelling together with the claimant, the court may determine that temporary protection against violence shall be in force for not longer than 30 days after the judgment enters into legal force.

(10) When rejecting a claim, the court shall revoke temporary protection against violence in the judgment. Temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.

(11) If a claim is left without examination or proceedings are terminated, the court shall revoke temporary protection against violence by a decision. Temporary protection against violence shall be in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.

(12) If a decision on temporary protection against violence has been adopted before filing a claim and the claim has not been filed within the time limit set by the court, the judge, upon receipt of a reasoned application from the potential claimant or respondent, shall adopt a decision on revocation of temporary protection against violence. In this case, litigation costs shall not be reimbursed.

(13) The application referred to in the second paragraph of this Article shall be examined in written proceedings. If the court considers it necessary, the application may be examined in a closed court session, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, at the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court session. The respondent's failure to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the application.

(With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.59 Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) In addition to what is provided in Article 230 of this Law, the court or judge shall indicate in the decision information about the parties to the case [first name, surname, personal identity number (if it is known), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration and place of residence].

(2) The court or judge, in a decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — shall, if necessary, indicate the time limit for voluntary execution of the decision.

(3) The court or judge shall warn the respondent in the decision on temporary protection against violence that the police will carry out control of execution of the decision and, if the decision is not executed voluntarily, the respondent will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(4) The court or judge shall indicate in the decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides — that:

1) the respondent has an obligation to notify the court of his or her further address for communication with the court if this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration and the respondent has not consented to electronic communication with the court;

11) the respondent is prohibited from alienating or transferring the dwelling, hindering or obstructing the use of the dwelling or deteriorating the condition of the dwelling regardless of whether the respondent is the owner, possessor or user of the dwelling;

2) the respondent has the right to submit an application to the court for replacement or revocation of the temporary protection against violence measure;

3) the date when the State Police familiarises the respondent with the decision shall be considered the date when the said decision is notified to the respondent, and that the respondent's refusal to familiarise himself or herself with the decision does not affect its legal consequences;

4) the decision is available in the online system.

(41) The court or judge shall indicate in the decision on imposition of a temporary protection against violence measure — obligation for the respondent to complete a social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour:

1) the contact information of the violent behaviour reduction service provider and the respondent's obligation to contact the violent behaviour reduction service provider within 10 days from the date of receipt of the decision;

2) the respondent's obligation to complete the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour within one year from the date of receipt of the decision and a warning to the respondent that if this course is not completed within one year, he or she will be liable in accordance with the Criminal Law;

3) the respondent's obligation to partially cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in the amount of 10 percent if the respondent has begun to complete this course within six months from the date of receipt of the decision, and in full if the respondent has begun to complete the course after six months from the date of receipt of the decision, as well as that if the respondent does not cover these costs voluntarily, they will be recovered in the procedure established in this Law;

4) a warning to the respondent that covering the costs of the rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour does not release him or her from the obligation to complete the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour and liability in accordance with the Criminal Law.

(5) A decision on temporary protection against violence (first and second paragraphs of Article 250.58) shall be executed immediately after its adoption, except for the decision part on covering the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour in accordance with what is provided in the second paragraph of Article 250.54A of this Law.

(With amendments made by the laws of 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.60 Revocation or Replacement of Ensuring Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) Temporary protection against violence measures, except for the temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law, may be replaced with other measures upon a reasoned application of a party by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits.

(2) Temporary protection against violence measures may be revoked upon a reasoned application of a party by the same court that imposed the temporary protection against violence measures, or the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits.

(3) The application referred to in the first and second paragraphs of this Article shall be decided in a closed court session, with prior notification to the parties to the case. The court, at the request of one party, may hear each party in a separate court session. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to examination of the application.

(4) A decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure shall be executed immediately after its adoption.

(With amendments made by the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021. The amendment in the first paragraph enters into force on 01.07.2021. See transitional provision point 164)

Article 250.61 Appeal of Decisions Adopted on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of Article 250.60 of this Law, against a decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for revocation of temporary protection against violence has been rejected.

(2) Submission of an interlocutory appeal against the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article shall not suspend their execution.

(3) If the decisions referred to in the first paragraph of this Article have been adopted without the presence of a party to the case, the time limit for submission of an interlocutory appeal shall be counted from the date of issuance of the relevant decision.

Article 250.62 Notification of a Decision on Temporary Protection Against Violence

(1) The court shall notify the parties of a decision on temporary protection against violence, a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure by issuing it against signature or by sending it to the official electronic address, or in a registered mail item. A decision by which an application for temporary protection against violence has been rejected, unless it has been examined with the participation of the parties, shall be notified only to the claimant.

(2) The court shall send a decision on temporary protection against violence, a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure immediately after their adoption to the State Police for execution control to its indicated email address and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence.

(3) If a decision on the question of temporary protection against violence has been adopted upon an application submitted through police intermediation (Article 250.56), the decision shall be available to the potential respondent and potential claimant in the online system on the next day after the court has received the application and police information. This date shall be considered the date when the said decision is notified to the potential respondent, and failure to deliver the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. If, for technical reasons, it is not possible to attach the decision to the online system on the specified date, the decision shall be available at the court office on the same date. In such case, the date when the decision is available at the court office shall be considered the date of notification of the decision.

(4) If a temporary protection against violence measure referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent upon a reasoned application of the claimant submitted without police intermediation, the court shall not send the decision to the respondent. The court shall send this decision and the claimant's contact information referred to in the third paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law to the State Police in accordance with the second paragraph of this Article. The State Police, when commencing control of execution of this decision, shall familiarise the respondent with the decision. The date when the State Police has familiarised the respondent with the decision shall be considered the date when the decision is notified to the respondent, and failure to deliver the decision to the respondent does not affect its legal consequences. Only after notification of the decision shall the decision be available to the respondent in the online system.

(5) If it appears from the materials of the case on temporary protection against violence that the interests of a minor child or a person with limited legal capacity are affected, the court shall additionally send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure to the orphan's court and the social service at the child's or person's place of residence. In other cases, the court shall send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on replacement or revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure to the social service at the claimant's place of residence if the claimant has requested it.

(6) If the temporary protection against violence measure provided for in point 7.1 of the first paragraph of Article 250.47 of this Law has been applied to the respondent, the court shall, immediately after its adoption, additionally send a decision on temporary protection against violence or a decision on revocation of a temporary protection against violence measure also to the violent behaviour reduction service provider to its indicated email address. The information referred to in point 3 of the second paragraph of Article 250.46 of this Law shall also be sent to the service provider. The court shall also inform the service provider of the day when the decision was notified to the respondent, except in cases when the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article. If the decision is notified in accordance with the fourth paragraph of this Article, the State Police shall inform the service provider of the day when the decision was notified to the respondent.

(With amendments made by the laws of 23.04.2015, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.62A Conditions for Execution and Execution Control if the Respondent Has Been Imposed an Obligation to Complete a Social Rehabilitation Course for Reduction of Violent Behaviour

(1) The court or judge, upon receipt from the violent behaviour reduction service provider of a certificate that the respondent has not completed the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour within one year, shall send this certificate and the decision by which the respondent was imposed the obligation to complete the said course to the State Police for execution control to its indicated email address and also to the State Police structural unit at the claimant's place of residence, so that it may decide on the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the respondent for malicious non-execution of a decision on protection against violence.

(2) The court or judge, upon receipt from the violent behaviour reduction service provider of a certificate that the respondent has not covered the costs of this course by the completion of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, shall send a writ of execution to the bailiff at the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — at the debtor's place of residence.

(3) The decision part by which the respondent has been imposed an obligation to cover the costs of the social rehabilitation course for reduction of violent behaviour, if the respondent has not covered these costs voluntarily, shall be executed in the procedure established in Part E of this Law.

(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

Article 250.63 Special Conditions for the Respondent's Communication with the Court if the Respondent Has Been Applied a Prohibition to Return and Remain in the Dwelling That Is the Respondent's Declared Place of Residence

(1) If a temporary protection against violence measure has been applied that imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the claimant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return and remain therein, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, further decisions on temporary protection against violence, decisions on replacement or revocation of this temporary protection against violence measure shall be notified by the court to the respondent electronically in accordance with Article 56

(2) If a provisional protection measure against violence has been applied which imposes an obligation on the respondent to leave the dwelling in which the applicant permanently resides, and establishes a prohibition to return and stay therein, and this dwelling is the respondent's declared place of residence or additional address indicated in the declaration, and if the applicant has brought an action within the time limit specified in the court decision on provisional protection against violence, the summonses and other court documents related to this action shall be communicated to the respondent electronically in the manner prescribed in Article 56 of this Law, but if that is not possible, at the address indicated by him or her for communication with the court. (3) If in the cases referred to in paragraphs one and two of this Article it is not possible to communicate to the respondent electronically or the respondent has not indicated his or her address for communication with the court, the respondent shall be summoned to court and other court documents shall be delivered and issued by summoning the respondent with a summons which is published in accordance with Article 59. (With amendments made by the Law of 11 November 2021, which enters into force on 1 December 2021.)

Article 250.64. Requesting and Hearing of Cases on Provisional Protection Against Violence Following an Application Submitted Before Bringing an Action

(1) If the applicant brings an action within the time limit specified in the decision on provisional protection against violence following an application submitted before bringing an action, in a court having jurisdiction which is not the court that determined the provisional protection measure against violence, the court having jurisdiction to hear the case on the merits shall request from the court that determined the provisional protection measure against violence the relevant case and attach it to the materials of the action case. (2) When examining the statement of claim, the court or judge, in relation to provisional protection against violence, at the request of a party to the case or on its own initiative, shall request evidence or invite institutions to provide an opinion. (In the wording of the Law of 25 March 2021, which enters into force on 20 April 2021.)

## (Chapter 19

In the wording of the law of 10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.65 Article. Procedure for hearing cases

(1) Cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law shall be heard by the Economic Court in the procedure of claims according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) Cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law within the meaning of this chapter are cases related to such infringements of competition law as are defined in Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or in the legal acts of Latvia or a Member State of the European Union whose main objective is the same as that of Articles 101 and 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018 and 01.10.2020, which enters into force on 01.01.2021.)

250.66 Article. Disclosure of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court, upon a reasoned request of the parties to the case, which is substantiated by reasonably available information, in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law may order the disclosure of evidence, observing:

1) the extent to which the request or the respondent's objections to the request are substantiated by available information justifying the request to disclose evidence;

2) the status of the evidence and the costs of obtaining it, in particular in relation to persons who are not parties to the case;

3) whether the evidence that is requested to be disclosed contains information of limited accessibility, in particular concerning other persons who are not parties to the case, and the procedure provided for the protection of such information of limited accessibility.

(2) The person from whom evidence is requested to be disclosed has the right to notify the court in writing of the status of the information requested to be disclosed and the costs of submission, substantiating them.

(3) The court may reject a request for disclosure of evidence if it considers that the scope of the evidence requested to be disclosed or the costs associated with the disclosure of evidence are not proportionate to the amount of the claim brought.

(4) The court, observing the person's right to protection of information of limited accessibility, requires that the person whose information provided has been given the status of information of limited accessibility submit a derivative of the relevant written evidence without indicating the information of limited accessibility.

(5) The court may restrict the right of a party's authorised representative to examine such evidence in the case which contains information of limited accessibility but has been submitted in unredacted form, and the disclosure of such information may cause substantial harm to a party to the case or another person.

(6) The court, when ordering the disclosure of evidence that has been submitted to a competition authority or is in the case materials of a competition authority, shall assess whether the request indicates the evidence as precisely as possible, based on the information provided by the party, and whether the submission of the evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law.

(7) In order to assess whether the submission of evidence to the court will not create obstacles to the effective application of competition law, the court shall request the opinion of the competition authority. After evaluating the opinion of the competition authority, the court shall decide on the question of disclosure of evidence.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.67 Article. Restrictions on disclosure of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The court shall not order disclosure from the parties or other persons of:

1) statements provided to a competition authority within the framework of a leniency programme;

2) settlement submissions for the conclusion of an administrative agreement with a competition authority.

(2) The court shall order disclosure of evidence from the case materials of a competition authority if it is not possible to obtain such evidence from the parties to the case or other persons.

(3) Upon a substantiated request of the claimant, the court, in order to ascertain that the materials submitted to the Competition Council comply with the provisions of paragraph one of this Article, shall request an opinion from the Competition Council and the view of the person who submitted such materials to the Competition Council.

(4) Having received the opinions referred to in paragraph three of this Article, the court may verify the information indicated in the opinions by requesting the submission of the authority's case materials, which shall not be attached to the civil case.

(5) The court shall adopt a decision on the attachment of materials submitted to the Competition Council to the case materials if the requirements set out in paragraph one of this Article do not apply to the materials submitted by the competition authority.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017 with amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

250.68 Article. Admissibility of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) The evidence referred to in paragraph one of Article 250.67 of this law shall not be admissible if a person has obtained it by using access to the case materials of a competition authority.

(2) Information which a person has obtained by using access to the case materials of a competition authority may be used as evidence only by the said person or a person who is the successor to the rights and obligations of the said person.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.69 Article. Grounds for exemption from proving in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

(1) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of the Competition Council that has entered into force or by a court judgment that has entered into legal force shall not be proved anew when hearing a claim for compensation for damages brought in accordance with Article 101 or 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union or the Competition Law.

(2) An infringement of competition law established by a decision of a competition authority of another Member State that has entered into force shall be deemed to be proved unless a party to the case submits to the court evidence of the absence of an infringement of competition law.

(3) If one party refers to evidence that is in the possession of the other party, and the latter, following a request by the court, refuses to submit the relevant evidence to the court or has destroyed it without denying that this evidence is or has been in its possession, the court may recognise as proved those facts for the confirmation of which the opposing party has referred to this evidence.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

250.70 Article. Liability for failure to submit, destruction or unauthorised use of evidence in cases concerning compensation for damages for infringements of competition law

If the court does not establish objective circumstances for the failure to submit evidence or a person has violated the restrictions on admissibility of evidence specified in Article 250.68 of this law, or the court has established that evidence has been destroyed, the court may impose a fine on a natural person of up to 14,000 euros, but on a legal person — up to 140,000 euros.
(In the wording of the law of 19.10.2017, which enters into force on 01.11.2017.)

## (Chapter 31

Wording of 05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision 144)

250.71 Article. Jurisdiction and procedure for examination

(1) Cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court in which the relevant insolvency proceedings have been declared, in the case provided for in the fourth part of Article 363.17 of this law and in the first part of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law. Cases shall be examined in claim proceedings according to general provisions, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.

(2) Cases concerning disputes about rights in insolvency proceedings within the meaning of this chapter shall also include cases concerning creditor claims in accordance with the provisions of the second and third parts of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(3) If a case for examination of a dispute about rights has been initiated before the commencement of insolvency proceedings in court and the examination of this case on the merits has not been commenced, the court shall transfer this case for examination to the court in which the relevant insolvency proceedings have been declared, if there is no procedural co-participation on the defendant's side among the parties to the case.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.72 Article. Content of statement of claim

In the statement of claim, in addition to that provided for in Article 128 of this law, the following shall be indicated:

1) an address in Latvia for communication with the court in order to receive court documents, if the plaintiff's place of residence or location is not in Latvia and the plaintiff has not consented to electronic communication with the court;

2) whether the plaintiff requests trial of the case in a court session, substantiating their request.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.73 Article. Leaving statement of claim without progress

(1) The court shall leave the statement of claim without progress if:

1) the statement of claim does not contain all the requisites provided for in the second or third part of Article 128 and in Article 250.72 of this law;

2) the documents provided for in Article 129 of this law are not attached to the statement of claim.

(2) On leaving the statement of claim without progress, the judge shall adopt a reasoned decision, send it to the plaintiff and set a time limit of up to 20 days for remedying deficiencies, counting from the day of sending the decision. The judge's decision may be appealed in the procedure provided for in this law. The appeal time limit shall be counted from the day when the decision is issued to the plaintiff.

(3) If the plaintiff remedies the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be considered as submitted on the day when it was first submitted to the court.

(4) If the plaintiff does not remedy the deficiencies within the set time limit, the statement of claim shall be considered as not submitted and shall be returned to the plaintiff. The decision on returning the statement of claim to the plaintiff is not subject to appeal.

(5) The return of the statement of claim to the plaintiff is an obstacle to its repeated submission to the court.

(6) The court, simultaneously with the decision on returning the statement of claim to the plaintiff, shall adopt a decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case and shall revoke the interim protection measure.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.74 Article. Grounds for establishing interim protection and applicable measures in insolvency proceedings

(1) The court, upon a reasoned application by the complainant, may adopt a decision on establishing an interim protection measure if there is reason to believe that the administrator's decision could violate the creditor's rights provided for in the Insolvency Law. The establishment of an interim protection measure is permissible when examining the question of accepting a complaint about the administrator's decision in the cases provided for in parts 1.1 and four of Article 363.17 of this law, if the administrator's decision has been appealed by the person provided for in the second or third part of Article 80 of the Insolvency Law.

(2) The court, when examining the question of establishing an interim protection measure, in addition to the circumstances indicated in the complaint about the administrator's decision, shall also take into account other materials of the insolvency proceedings case.

(3) The application for establishing an interim protection measure shall indicate the interim protection measure which the court is requested to establish until the judgment is made.

(4) The complainant has the right to request the court to establish the following interim protection measures:

1) a prohibition to participate in the creditors' meeting with voting rights for the creditor whose recognised claim is the subject of the complaint;

2) a prohibition to submit objections regarding the information received under the first and second parts of Article 81 of the Insolvency Law for the creditor whose recognised claim is the subject of the complaint.

(5) The court shall decide on the application for establishing an interim protection measure no later than the next day after the complaint about the administrator's decision has been received, without prior notice to the administrator and creditors.

(6) The administrator is responsible for observing the prohibition on performing certain actions from the moment when this decision is communicated to them. The court shall notify the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register about the application of the interim protection measure.

(7) The court, upon a reasoned application by the complainant or interested person, may replace the established interim protection measure with another interim protection measure.

(8) The court, upon a reasoned application by an interested person, may revoke the interim protection measure.

(9) If an interim protection measure has been established but a claim for examination of a dispute about rights has not been brought and the court has not set a time limit for bringing the claim, then, when adopting a decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case, the court shall simultaneously revoke the interim protection measure.

(10) If an interim protection measure has been established before bringing a claim for examination of a dispute about rights and the claim has not been brought within the time limit set by the court, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(11) When rejecting a claim for examination of a dispute about rights, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(12) If a claim for examination of a dispute about rights has been left without examination or the proceedings have been terminated, the court shall simultaneously decide on the complaint about the administrator's decision and revoke the interim protection measure. The interim protection measure shall be in force until the day when the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case enters into legal force.

(13) A separate complaint may not be submitted against a decision by which an interim protection measure has been established, replaced or revoked.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.75 Article. Examination of case in written proceedings and drafting of judgment

(1) The examination of the case in written proceedings shall be commenced no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission, timely notifying the parties to the case of the date when the judgment will be available in the online system. The court shall inform about the composition of the court that will examine the case and shall explain the right to challenge the judge. The date when the judgment is available in the online system shall be considered as the date of drafting the judgment. If, for technical reasons, it is not possible to attach the judgment to the online system on the date of drafting the judgment, the judgment on the same date shall be available at the court office. In such case, the date when the judgment is available at the court office shall be considered as the date of drafting the judgment.

(2) Upon a written request by a party to the case, the judgment shall be sent immediately after the date of drafting the judgment. Receipt of the judgment does not affect the calculation of the time limit.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

250.76 Article. Trial of case in court session

(1) The court shall try the case in a court session if a reasoned request by a party to the case has been received and if the court considers it necessary to try the case in a court session.

(2) The court shall set the date of the court session no later than within 30 days after receipt of the explanation or expiry of the time limit for its submission.

(3) If the court postpones the examination of the case, the next court session date shall be set no later than within 15 days, except in cases where there is an objective ground for a longer time limit.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law, which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

250.77 Article. Appeal of judgment, entry into force and entry into force of decision on examination of complaint

(1) The parties to the case may appeal the court judgment in appeal proceedings if one of the grounds for initiating appeal proceedings provided for in Article 440.2 of this law exists.

(2) The judgment shall enter into force after the time limit for submitting an appeal has expired.

(3) If the judgment has been appealed and the appellate court refuses to initiate appeal proceedings, the judgment of the first instance court and the decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision shall enter into force simultaneously with the decision by which initiation of appeal proceedings has been refused.

(4) The court decision on the complaint about the administrator's decision in the case provided for in the fourth part of Article 363.17 of this law shall enter into force if an appeal has not been submitted within the time limit provided for by law.

(5) After the entry into force of the decisions referred to in this Article, they shall also be sent to the administrator and the Insolvency Control Service.
(Wording of 31.05.2018. law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which comes into force on 01.12.2021.)

## (Chapter 28

02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.78 Procedure for Examining Cases

Cases concerning unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure of trade secrets that has occurred or is reliably possible in the future (hereinafter – infringement) shall be examined by a court in claim proceedings according to general rules, observing the exceptions provided for in this chapter.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.79 Protection of Information Containing Trade Secrets

(1)	If the court, upon a reasoned request of a party, recognises that the case contains a document containing trade secrets that has been submitted in non-redacted form, and the disclosure of this information may cause substantial harm to a participant in the case or another person, the court may restrict the right of a person participating in the examination of the case to become acquainted with this part of the case materials by including the relevant evidence in a separate volume.  

(2)	The court, observing a person's right to protection of trade secrets, requests that the person whose information provided has the status of a trade secret submit a derivative of the relevant written evidence without indicating information containing trade secrets or by submitting it in redacted form.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.80 Basis for Application of Provisional Protection Measure and General Rules

(1)	The court, upon a reasoned application of the claimant, may adopt a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure if there is a basis to consider that:

1)	a trade secret exists and the claimant is its holder;  

2)	the right to protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure is being infringed or could be infringed.  

(2)	The court, when deciding on the satisfaction or rejection of the application or assessing the proportionality of the application of a provisional protection measure, takes into account what is provided for in Article 250.88 of this law.  

(3)	It is permissible to examine the question of the application of a provisional protection measure at any stage of the proceedings, as well as before bringing a claim to court.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.81 Provisional Protection Measures

(1)	The application for the application of a provisional protection measure shall indicate the relevant provisional protection measure.  

(2)	Provisional protection measures are:

1)	a prohibition on the respondent or a specific person who makes the commission of an infringement possible from using or disclosing a trade secret, producing, offering, placing on the market or using infringing goods for the said purposes;  

2)	seizure of movable property with which rights to protection of a trade secret against unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure are possibly being infringed.  

(3)	The court, when deciding on an application that is not related to the disclosure of a trade secret, may not apply the provisional protection measures provided for in paragraph two of this Article, but impose on the respondent an obligation to pay a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or submit an equivalent guarantee to the court in order to ensure compensation to the trade secret holder.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.82 Application of Provisional Protection Measure Before Bringing a Claim

(1)	A potential claimant may request that a provisional protection measure be applied before bringing a claim within three months from the day when he or she learned or should have learned of the infringement of rights or a possible infringement.  

(2)	When submitting an application, the potential claimant shall provide evidence confirming the infringement of rights or a possible infringement.  

(3)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim shall be submitted to the court in which the claim is to be brought.  

(4)	When satisfying an application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim, the judge shall set a time limit for the claimant to submit a claim application to the court, not longer than 30 days.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.83 Examination of the Question of Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure before bringing a claim, as well as in cases where it is not possible to determine who will be the participants in the case, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of receipt of the application, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the participants in the case. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of its receipt, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  

(2)	An application for the application of a provisional protection measure, if the application is submitted simultaneously with the bringing of a claim, shall be decided by the court or judge within 10 days of the initiation of the case, without holding a court session and without prior notice to the participants in the case, or within 10 days of receipt of the application if the case has already been initiated. If the judge considers it necessary to clarify additional circumstances, the application shall be decided within 15 days of the initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, within 15 days of its receipt, inviting the applicant and potential participants in the case to a court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  

(3)	If delay could cause irreversible harm to the trade secret holder and if it is not necessary to request additional evidence, the judge shall decide the application for the application of a provisional protection measure no later than the next day after the initiation of the case or, if the case has already been initiated, no later than the next day after receipt of the application, without prior notice to the respondent and other participants in the case.  

(4)	If a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure has been adopted without the presence of the respondent or other participants in the case, the court shall notify the respondent and other participants in the case of this decision no earlier than the third day after the adoption of the decision.  

(5)	When satisfying an application for the application of a provisional protection measure, the court or judge may instruct the claimant to secure losses that could arise for the respondent or other persons mentioned in point 1 of paragraph two of Article 250.81 of this law in connection with the application of a provisional protection measure, by paying a specified sum of money into the deposit account of a bailiff or submitting an equivalent guarantee to the court. If the claimant has not fulfilled the imposed obligation or has not submitted to the court a certificate issued by a bailiff confirming the payment of the sum of money into his or her deposit account within the time limit set by the court or judge, the court or judge shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the provisional protection measure. The decision on securing losses shall be notified to the respondent after the claimant has paid the sum of money determined by the court or judge into the deposit account of the bailiff.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.84 Replacement or Cancellation of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	The court, upon an application of the claimant, may replace the determined provisional protection measure with another measure.  

(2)	A provisional protection measure may be cancelled by the same court upon an application of a participant in the case.  

(3)	The court, upon receipt of an application from the claimant, another potential participant in the case or a person to whom the applied provisional protection measure relates, shall adopt a decision on the cancellation of the provisional protection measure if:

1)	a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure was adopted before bringing a claim and the claim has not been brought within the time limit set by the court;  

2)	the relevant information that was considered a trade secret no longer meets the requirements for a trade secret provided for in the Trade Secret Protection Law for reasons that cannot be associated with the respondent.  

(4)	When rejecting a claim, the court shall cancel the provisional protection measure in the judgment. The provisional protection measure is in force until the day the judgment enters into legal force.  

(5)	If a claim is left without examination or proceedings are terminated, the court shall cancel the provisional protection measure in the decision. The provisional protection measure is in force until the day the decision enters into legal force.  

(6)	The applications mentioned in paragraphs one, two and three of this Article shall be decided in a court session, with prior notice to the participants in the case. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the application.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.85 Appeal of Decisions Adopted Regarding Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	A separate complaint may be submitted against a decision by which the determined provisional protection measure has been replaced, a decision by which an application for the application of a provisional protection measure has been rejected, and a decision by which an application for the cancellation of a provisional protection measure has been rejected.  

(2)	If a decision on the application of a provisional protection measure has been adopted without the presence of a participant in the case, the time limit for submitting a separate complaint shall be counted from the day of issuance of the decision.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.86 Execution of Decision on Application of Provisional Protection Measure

(1)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure and a decision on the cancellation of a provisional protection measure shall be executed immediately after its adoption.  

(2)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure that has been adopted with the condition mentioned in paragraph five of Article 250.83 of this law shall be executed after the claimant has paid the sum of money determined by the court or judge into the deposit account of the bailiff or submitted an equivalent guarantee to the court. The writ of execution shall be issued after the payment of the sum of money determined by the court or receipt of the equivalent guarantee.  

(3)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure by seizing movable property with which an infringement has possibly been committed shall be executed in the procedure provided for in Chapter 71 of this law.  

(4)	A decision on the application of a provisional protection measure by establishing a prohibition on performing specific actions with which an infringement has possibly been committed shall be executed by a bailiff and notified of the court decision to the respondent or the relevant third party in the procedure provided for in Article 555 of this law.  

(5)	The cancellation of an applied provisional protection measure shall be executed pursuant to an order of the bailiff who executed the decision on the application of the provisional protection measure.  

(6)	A decision on the replacement of a provisional protection measure shall be executed by a bailiff, first applying the replacement provisional protection measure and then cancelling the replaced provisional protection measure.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 250.87 Compensation for Harm Caused by Provisional Protection Measure

The respondent is entitled to claim compensation for harm caused to him or her in connection with the determination of a provisional protection measure if the provisional protection measure has been cancelled in the case provided for in point 1 of paragraph three of Article 250.84 of this law, if the claim brought against him or her has been rejected, left without examination or proceedings have been terminated in the cases provided for in points 2 and 4 of Article 223 of this law.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)

Article 250.88 General Rules for Examination of Claim Application and Application of Legal Protection Measures

The court, when deciding on the full or partial satisfaction of a claim or on its full or partial rejection or assessing the proportionality of the application of a legal protection measure, takes into account the circumstances of the relevant case, including where possible:

1)	the value of the trade secret or other specific characteristics of the trade secret;  

2)	the measures taken to protect the trade secret;  

3)	the respondent's conduct in acquiring, using or disclosing the trade secret;  

4)	the consequences of the unlawful use or disclosure of the trade secret;  

5)	the legitimate interests of the parties and the impact of the application of a provisional protection measure on them;  

6)	the legitimate interests of third parties and society;  

7)	the protection of fundamental rights.  
(28.02.2019. version of the law, which enters into force 01.04.2019.)
