## (Chapter 30

In the wording of the 09.2010 law, which enters into force on 01.11.2010.)

Article 363.1 Jurisdiction over Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a legal entity insolvency proceedings case in accordance with an application by the debtor, a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, based on the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (2) A case concerning the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be examined by the court based on the location of the debtor's centre of main interests, but in the case of initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation — based on the location of the debtor's establishment (within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council). (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

Article 363.2 Content of a Creditor's or Majority of Creditors' Application for Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) A creditor shall indicate in an application for legal entity insolvency proceedings (hereinafter in this Chapter — insolvency proceedings application):

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 2) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 3) the sign of insolvency proceedings; 4) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (11) If the application is submitted by several creditors or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law, the information referred to in point 1.1 of the first paragraph of Article 254 of this Law shall be indicated for each creditor on whose authority the insolvency proceedings application is submitted. (2) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application, the creditor shall attach a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (3) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 1 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the substantiation and amount of the claim shall be attached to the application, as well as a document issued by a bailiff regarding the impossibility of recovering the debt from the debtor. (4) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, evidence of the substantiation and amount of the claim, a copy of the warning of the intention to submit an insolvency proceedings application, documents regarding the issuance or sending of the warning (receipt for sending a document with confirmation of the content of the shipment) shall be attached to the application, and the application shall also certify that the debtor has not raised substantiated objections against it. (5) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 4 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, the application shall indicate for what period wages and compensation for harm have not been paid, and a certificate issued by the employer regarding the amount of wages and mandatory social insurance contributions shall be attached to it, but if the employer has not issued the said certificate, this fact shall be indicated in the application. (51) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application in accordance with the sign referred to in point 7 or 8 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law, the application shall, in addition to the information referred to in the first paragraph of this Article, indicate the case number for legal protection proceedings. Documents substantiating the facts stated in the application shall be attached to the application. (6) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application that insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) or (2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor, the creditor shall indicate the substantiation of the application therein and attach evidence confirming the circumstances on which the application is based, if such evidence is in his or her possession. (7) When submitting an insolvency proceedings application that insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor, the creditor shall send it to the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of the said Regulation. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021. The provision of the second paragraph regarding the payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit, insofar as it relates to employees whose only legal remedy is the declaration of the employer as insolvent, has been found to be incompatible with the first sentence of Article 92 of the Constitution of the Republic of Latvia by the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 20.04.2012, which enters into force on 24.04.2012.)

Article 363.3 Content of a Debtor's Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) An insolvency proceedings application on behalf of the debtor may be submitted by the management institution or partners of a general partnership who have representation rights, or a specially authorised person. (2) The debtor shall indicate in the insolvency proceedings application:

1) (deleted by the law of 11.11.2021); 2) the sign of insolvency proceedings; 3) information about the location of the debtor's centre of main interests within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) whether the debtor conducts or has conducted in another European Union Member State within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and its location; 5) the case number for legal protection proceedings, if the insolvency proceedings application is submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 9 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law; 6) the debtor's legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court. (3) The debtor shall attach to the insolvency proceedings application:

1) a list of members of management institutions, auditors (members of audit institutions) and procurators, indicating the name, surname, address and other information by which they can be identified and reached; 2) evidence that the intention to submit an insolvency proceedings application has been notified to the members (shareholders) of the commercial company, members of the association or other founders or members of the legal entity; 3) evidence of representation rights; 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (4) When submitting an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor shall, in addition to the documents specified in the third paragraph of this Article, attach to the insolvency proceedings application a certification regarding the location of the debtor's centre of main interests. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 18.04.2013, 08.12.2016, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.4 Content of a Debtor's Insolvency Proceedings Application in Liquidation Proceedings

(1) An insolvency proceedings application on behalf of the debtor shall be submitted by the liquidator in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in point 6 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law. (2) The provisions of the second, third and fourth paragraphs of Article 363.3 of this Law shall apply to the liquidator's insolvency proceedings application. (With amendments made by the law of 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017.)

Article 363.5 Content of an Insolvency Proceedings Application by a Person Referred to in Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council

(1) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall submit an insolvency proceedings application to the court to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor. (2) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall indicate in the insolvency proceedings application:

1) the debtor's firm (name), registration number and legal address that was registered for the debtor three months before the application was submitted to the court, and the legal address on the day of submission of the application; 2) the name of the court that has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, the date of adoption and entry into force of the court decision; 3) the substantiation for initiating insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor; 4) information on whether insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have been initiated against the debtor in another European Union Member State (hereinafter — Member State). (3) The person referred to in point (a) of Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall attach to the insolvency proceedings application:

1) the court decision on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor and a translation thereof certified in the prescribed manner in the official language; 2) the court decision or other certification regarding the appointment of an administrator in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and a translation thereof certified in the prescribed manner in the official language; 3) documents certifying that the debtor conducts or has conducted in Latvia within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) a document certifying payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit. (With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 08.12.2016, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.6 Content of an Administrator's Insolvency Proceedings Application
(Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017, which enters into force on 01.07.2017. See transitional provision point 125)

Article 363.7 Receipt and Registration of an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall accept an insolvency proceedings application from the debtor on whose behalf the application is submitted or from a person who is authorised to submit the application. An insolvency proceedings application shall be submitted in person in paper form or in an online system. (2) Upon receiving an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall verify the identity of the applicant. If it is not possible to verify the identity of the applicant of an application submitted in person in paper form or the applicant does not have the appropriate authorisation, the application shall not be accepted. (3) An insolvency proceedings application shall be registered in a separate register, which shall be signed by the applicant and the recipient. If an insolvency proceedings application is received in the online system, the entry in the register shall be made by the recipient. (With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.8 Prohibition on Amending the Subject Matter of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and on the Debtor Withdrawing an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) In insolvency proceedings cases, amendment of the subject matter of an insolvency proceedings application is not permitted. (2) The debtor is not entitled to withdraw an insolvency proceedings application. Article 363.9 Resolution of the Question of Acceptance of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and Initiation of a Case

(1) Within five days of receiving an insolvency proceedings application, the judge shall adopt a decision:

1) to leave the insolvency proceedings application without progress; 2) to refuse to accept the insolvency proceedings application; 3) to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case. (2) If an insolvency proceedings application is left without progress, the judge shall adopt a decision to accept the insolvency proceedings application and initiate a case no later than the next day after the deficiencies specified in the decision have been remedied. If the time limit for remedying the deficiencies specified in the decision has expired and they have not been remedied, the application shall be considered as not submitted and returned to the applicant. (3) The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application if it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application. (4) The court shall initiate a legal entity insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative if, when adopting a decision to terminate legal protection proceedings, it establishes the sign of legal entity insolvency proceedings specified in point 7 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law. (5) The judge shall adopt a decision to consolidate the initiated legal entity insolvency proceedings cases into one proceeding if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following another creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application. (6) The judge shall adopt a decision to suspend proceedings in a case following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, it is established that a legal entity insolvency proceedings case has been initiated against the debtor following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application. Upon declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings following the debtor's insolvency proceedings application, the court shall resume proceedings in the suspended case following the creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application and terminate it. The state fee paid shall be refunded to the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law in full. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 01.06.2017 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision point 179)

Article 363.10 Court Actions in Preparing a Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Case for Examination

(1) The judge shall immediately send the decision on the initiation of a case to:

1) (deleted by the law of 31.05.2018); 2) the Bank of Latvia, if the decision has been adopted regarding a financial market participant whose activities are supervised by the Bank of Latvia in accordance with the requirements of regulatory enactments; 3) the administrator of the proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if a case has been initiated in Latvia following an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) the debtor. (2) If a case has been initiated following a creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law insolvency proceedings application, the judge shall send the creditor's or the majority of creditors' specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law application and the decision on the initiation of the case to the debtor, inform the debtor and the creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law of the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, as well as of the debtor's right to raise substantiated objections against the claim stated in the insolvency proceedings application no later than three days before the day of examination of the insolvency proceedings application, including to provide evidence that the debtor is able to cover the obligations stated in the insolvency proceedings application. (3) After the initiation of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case, using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, an administrator candidate shall be selected from the list of administrator candidates (hereinafter — Candidate List) maintained in the Electronic Insolvency Accounting System of the Insolvency Control Service, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (4) Having established that there are restrictions for the administrator candidate to perform the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, a new administrator candidate shall be selected from the Candidate List, and the judge shall assess his or her suitability for performing the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023.)

Article 363.11 Procedure for Examination of an Insolvency Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall examine an insolvency proceedings application submitted by a creditor or the majority of creditors specified in the third paragraph of Article 42 of the Insolvency Law within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case. The applicant of the insolvency proceedings application and the debtor shall be invited to the court session. If several creditors' insolvency proceedings applications are consolidated into one proceeding, those applicants who can be notified of the court session at least seven days before the respective session shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (2) The court shall examine an insolvency proceedings application submitted by the debtor in written proceedings within seven days from the day of initiation of the case. The court shall examine the application in written proceedings, except in cases where it considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the debtor shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of this person is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (3) (Deleted by the law of 01.06.2017)

(31) If an application has been submitted for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the application shall be examined in written proceedings within 15 days from the day of initiation of the case or, if the court considers it necessary, in a court session. If the insolvency proceedings application is examined in a court session, the applicant, the debtor and the administrator of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be invited to the session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the case. (4) If, before the drafting of the judgment, the court establishes that the applicant has not paid the state fee or the insolvency proceedings deposit, except in cases where the court has initiated a legal entity insolvency proceedings case on its own initiative or has exempted an employee from payment of the deposit, it shall leave the insolvency proceedings application without examination. The exception specified in this paragraph does not apply to cases where a legal protection proceedings application has been submitted repeatedly within one year. (5) The judge may adopt a decision on full or partial exemption of an employee from payment of the insolvency proceedings deposit if he or she submits the insolvency proceedings application after it has not been possible to execute a court decision on the recovery of a debt from the debtor by applying enforcement measures and the employee, taking into account his or her financial situation, cannot pay the insolvency proceedings deposit. (6) When examining an application for the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall take into account the provisions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 01.06.2017 and 31.05.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018. See transitional provision point 146)

Article 363.12 Sequence of Examination of an Insolvency Proceedings Application and a Legal Protection Proceedings Application

(1) The court shall suspend proceedings if, before the commencement of the examination on the merits of a legal entity insolvency proceedings case, it establishes that a legal protection proceedings case has been initiated in respect of the debtor. (2) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be suspended until a decision is adopted in the legal protection proceedings case. (3) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be terminated if, in accordance with the decision, legal protection proceedings are implemented in respect of the debtor. (4) Proceedings in a legal entity insolvency proceedings case shall be resumed and examined in the procedure specified in this Chapter if legal protection proceedings in respect of the debtor are terminated on the basis of the second paragraph of Article 341.10 of this Law. Article 363.13 Court Decision in a Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings Case

(1) Legal entity insolvency proceedings shall be declared by the court, and its judgment is not subject to appeal, except for a judgment by which an insolvency proceedings application for a legal entity has been rejected. A judgment by which an insolvency proceedings application for a legal entity has been rejected may be appealed in the appellate procedure if one of the grounds for initiating appellate proceedings specified in Article 440.2 of this Law exists. (2) The court shall declare legal entity insolvency proceedings if, on the day of examination of the application, it establishes the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated in the application. (3) Upon granting the application, the court shall appoint the administrator candidate selected in the procedure specified in Article 363.10 of this Law as administrator. (4) When declaring insolvency proceedings in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court shall indicate in the judgment the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated, or indicate in the decision referred to in the fifth paragraph of this Article the type of insolvency proceedings if insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council are initiated. (5) If the court establishes that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia, it shall declare a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and adopt a decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Against the court decision establishing that the debtor's centre of main interests is located in Latvia and Latvia has jurisdiction to initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the debtor or any creditor may submit an appeal in accordance with Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council within 30 days from the day of pronouncement of the decision. The submission of an appeal does not suspend the initiation of insolvency proceedings. (6) The court shall initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the debtor conducts or has conducted in Latvia within a three-month period before the submission of the application an establishment within the meaning of Article 2(10) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. Having established that the court of another Member State that has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor was entitled to initiate such proceedings, the court shall render a judgment on the initiation of insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council against the debtor, without observing the provisions of the second paragraph of this Article. The court shall not initiate insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council if it establishes that the conditions of Article 38 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council have occurred. (7) The court, when declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings and terminating legal protection proceedings, shall appoint the administrator candidate selected in the procedure specified in Article 363.10 of this Law as administrator. (8) When declaring legal entity insolvency proceedings, the court shall send the judgment to the appointed administrator, the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, if it has initiated insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation against the debtor in Latvia, and to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (9) If the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated in the application is not established, the court shall reject the insolvency proceedings application and terminate the legal entity insolvency proceedings case, and also decide the question of whether the insolvency proceedings application is to be recognised as unfounded or deliberately false. The court shall reject an insolvency proceedings application submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law if it establishes that no later than three days before the day of examination of the case the debtor has raised substantiated objections against the claim stated in the insolvency proceedings application or that the obligations for which the insolvency proceedings application was submitted have been covered in full. (10) Having recognised the insolvency proceedings application as unfounded or deliberately false, the court shall recover litigation costs from the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application. If the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application withdraws his or her application because the debtor has voluntarily covered the obligations stated in the insolvency proceedings application before the day of examination of the case, the court, when deciding on the termination of the case, shall, at the request of the applicant of the insolvency proceedings application, award the court costs paid by the applicant from the debtor. In other cases, these costs shall be indicated in the court judgment and included in the insolvency proceedings costs. (11) When rejecting an insolvency proceedings application submitted in accordance with the sign of insolvency proceedings referred to in points 2 and 3 of the first paragraph of Article 57 of the Insolvency Law because on the day of examination of the application the court does not establish the sign of insolvency proceedings indicated therein, as the debtor has covered part of the obligations indicated in the application before the day of examination of the case in order to prevent the declaration of legal entity insolvency proceedings, it shall, when deciding on the termination of the case, award the court costs paid by the applicant from the debtor. (12) When rejecting an insolvency proceedings application, the court shall send the judgment to the Insolvency Control Service. (With amendments made by the laws of 18.04.2013, 12.02.2015, 01.06.2017, 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Article 363.14 Questions to be Decided by the Court After Declaration of Legal Entity Insolvency Proceedings

(1) After the declaration of the debtor's insolvency proceedings, the court shall, on the basis of a relevant application, decide on:

1) the removal of an administrator in the cases specified in the Insolvency Law, setting a time limit for the preparation of a document and property acceptance and transfer act and the transfer of documents and property to another administrator; 2) the appointment of a new administrator candidate as administrator if the previous administrator has been removed from the respective insolvency proceedings; 3) the performance of actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council; 4) the approval of an immovable property or enterprise auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and the registration of the sold immovable property in the name of the purchaser, as well as the deletion of the insolvency note in the land register; 5) (deleted by the law of 11.09.2014); 6) the termination of insolvency proceedings. (2) An administrator may be removed by the court on its own initiative if, when examining an application or complaint in an insolvency proceedings case, it establishes that the administrator does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments or does not execute a court decision. (3) If, after the declaration of insolvency proceedings, the court has adopted a decision to remove an administrator, after its adoption the court shall appoint an administrator candidate selected from the Candidate List using automated selection provided by the Court Information System as administrator. (4) (Deleted by the law of 31.05.2018)

(5) Having established that there are restrictions for the administrator candidate to perform the duties of an administrator in the respective legal entity insolvency proceedings, the judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. The judge shall adopt a decision to appoint an administrator candidate as administrator in the procedure specified in the third paragraph of this Article. (6) If, following an application by the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the court establishes that the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of this Regulation No 2015/848 is in the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of this Regulation, it shall adopt a decision on the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council and determine appropriate measures to ensure the interests of the creditors of the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation. (7) If, following an application by the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of this Regulation or a creditor, the court establishes that the performance of actions specified in Article 46(1) of the said Regulation No 2015/848 is no longer justified, it shall adopt a decision on the performance of the action specified in Article 46(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council. (8) The court shall send the decision on the performance of actions specified in Article 46 of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council to the debtor's representative and the administrator. (9) The court shall send the decisions referred to in points 1, 2, 3 and 6 of the first paragraph of this Article to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register. (10) The court shall examine a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, a complaint against an administrator's decision, as well as a complaint against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding the actions of an administrator in insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation. The court shall send the decision adopted after the examination of the said complaints, except for a decision on a complaint against a creditors' meeting decision, to the Insolvency Control Service. (11) The court shall examine an application and a complaint within 15 days from the day of receipt of the application or complaint. The judge shall examine an application in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where he or she considers it necessary to examine the case in a court session. The judge shall examine a complaint in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where the administrator requests that the case be examined in a court session or the court considers it necessary to examine the complaint in a court session. The applicant or complainant, the administrator, the debtor's representative and other interested persons shall be invited to the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the question. (12) A court decision on the examination of an application or complaint is not subject to appeal. A court decision on the removal of an administrator on the basis of point 1, 2, 3, 4 or 7 of the second paragraph of Article 22 of the Insolvency Law is subject to appeal in the part regarding the established non-compliance with the requirements of regulatory enactments or non-execution of a court decision, by submitting an appeal. The regional court shall examine this appeal within 15 days. (121) An appeal may be submitted against a court decision in a case on the approval of an auction act. (13) For the examination of the questions referred to in this Article, the court may request that the administrator submit a report on his or her activities or other information, but the administrator involved in the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council — information necessary for the adoption of the decisions referred to in this Article. (14) The regional court, when examining the appeal referred to in the twelfth paragraph of this Article, has the right to:

1) leave the decision unchanged and reject the complaint; 2) revoke the decision and decide the question on the merits with its own decision. (15) The decision referred to in the fourteenth paragraph of this Article shall enter into force and be enforceable immediately. (16) The regional court shall send the decisions referred to in the fourteenth paragraph of this Article to the Insolvency Control Service.

363.15 pants. Lēmums par mantas pārdošanas akta apstiprināšanu maksātnespējas procesā

(1)	Ja administrators pārdevis nekustamo īpašumu vai uzņēmumu izsoles ceļā, izsoles aktu iesniedz tiesā apstiprināšanai pēc tam, kad nosolītājs samaksājis visu no viņa pienākošos summu. Administrators pieteikumā norāda ziņas par lietā veiktajām darbībām, kas saistītas ar īpašuma pārdošanu, pievienojot to apliecinošus dokumentus, kā arī dokumentus, kas apstiprina, ka tiesas izdevumi par minētā pieteikuma iesniegšanu tiesā ir samaksāti. (2)	Tiesa apstiprina izsoles aktu saskaņā ar šā likuma noteikumiem par nekustamā īpašuma izsoli (izņemot šā likuma 613.panta trešajā un devītajā daļā noteikto). Section 363.15 Decision on Approval of the Act of Sale of Property in Insolvency Proceedings

(1) If the administrator has sold immovable property or an enterprise by auction, the auction act shall be submitted to the court for approval after the successful bidder has paid the entire amount due from him or her. (2) The court shall approve the auction act in accordance with the provisions of this Law on the auction of immovable property (except as provided for in Paragraphs three and nine of Section 613 of this Law). (3) The actions specified in this Section shall be performed by the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency

proceedings case is located. (4) No later than within three days from the day when the court decision on approval of the auction act has entered into force, the administrator shall pay the state and chancellery fee referred to in Section 611, Paragraph two, Point 4 of this Law into the state budget and notify the acquirer and the district (city) court thereof. (1) After declaration of a legal person's insolvency proceedings, an application for legal protection proceedings in out-of-court legal protection proceedings shall be submitted to the court in whose proceedings the legal person's insolvency proceedings case is located. Section 363.17 Examination in Court of Complaints Against Administrator's Decision in Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative or third party whose lawful rights have been infringed against an administrator's decision or auction calculation in a legal person's insolvency proceedings in the cases specified in the Insolvency Law. (11) If there is reason to believe that the rights of the complainant may be infringed, the complainant shall have the right, simultaneously with the submission of a complaint against the administrator's decision, to request the court to impose interim protection measures in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law. (2) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and instruct the administrator to remedy the violation committed. (3) If the court finds that the appealed administrator's decision or auction calculation complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint. (4) If, when examining a complaint against an administrator's decision, the court finds that there is a dispute over rights, it shall set a time limit, not longer than one month, within which the complainant may bring an action in the procedure specified in Chapter 30.7 of this Law. Section 363.18 Examination in Court of Complaints Against Creditors' Meeting Decision in Legal Person's Insolvency Proceedings

(1) A complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative or administrator against a creditors' meeting decision in a legal person's insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court. (2) Having found the appealed creditors' meeting decision to be non-compliant with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall revoke it. (3) When revoking a creditors' meeting decision on non-approval of insolvency proceedings expenses, non-approval of administrator's remuneration or refusal to extend the term of insolvency proceedings, the court may simultaneously decide on approval of insolvency proceedings costs, approval of administrator's remuneration or extension of the term of insolvency proceedings. (4) Having found that the appealed creditors' meeting decision complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, the court shall reject the complaint. (5) The complainant shall have the right to withdraw the complaint before the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision to terminate the complaint proceedings. (1) Courts shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor's representative, administrator or third party whose lawful rights have been infringed against a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service regarding administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or imposition of a legal obligation and regarding deposit payment. 363.34 Article. Examination in Court of Complaints Regarding a Decision Adopted by the Insolvency Control Service Concerning the Administrator's Actions in Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings or the Imposition of a Legal Obligation

(1) The court shall examine a complaint by a creditor, debtor, administrator, or third person whose legal rights have been infringed, regarding a decision adopted by the Insolvency Control Service concerning the administrator's actions in insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation. A complaint regarding a decision of the Insolvency Control Service that has been adopted after the termination of the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings shall be examined by the court in the procedure specified in this Article.

(2) If the court finds that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service does not comply with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall grant the complaint and decide on:

1) revocation of the decision of the Insolvency Control Service in whole or in part;

2) imposition of an obligation on the Insolvency Control Service to adopt or examine a complaint regarding the administrator's actions;

3) imposition of an obligation on the administrator to remedy the committed violation, except in cases where the natural person insolvency proceedings have been terminated.

(3) If the court establishes that the appealed decision of the Insolvency Control Service complies with the requirements of regulatory enactments, it shall reject the complaint.

(4) The complainant has the right to withdraw his or her complaint until the completion of its examination on the merits. If the complainant withdraws the submitted complaint, the court shall adopt a decision on termination of the complaint proceedings.

(5) The court shall immediately send the adopted decision to the Insolvency Control Service after examination of the complaint.

(6) If a decision of the Insolvency Control Service regarding the administrator's actions in natural person insolvency proceedings or the imposition of a legal obligation has been adopted within one year after the termination of the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, the complaint regarding the decision of the Insolvency Control Service shall be submitted to the court in whose jurisdiction the relevant case concerning the natural person insolvency proceedings was located.

(With amendments made by the laws of 31.05.2018 and 11.11.2021, which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

363.35 Article. Termination of Debt Discharge Procedure

(1) The court shall examine the issue of termination of the debt discharge procedure upon application by the debtor or administrator.

(2) The court shall approve the termination of the debt discharge procedure if it establishes that the debtor has fulfilled the debt discharge plan and no objections have been received from creditors and the debtor, or the objections received are to be considered unfounded.

(3) Upon approving the termination of the debt discharge procedure, the court shall decide on the discharge of obligations that have not been fulfilled during the debt discharge process.

(4) The debtor, creditor, or administrator shall attach to the application for termination of the debt discharge procedure evidence confirming the circumstances indicated in the application.

(5) Upon approving the termination of the debt discharge procedure, the court shall simultaneously adopt a decision on termination of the insolvency proceedings.

363.36 Article. Termination of Natural Person Insolvency Proceedings

(1) The court shall adopt a decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings if:

1) after approval of the completion of bankruptcy procedure, the debt discharge procedure is not applied to the debtor;

2) the debtor has settled all his or her obligations;

3) it establishes restrictions on the application of natural person insolvency proceedings;

4) it establishes restrictions on the application of debt discharge procedure;

5) the debtor fails to fulfil the debt discharge plan;

6) the debt discharge plan has been fulfilled;

7) during the bankruptcy procedure, creditors' claims have not been submitted in accordance with the time limits specified in the Insolvency Law, simultaneously also terminating the bankruptcy procedure;

8) legal protection proceedings have been declared for the debtor's individual merchant, individual (family) enterprise, farm, or fishery in out-of-court legal protection proceedings, simultaneously terminating the natural person insolvency proceedings.

(2) If the court, upon terminating the debt discharge procedure, establishes that the debtor is to be released from debt obligations in accordance with Article 164 of the Insolvency Law, it shall simultaneously with the termination of the procedure release him or her from the obligations specified in the natural person debt discharge plan.

(21) The court, upon application by the administrator of the procedure specified in Article 3(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, submitted in accordance with Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may terminate the insolvency proceedings specified in Article 3(2) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council.

(3) The court shall immediately send the decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register.

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.02.2015, 31.05.2018, 11.11.2021, and 16.03.2023, which enter into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

363.37 Article. Application for Revocation of Debtor's Release from Obligations and Its Acceptance

(1) The debtor, creditor, or other person whose legal rights have been infringed has the right to submit an application for revocation of the debtor's release from obligations within the time limit and in the cases specified in Article 165.1 of the Insolvency Law.

(2) If the applicant is not the debtor, the application shall be sent to the debtor, setting a time limit for submission of an explanation, not exceeding 30 days. The application shall be sent to the administrator who was appointed in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings, setting a time limit for submission of an opinion, not exceeding 30 days.

(3) Acceptance of the application shall not suspend the effect of the court decision on termination of natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision refusing to accept the application.

(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

363.38 Article. Examination of Application for Revocation of Debtor's Release from Obligations and Court Decision

(1) The application shall be examined in written proceedings without holding a court session, except in cases where the court considers it necessary to examine the application in a court session or a party to the case so requests, substantiating his or her request.

(2) The court shall grant the application if it establishes that there exists a basis specified in the second or third paragraph of Article 165.1 of the Insolvency Law for revoking the debtor's release from obligations.

(3) If the court grants the application, it shall send the decision to the responsible institution that makes entries in the insolvency register and to the administrator who was appointed in the relevant natural person insolvency proceedings.

(4) The applicant may submit an appeal against the court decision rejecting the application.

(In the wording of the law of 16.03.2023, which enters into force on 29.03.2023. See transitional provision 179)

### 374. pants

Judge's actions in preparing a credit institution insolvency case for hearing

(1)	After initiation of a credit institution insolvency proceedings case, an administrator candidate is selected from the List of Candidates using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, and the judge evaluates his or her suitability for performing the administrator's duties in the respective credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(11) Having established that there are restrictions on the administrator candidate's performance of administrator duties in the specific credit institution insolvency proceedings, the judge adopts a decision to refuse to appoint the administrator candidate as administrator. Using automated selection provided by the Court Information System, another administrator candidate is selected from the List of Candidates, and the judge evaluates his or her suitability for performing the administrator's duties in the respective credit institution insolvency proceedings.

(2)	A person to whom the restrictions set out in the Credit Institution Law apply may not be appointed as administrator.

(3)	When appointing an administrator, he or she shall be instructed to:

1)	prepare a list of persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory;

2)	prepare a report on the credit institution's assets (property) at their actual (market) value;

3)	identify property belonging to third parties that is in the possession or holding of the credit institution and prepare a list of such property;

4)	prepare a list of creditors according to the data in the credit institution's accounts, indicating information about creditors, the amounts of debts and obligations and the performance deadlines;

5)	submit the said information to the court before the hearing of the case.

(4)	A declaration signed by the administrator shall be attached to the case, which confirms his or her consent to assume office and to assume the liability provided for by law.

(5)	(Deleted as of 01.09.2023. by the law of 16.03.2023. See transitional provision 181)
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The new wording of the first part, part 1.1 and the amendment on the deletion of the fifth part enter into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision 181)

### 375. pants. Hearing of credit institution insolvency cases and liquidation cases

(1)	The court shall hear a credit institution insolvency case and liquidation case within 10 days from the date of initiation of the case.

(2)	The applicant, the representative of the credit institution, the representative of the Bank of Latvia, and in an insolvency case — also the administrator, shall be invited to the court session.

(3)	In a credit institution insolvency case and liquidation case, withdrawal from the application or amendment thereof is not permitted.

(4)	When hearing a credit institution insolvency case, the court shall verify whether there is any of the circumstances provided for in the Credit Institution Law indicating the insolvency of the credit institution and whether the pre-trial examination procedure for the application provided for in Section 367 of this Law has been observed.

(5)	When hearing a credit institution liquidation case, the court shall not assess the solvency of the credit institution.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001., 12.02.2009., 11.11.2021. and 16.03.2023., which enters into force on 29.03.2023. The amendment in the first part replacing the word "seven" with the number "10" enters into force on 01.09.2023. See transitional provision 181)

### 376. pants. Court judgment in a credit institution insolvency case

(1)	If the court establishes any of the circumstances indicating the insolvency of the credit institution, it shall, by its judgment, declare the credit institution insolvent and determine that the insolvency of the credit institution occurs on the day of pronouncement of the court judgment. The judgment is final and not subject to appeal.

(2)	When making a judgment on the insolvency of a credit institution, the court shall confirm the appointed administrator.

(3)	On the basis of the application of the Bank of Latvia and the list prepared by the administrator, the court shall determine those representatives of the credit institution and persons whose participation in the insolvency proceedings is mandatory.

(4)	The judgment is the basis for suspension of civil proceedings initiated against the credit institution and for termination of enforcement proceedings in cases concerning the recovery of amounts awarded but not recovered from the credit institution.

(5)	If the court does not establish circumstances indicating the insolvency of the credit institution, it shall reject the application, simultaneously terminating the insolvency proceedings and deciding the question of whether the application is to be recognised as knowingly false in accordance with the Credit Institution Law.

(1)	Pieteikumu par nekustamā īpašuma labprātīgu pārdošanu izsolē tiesas ceļā var iesniegt īpašnieks vai ķīlas ņēmējs, kuram ir tiesības pārdot ķīlu par brīvu cenu.

(3)	Pārdošanas nosacījumos norāda:

1)	pārdodamā nekustamā īpašuma sastāvu;  

2)	nekustamā īpašuma apgrūtinājumus un ieķīlājumus;  

3)	izsoles sākumcenu;  

4)	nosolītās augstākās cenas samaksas veidu un kārtību;  

5)	tiesības nekustamajā īpašumā, kuras īpašnieks patur sev;  

6)	citus pārdošanas nosacījumus, kurus pārdevējs atzīst par nepieciešamiem.  

(4)	Ja pārdodamais nekustamais īpašums atrodas vairāku personu kopīgā īpašumā, tad, nosakot pārdošanu izsolē tiesas ceļā pēc īpašnieka pieteikuma, ir vajadzīga visu kopīpašnieku piekrišana.  

(5)	Ja vienam un tam pašam ķīlas ņēmējam viena un tā paša parādnieka nekustamajiem īpašumiem ir reģistrētas pirmās hipotēkas un tie savstarpēji ir funkcionāli saistīti vai tiem ir kopēja robeža, pieteicējam ir tiesības lūgt tiesu pieteikumā norādītos nekustamos īpašumus izsolīt kā kopību.

Seventh section Enforcement of obligations through court proceedings

49.	chapter
Voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings

### 395. Article. Jurisdiction

An application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the immovable property.

### 396. Article. Application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings

(1)	An application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings may be submitted by the owner or the pledgee who has the right to sell the pledge at a free price.  

(2)	The application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction through court proceedings shall be accompanied by the terms of sale and a printout from the relevant land register section indicating the valid entries and notes, but if the application has been submitted by the pledgee, also the pledge agreement, evidence of warning to the debtor, unless it follows from the law that such warning is not necessary. Confirmation of the issuance of the warning may also be an act drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his assistant regarding refusal to receive the warning.  

(3)	The terms of sale shall indicate:

1)	the composition of the immovable property to be sold;  

2)	encumbrances and mortgages on the immovable property;  

3)	the starting price of the auction;  

4)	the method and procedure for payment of the highest price bid;  

5)	rights in the immovable property that the owner retains;  

6)	other terms of sale that the seller considers necessary.  

(4)	If the immovable property to be sold is in the joint ownership of several persons, then, when determining the sale at auction through court proceedings upon the owner's application, the consent of all co-owners is required.  

(5)	If the same pledgee has first mortgages registered on immovable properties of the same debtor and they are functionally related to each other or have a common border, the applicant has the right to request the court to auction the immovable properties specified in the application as a whole.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., Constitutional Court judgment of 24.11.2010., laws of 20.12.2010., 08.09.2011. and 11.11.2021., which comes into force 01.12.2021.)

### 397. Article. Judge's decision

(1)	The application for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction shall be examined by a judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the documents attached thereto within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor.  

(2)	The judge shall make a decision to allow the sale at auction, having ascertained that:

1)	the immovable property belongs to the applicant or the pledgee's debtor and the pledgee has the right to sell the immovable property at a free price;  

2)	there are no lawful obstacles to the sale of this immovable property with the terms specified in the application.  
(31.10.2002. law version, which comes into force 01.01.2003.)

### 398. Article. Auction procedure

The sale at auction shall be carried out by a bailiff in the manner established in this law for the enforcement of court judgments, observing the provisions of Articles 2075, 2083, 2084, 2087, 2089 and 2090 of the Civil Law and the following conditions:

1)	the immovable property shall be described and appraised only if requested by the person on whose application the sale is taking place;  

2)	the announcement shall indicate the terms of sale, as well as that the sale is voluntary;  

3)	the auction shall begin by reading out the terms of sale;  

4)	at the request of the applicant, the auction may be considered to have taken place even if only one buyer has appeared;  

5)	if, in accordance with the terms of sale, the acceptance of the highest price bid depends on the person on whose application the sale is taking place, and if he has not expressed his opinion within the time provided for in the terms of sale or determined by the court, it shall be considered that he has tacitly agreed to the highest price bid.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which comes into force 01.01.2003.)

### 399. Article. Documents to be issued to the buyer

(1)	After the buyer of the immovable property has fulfilled all the terms of sale, the district (city) court shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act (Articles 611 and 613) and the registration of the sold immovable property in the buyer's name. If insolvency proceedings have been declared for the owner of the immovable property, the district (city) court in whose jurisdiction the legal person's insolvency proceedings case is located shall decide on the confirmation of the auction act and the registration of the sold immovable property in the buyer's name.

### 400. pants. Obligations for which uncontested enforcement is permissible

(1)	Uncontested enforcement of obligations is permissible:

1)	under agreements for obligations secured by a public mortgage or commercial pledge;  

2)	under notarised and legally equivalent fixed-term agreements for payment of money or delivery of movable property;  

3)	under notarised or land register-recorded fixed-term property lease or rental agreements that provide for the lessee's or tenant's obligation to vacate the leased or rented property due to expiry of the term or non-payment of lease or rental payments, as well as the obligation to pay the lease or rental payment;  

4)	under protested bills of exchange that have not been issued in the form of a notarial deed.  

(11) The first paragraph of this section does not apply to notarial deeds drawn up in the procedure established in Section D1 of the Notaries Law.  

(2)	The obligations specified in the first paragraph of this section are not subject to uncontested enforcement if:

1)	such enforcement is directed against state or municipal property;  

2)	the obligation has been extinguished by limitation, the expiry of which is clearly evident from the deed itself.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 23.05.2013., 25.03.2021. and 16.06.2022., which enter into force on 07.07.2022.  
The new wording of paragraph 1, point 4 enters into force on 01.10.2022. See transitional provision 178)

### 401. pants

Persons who may submit an application for uncontested enforcement

An application for uncontested enforcement may be submitted by:

1)	a person in whose name the deed (agreement, bill of exchange) has been issued;  

2)	a person to whom the deed has been transferred by a separate land register deed or notarial deed;  

3)	the heir of the said persons, if his or her inheritance rights have been proven by a court judgment, certificate of inheritance or European Certificate of Succession regarding the entry into legal force of a will or confirmation of inheritance rights, or a court decision by which he or she has been placed in possession of the bequeathed property (Section 638 of the Civil Law), or a court decision or notarial confirmation by which it is recognised that he or she has accepted the inheritance (Section 697 of the Civil Law);  

4)	a guarantor who has paid in place of the debtor on the basis of a court judgment or in the procedure of enforcement, or whose payment has been confirmed by an inscription on the deed;  

5)	under immovable property lease or rental agreements — the acquirer of such property, if the acquirer's rights are certified by a land register deed or by the documents specified in point 3 of this section regarding the transfer of property by way of inheritance;  

6)	under protested bills of exchange — the holder of the bill in whose name the bill has been protested, as well as the guarantor, endorser (girant) and intermediary who have paid the bill and bring a recourse claim.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 23.05.2013. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force on 02.07.2015.  
The amendment to point 3 enters into force on 17.08.2015. See transitional provision 108)

### 402. pants. Persons against whom uncontested enforcement is permissible

Uncontested enforcement is permissible:

1)	against a person in whose name the deed has been issued (contracting party), but under a protested bill of exchange — against all persons liable for it;  

2)	against a guarantor if he or she has assumed the obligation as the debtor himself or herself (second paragraph of Section 1702 of the Civil Law);  

3)	against the heir of the person who assumed the obligations, if there is evidence of acceptance of the inheritance as specified in point 3 of Section 401 of this Law.

### 403. pants. Jurisdiction

(1)	Applications for uncontested enforcement in monetary payment obligations, movable property delivery obligations or obligations under agreements secured by a commercial pledge shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the debtor's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the place of residence or registered address.  

(2)	Applications for uncontested enforcement under immovable property mortgage deeds and under obligations to vacate or return leased or rented immovable property shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the location of the immovable property

. If the obligation is secured by several immovable properties and the applications fall within the jurisdiction of different district (city) courts, the application shall be examined by the district (city) court at the applicant's choice — according to the location of one immovable property.  

(3)	Applications for uncontested enforcement under a ship mortgage bond shall be submitted to the district (city) court according to the place of registration of the mortgage.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012. and 25.10.2018., which enter into force on 28.11.2018. Amendments to the section enter into force on 01.06.2019. See transitional provision 151)

### 404. pants. Content of the application

(1)	The application shall indicate which obligation and under which deed the creditor requests to be subjected to uncontested enforcement.  

(11) The application shall include a confirmation that the court has been provided with truthful information about the facts and that the applicant or representative, if the application is submitted by a representative, has been informed that the Criminal Law provides for liability for submitting a false application.  

(2)	An application for uncontested enforcement for payment of money shall indicate the principal debt to be recovered, contractual penalties and interest — both agreed and statutory, but under a bill of exchange — also expenses related to the protest and statutory compensation, as well as the name of the credit institution and account number to which payment is to be made.  

(3)	The following shall be attached to the application:

1)	the deed to be executed in uncontested procedure;  

11)	under a protested paper form bill of exchange — the bill, its derivative and protest deed in paper form;  

12)	under a protested electronic bill of exchange — the electronic bill and electronic protest deed;  

2)	a document on payment of the state fee, except where the application has been submitted and payment made in the online system;  

3)	proof of issuance of a warning to the debtor (including to the owner of immovable property or the pledgor of a commercial pledge), unless it follows from the law that such a warning is not necessary. Confirmation of issuance of the warning may also be a deed drawn up by a sworn bailiff or his or her assistant regarding refusal to receive the warning.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011., 19.12.2013., 22.06.2017., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 405. pants. Judge's decision

(1)	An application for uncontested enforcement of obligations shall be decided by a judge sitting alone on the basis of the submitted application and attached documents within seven days from the date of submission of the application, without notifying the applicant and the debtor.  

(2)	The judge, having verified the validity of the submitted application and having found it to be satisfiable, shall adopt a decision determining which obligation and in what amount is to be executed in uncontested procedure. The decision shall be communicated to the applicant and the debtor.  

(21) If the decision establishes a person's obligation to vacate leased or rented property before the end of the term specified in the agreement, the judge shall in this paragraph set a two-month period for voluntary execution of the decision.  

(3)	The judge's decision enters into force immediately and has the force of an enforcement document. The decision is enforceable in accordance with the rules for execution of judgments. It shall be submitted for execution together with a copy of the deed subjected to uncontested enforcement.  

(4)	If the judge finds that the application is not justified or that the amount of the contractual penalty specified in the application is disproportionate to the principal debt, or that the enforceable deed contains unfair contract terms infringing consumer rights, he or she shall adopt a decision to reject it. The judge shall send the decision together with the submitted documents to the applicant.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009., 25.03.2021. and 11.11.2021., which enter into force on 01.12.2021.)

(1)	Ja parādnieks uzskata, ka kreditora prasījums nav pamatots pēc būtības, viņš sešu mēnešu laikā no lēmuma nosūtīšanas dienas var celt prasību pret kreditoru, lai apstrīdētu prasījumu. Prasība ceļama tiesā šajā likumā noteiktajā prasības celšanas vispārējā kārtībā.

(4)	Pieņemot lēmumu par parādnieka pieteikumu par bezstrīdus piespiedu izpildīšanas vai notariālā izpildu akta izpildīšanas apturēšanu, tiesa vai tiesnesis ņem vērā prasības pirmsšķietamo (prima facie) formālo juridisko pamatojumu.  

(41) Pieņemot lēmumu par maksātnespējas procesa administratora pieteikumu par pagaidu aizsardzības līdzekli — balsstiesību atņemšanu, tiesa ņem vērā prasības pirmšķietamo (prima facie) formālo juridisko pamatojumu. Tiesas lēmums nav pārsūdzams.  

(5)	Lēmums par parādnieka pieteikumu par bezstrīdus piespiedu izpildīšanas vai notariālā izpildu akta izpildīšanas apturēšanu, ar kuru parādnieka pieteikums apmierināts, nav pārsūdzams un ir izpildāms nekavējoties pēc tā pieņemšanas. Par lēmumu, ar kuru pieteikums noraidīts, parādnieks var iesniegt blakus sūdzību.  

(6)	Pēc kreditora motivēta pieteikuma tiesa, kura apturējusi izpildi vai kuras lietvedībā atrodas lieta, kas izskatāma pēc būtības, var atcelt izpildes apturēšanu. Lēmums par izpildes apturēšanas atcelšanu nav pārsūdzams un ir izpildāms nekavējoties pēc tā pieņemšanas. Par lēmumu, ar kuru pieteikums noraidīts, kreditors var iesniegt blakus sūdzību.

### 406. Section. Procedure for Contesting Undisputed Enforcement

(1) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated on the merits, he or she may, within six months from the date of sending the decision, bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim. The action shall be brought in court in accordance with the general procedure for bringing an action established in this law.

(2) If the debtor considers that the creditor's claim is not substantiated on the merits, he or she may, within six months from the date on which the notarial writ of execution issued by a sworn notary has been sent to the debtor, bring an action against the creditor to contest the claim.

(3) When bringing an action, the debtor may request suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution issued by a sworn notary, but if the claimant has already received satisfaction in such manner — request security for the claim.

(31) When bringing an action against the creditor to contest a claim based on a court decision on undisputed enforcement of obligations, an insolvency administrator may request the court to apply an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights.

(4) When adopting a decision on the debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution, the court or judge shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim.

(41) When adopting a decision on the insolvency administrator's application for an interim protective measure — deprivation of voting rights, the court shall take into account the prima facie formal legal basis of the claim. The court's decision is not subject to appeal.

(5) A decision on the debtor's application for suspension of undisputed enforcement or execution of a notarial writ of execution, by which the debtor's application has been satisfied, is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. Regarding a decision by which the application has been rejected, the debtor may submit an appeal.

(6) Upon a reasoned application by the creditor, the court which has suspended execution or in whose proceedings the case to be examined on the merits is pending may revoke the suspension of execution. A decision on revocation of suspension of execution is not subject to appeal and is enforceable immediately upon its adoption. Regarding a decision by which the application has been rejected, the creditor may submit an appeal.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012., 23.05.2013., 30.10.2014., 12.02.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enter into force on 01.12.2021.)
