### 465. Section. Scheduling of a Case for Hearing in a Supreme Court Session

(1)	The time of case hearing, the composition of the court and the rapporteur shall be determined by the President of the Department of the Supreme Court. The participants in the case shall be notified of the time and place of the case hearing.

(2)	In the cassation instance, a case shall be heard by three judges, but in cases provided for in this law — by a panel of judges consisting of not less than seven judges.
(As amended by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 12.02.2015, which enter into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 466. Section. Commencement of Case Hearing

(1)	The presiding judge shall open the court session and announce which case the Supreme Court is hearing.

(2)	The presiding judge shall ascertain which participants in the case have appeared, their identity and the authorisation of representatives.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002, 12.02.2004 and 30.10.2014, which enters into force on 01.01.2015.)

### 467. Section. Explanation of Rights and Obligations to Participants in the Case

(1)	The presiding judge shall announce the composition of the court, as well as name the prosecutor and interpreter, if one participates in the court session, and shall explain to the participants in the case their right to file challenges, as well as other procedural rights and obligations.

(2)	The grounds for challenge and the procedure for deciding a challenge shall be determined by Sections 19 to 21 of this law.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 12.02.2004, which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

### 468. Section. Consequences Arising if Participants in the Case Do Not Appear at the Court Session

The non-appearance of those participants in the case who have been duly notified of the time and place of the cassation instance court session shall not be an obstacle to the hearing of the case.

### 469. Section. Decision on an Application

Applications by participants in the case related to the hearing of the case shall be decided after hearing the opinion of other participants in the case.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 as amended by the law of 12.02.2004, which enters into force on 10.03.2004.)

### 470. Section. Report on the Case

The hearing of a case shall commence with the report on the case by the rapporteur judge.
(As amended by the law of 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 471. Section. Explanations of Participants in the Case and Opinion of the Prosecutor

(1)	After the judge's report, the court shall hear the explanations of the parties or their representatives. The court may determine in advance the time for giving explanations, but it must be granted equally to both parties.

(2)	The first to speak shall be the participant in the case who has submitted the cassation complaint, or the prosecutor, if he or she has submitted a protest. If both parties have appealed the judgment, the plaintiff shall speak first.

(3)	Judges may ask questions to the participants in the case.

(4)	Each party shall have the right to one rebuttal.

(5)	If the prosecutor participates in a case in which no cassation protest has been submitted, he or she shall give an opinion after the parties' explanations and rebuttals.
(As amended by the laws of 31.10.2002, 12.02.2004 and 12.02.2015, which enters into force on 01.03.2015.)

### 472. Section. Procedure for Rendering a Judgment

(1)	After the explanations of the participants in the case and the opinion of the prosecutor, the court shall retire to deliberation in order to render a judgment.

(2)	If, when hearing a case in a composition of three judges, the court does not reach a unanimous opinion or all judges consider that the case should be heard in an extended composition, the court shall adopt a decision to refer the case for hearing in an extended composition of the Supreme Court.

(3)	When hearing a case in an extended composition, the judgment shall be rendered by a majority of votes and shall be signed by all judges.

(4)	After the judges' deliberation, the court shall return to the courtroom and the presiding judge shall announce the judgment by reading its operative part and shall notify when the participants in the case may familiarise themselves with the judgment.

(5)	A judge who, when hearing a case in the extended composition of the Supreme Court, has had a different opinion on the interpretation of the law or the application of the law, shall have the right within 15 days after the drafting of the judgment to express in writing his or her separate opinion, which shall be attached to the case.

(6)	If the judges acknowledge that it is not possible to render a judgment in this court session, the Supreme Court shall schedule the next court session, which shall take place within the next 14 days and at which it shall announce the judgment.
(As amended by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 12.02.2015, 09.06.2016, 14.12.2017 and
11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

472.1 Section. Suspension of Proceedings in the Cassation Instance

If the cassation instance court adopts a decision to refer a question to the Court of Justice of the European Union for the adoption of a preliminary ruling, it shall suspend the proceedings until the decision of the Court of Justice of the European Union enters into legal force.
(In the wording of the law of 07.04.2004 as amended by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

58. Chapter
Judgment of the Cassation Instance Court

### 473. Section. Limits of Case Hearing

(1)	The court, when hearing a case in cassation proceedings, shall verify the legality of the judgment in the case in the appealed part with respect to the persons who have appealed the judgment or joined the cassation complaint, and with respect to the arguments stated in the cassation complaint.

(2)	The court may set aside the entire judgment, even though only a part of it has been appealed, if it finds such violations of law that have led to incorrect adjudication of the entire case.

### 474. Section. Rights of the Cassation Instance Court

The court, having heard the case, may render one of the following judgments:

1)	leave the judgment unchanged and dismiss the complaint;

2)	set aside the entire judgment or a part thereof and refer the case for new hearing to the appellate or first instance court;

3)	set aside the entire judgment or a part thereof and leave the application without examination or terminate the proceedings if the second instance court has not complied with the provisions of Section 219 or 223 of this law;

4)	amend the judgment in the part concerning the amount of the claim if it has been incorrectly determined by erroneously applying a substantive law provision.
(As amended by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 475. Section. Content of the Cassation Instance Court Judgment

(1)	The judgment of the cassation instance court shall consist of an introductory, descriptive, reasoning and operative part.

(2)	In the introductory part, the court shall indicate:

1)	the name and composition of the court;

2)	the time of rendering the judgment;

3)	the participants in the case and the subject of the dispute;

4)	the persons who have submitted a cassation complaint (counter-complaint) or joined it.

(3)	In the descriptive part, the court shall indicate:

1)	a brief statement of the circumstances of the case;

2)	the essence of the judgment of the appellate instance court;

3)	the arguments of the cassation complaint;

4)	the arguments of the counter-complaint or the essence of the explanation.

(4)	In the reasoning part, the court shall indicate:

1)	when dismissing the cassation complaint — the arguments for which the complaint has been dismissed;

2)	when granting the cassation complaint — the arguments concerning the violations of legal provisions committed by the court, their incorrect application or violation of the limits of competence.

(5)	In the operative part, the court shall indicate the decision in accordance with the relevant point of Section 474 of this law.

(6)	If the court, when hearing a case, acknowledges that the reasoning contained in the appealed judgment on the issue of application of legal provisions is correct, it may indicate in the reasoning part of the judgment that it acknowledges the respective argumentation as correct. In such a case, the arguments provided for in point 1 of paragraph four of this Section may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.

(7)	If the court, when hearing a case, acknowledges that the appealed judgment does not comply with the case-law of the Supreme Court that has been established in other similar cases and the appealed judgment does not indicate with reasoning why there has been a departure from the case-law, the court may render a judgment in the reasoning part of which it indicates the case-law that has not been observed or the non-observance of which has not been justified. In such a case, the descriptive part may not be included in the judgment and the arguments provided for in point
2 of paragraph four of this Section may not be indicated in the reasoning part of the judgment.
(As amended by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### 476. Section. Binding Nature of Instructions of the Cassation Instance Court

(1)	The interpretation of law expressed in the judgment of the cassation instance court shall be binding on the court that hears this case anew.

(2)	The cassation instance court shall not indicate in its judgment what judgment should be rendered when hearing the case anew.

### 477. Section. Legal Force of the Judgment of the Court of Cassation

The judgment of the court of cassation is not subject to appeal and enters into force at the moment of its pronouncement.

Section 477.1 Actions of the Court of Cassation After Examination of the Cassation Complaint and Cassation Protest

After making (adopting) the decision referred to in the second part of Section 462, the third part of Section 464, the second part of Section 464.3 and points 1 and 4 of Section 474 of this Law, the court of cassation immediately sends the case to the court of appeal for the issuance of a writ of execution.
(In the wording of the law of 22.05.2008 with amendments made by the laws of 15.03.2012 and 14.12.2017, which enters into force on 15.01.2018. The amendment to the section regarding the exclusion of the word "full" enters into force on 01.03.2018. See transitional provision point 137)

Eleventh Division Reopening of a Case in Which a Judgment or Decision
Has Entered into Legal Force

Chapter 59
Reopening of a Case Due to Newly Discovered Circumstances

### Section 478. Submission of an Application

(1) Reopening of a case due to newly discovered circumstances is initiated upon the application of a party to the case. The application is submitted to the same court whose judgment or decision completed the examination of the case on the merits.

(2) The application may be submitted within three months from the day when the circumstances that constitute grounds for reopening the case were established.

(3) The application may not be submitted if more than 10 years have passed since the entry into force of the judgment or decision. This condition does not apply to cases where the newly discovered circumstances are a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court (point 6 of Section 479).

(31) An unsigned application is considered not submitted and is sent back to the submitter, refunding the security deposit.

(4) The judge adopts a decision to refuse to accept the application if:

1) the application is not accompanied by a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court with the application;

2) the security deposit has not been paid in the manner and amount prescribed by law;

3) the time limit specified in the second or third part of this section has been missed;

4) the application does not specify circumstances which, in accordance with Section 479 of this Law, may be recognised as newly discovered circumstances;

5) the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow from it that the factual or legal circumstances material to the resolution of the matter have substantially changed.

(5) The judge's decision to refuse to accept the application in accordance with points 1 and 2 of the fourth part of this section is not subject to appeal. An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the judge's decision to refuse to accept the application in accordance with points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth part of this section.

(6) If it does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the application that the representative is authorised to apply to the court with this application, the judge leaves the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Section 133 of this Law ensue.

(7) When submitting the application, a security deposit is payable in the amount specified in point 4 of the first part of Section 43.1 of this Law. If the court fully or partially revokes the contested court decision or if the application is withdrawn before its examination, the security deposit is refundable.

(8) If the court refuses to accept the application on the basis of points 1 and 2 of the fourth part of this section, the paid security deposit is refunded. If the court refuses to accept the application on the basis of points 3, 4 and 5 of the fourth part of this section, the security deposit is not refunded.

(9) The security deposit need not be paid by persons who, in accordance with law, are exempt from state duty. The court or judge, taking into account the financial situation of a natural person, may fully or partially exempt the person from payment of the security deposit.
(With amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009, 30.10.2014, 09.06.2016, 19.10.2017, 01.10.2020, 25.03.2021 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 479. Newly Discovered Circumstances

The following are recognised as newly discovered circumstances:

1) material circumstances of the case that existed at the time of examination of the case but were not and could not have been known to the applicant;

2) deliberately false witness testimony, deliberately false expert opinion, deliberately false translation, forged written or material evidence, on the basis of which the judgment was made, established by a judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force;

3) criminal activities, due to which an unlawful or unfounded judgment was made or a decision was adopted, established by a judgment in a criminal case that has entered into legal force;

4) the revocation of the judgment of that court or decision of another institution on the basis of which the judgment was made or decision was adopted in this case;

5) the recognition of the legal norm applied in adjudicating the case as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force;

6) a decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court in this case, from which it follows that proceedings must be initiated anew. In such a case, when adopting a decision in the reopened case, the court must base itself on the facts established in the decision of the European Court of Human Rights or another international or supranational court and their legal assessment.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 22.05.2008, which enters into force on 25.06.2008.)

### Section 480. Time Limit for Submission of an Application

The time limit for submission of an application is calculated:

1) for the circumstances specified in point 1 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day of discovery of these circumstances;

2) in the cases specified in points 2 and 3 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the judgment in the criminal case entered into legal force;

3) in the cases specified in point 4 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the court decision entered into legal force, by which the judgment in a civil case or criminal case was revoked, or when the decision of another institution was revoked, on the basis of which the judgment or decision is based that is requested to be revoked due to newly discovered circumstances;

4) in the case specified in point 5 of Section 479 of this Law — from the day when the judgment or other decision entered into force, in connection with which the applied legal norm loses force as inconsistent with a legal norm of higher legal force.
(With amendments made by the laws of 20.06.2001 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 481. Examination of the Application

(1) The application due to newly discovered circumstances is examined in written proceedings.

(2) When examining the application, the provisions of law on the inadmissibility of a judge participating in the repeated examination of a case are not applicable.
(In the wording of the law of 05.02.2009 with amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

### Section 482. Court Decision

(1) The court, having examined the application, verifies whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are to be recognised as newly discovered circumstances in accordance with Section 479 of this Law.

(2) If the court establishes newly discovered circumstances, it revokes the contested judgment or decision in full or in part thereof and refers the case for new examination to the same court or to a lower instance court.

(3) If the court recognises that the circumstances specified in the application are not to be considered newly discovered, it rejects the application.

(4) An interlocutory appeal may be submitted against the court decision by which the application for reopening of the case due to newly discovered circumstances has been rejected.
(With amendments made by the law of 09.06.2016, which enters into force on 13.07.2016.)

Chapter 60
Reopening of Cases Due to Material Violations of Substantive and Procedural Legal Norms

### Section 483. Submission of a Protest

A protest against a court decision that has entered into force may be submitted to the Supreme Court by the Prosecutor General if no more than 10 years have passed since the entry into force of the decision.
(In the wording of the law of 25.03.2021, which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### Section 484. Grounds for Submission of a Protest

The grounds for submission of a protest against a court decision that has entered into force are material violations of substantive or procedural legal norms established in cases that have been examined only in the court of first instance, if the court decision has not been appealed in the manner prescribed by law for reasons independent of the parties to the case, or if the court decision has infringed the rights of state or municipal institutions or the rights of persons who have not been parties to the case.

Reopening of a Case in Connection with Review of a Decision in Cases Provided for in European Union Legal Norms

## (Chapter 08

09.2011. Law version, which comes into force on 30.09.2011.)

485.1 pants. Submission of Application

(1)	Reopening of a case in connection with review of a decision may be initiated by the defendant, based on Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 April 2004 creating a European Enforcement Order for uncontested claims (hereinafter – European Parliament and Council Regulation No 805/2004), Article 18 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007, Article 20 of European Parliament and Council Regulation No 1896/2006, or Article 19 of Council Regulation (EC) No 4/2009 of 18 December 2008 on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and cooperation in matters relating to maintenance obligations (hereinafter – Council Regulation No 4/2009), by submitting an application:

1)	for review of a judgment or decision of a district (city) court – to the relevant regional court;  

2)	for review of a judgment or decision of a regional court – to the Supreme Court;  

3)	for review of a judgment or decision of the Court Chamber – to the Civil Cases Department of the Supreme Court.  

(2)	An application may be submitted within 45 days, but in accordance with European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007 within 30 days from the day when the review circumstances provided for in the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of this Section became known.  

(3)	An application may not be submitted if the limitation period has expired for submitting for enforcement the enforcement document concerning the relevant decision.  

(4)	An application which does not specify circumstances that in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of this Section may be recognised as circumstances for review of a decision shall not be accepted and shall be returned to the submitter. A judge shall refuse to accept for review an application for reopening of a case in connection with review of a decision also if the application has been submitted repeatedly and it does not follow therefrom that the circumstances for review of the decision have changed for resolution of the matter. An appeal may be submitted against such decision of a judge.  
(With amendments made by the Laws of 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015 and 01.06.2017, which comes into force on 01.07.2017. The amendment in paragraph two in connection with European Parliament and Council Regulation No 861/2007 comes into force on 14.07.2017. See transitional provision Point 126)

485.2 pants. Review of Application

An application for review of a decision shall be reviewed in written proceedings.  

485.3 pants. Court Decision

(1)	The court, having reviewed the application, shall verify whether the circumstances indicated by the applicant are to be recognised as circumstances for review of a decision in accordance with the European Union legal norms mentioned in paragraph one of Section 485.1 of this Law.  

(2)	If the court establishes circumstances for review of a decision, it shall set aside the contested decision in full and refer the case for new review to the court of first instance.  

(3)	If the court finds that the circumstances indicated in the application are not to be regarded as circumstances for review of a decision, it shall reject the application.  

(4)	An appeal may be submitted against the court decision.

Pieteikuma iesniegšana par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei

(1)	Ja pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas spriedums izpildāms Latvijā un labprātīgi netiek pildīts, ieinteresētā puse pieteikumu par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei var iesniegt rajona (pilsētas) tiesā pēc parādnieka deklarētās dzīvesvietas, bet, ja tādas nav, — pēc parādnieka dzīvesvietas vai juridiskās adreses vai pēc šķīrējtiesas sprieduma izpildes vietas.  

(2)	Pieteikumam par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei pievieno:

1)	pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas spriedumu;  

2)	šķīrējtiesas līgumu, kas apliecina pušu rakstveida vienošanos par civiltiesiskā strīda nodošanu izskatīšanai šķīrējtiesā;  

3)	(izslēgts ar 11.11.2021. likumu);  

4)	dokumentus, kas apstiprina valsts nodevas un ar pieteikumu par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei saistīto izdevumu samaksu.  

(3)	Šā panta otrās daļas 4.punktā minētos dokumentus var nepievienot, ja pieteikums iesniegts un samaksa veikta tiešsaistes sistēmā vai ja pieteikumā iekļauj ziņas par veikto valsts nodevas maksājumu un ar pieteikuma par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei saistīto izdevumu samaksu, norādot maksātāja identifikācijas datus — vārdu, uzvārdu, personas kodu vai nosaukumu un reģistrācijas numuru, ja tie atšķiras no pieteicēja datiem, kā arī maksājuma rīkojuma datumu un numuru. Veicot maksājumu, maksājuma rīkojuma mērķī norāda informāciju par parādnieku — viņa vārdu, uzvārdu, personas kodu vai nosaukumu un reģistrācijas numuru. Šajā gadījumā rajona (pilsētas) tiesa minētos maksājumus atzīst par saņemtiem valsts budžetā, izmantojot budžeta elektronisko norēķinu sistēmu.  

(4)	(Izslēgta ar 11.11.2021. likumu)

(2)	Paskaidrojumā lietas dalībnieks norāda:

5)	citus apstākļus, kurus viņš uzskata par nozīmīgiem pieteikuma izskatīšanā.

### 535. pants

Pieteikuma par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei izlemšana

(1)	Lēmumu par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei vai lēmumu par atteikumu izsniegt izpildu rakstu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei pieņem tiesnesis uz iesniegto dokumentu pamata, neaicinot lietas dalībniekus, 20 dienu laikā no dienas, kad paskaidrojumi nosūtīti pārējiem lietas dalībniekiem, vai 20 dienu laikā no dienas, kad beidzies termiņš paskaidrojumu sniegšanai. Pieņemot lēmumu par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei, tiesnesis izlemj arī jautājumu, vai atlīdzināma valsts nodeva par šāda izpildu raksta izsniegšanu un vai atlīdzināmi ar lietas izskatīšanu saistītie izdevumi. Lēmumu pusēm nosūta triju dienu laikā. Lēmumu par atteikumu izsniegt izpildu rakstu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei pastāvīgajai šķīrējtiesai nosūta uz tās mājaslapā norādīto elektroniskā pasta adresi.  

(2)	Tiesa var izprasīt no pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas lietu vai citu informāciju, ja tā nepieciešama šā panta pirmajā daļā minētā lēmuma pieņemšanai.  

(3)	Lēmums par izpildu raksta izsniegšanu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei nav pārsūdzams.  

(4)	Par lēmumu atteikt izsniegt izpildu rakstu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei var iesniegt blakus sūdzību 10 dienu laikā no lēmuma saņemšanas dienas.  

(5)	Lēmums par atteikumu izsniegt izpildu rakstu pastāvīgās šķīrējtiesas sprieduma piespiedu izpildei stājas spēkā pēc tam, kad beidzies blakus sūdzības iesniegšanas termiņš un blakus sūdzība nav iesniegta.

(1)	When an application for issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award has been received by the district (city) court, it shall be immediately sent to the other participants in the case to their official electronic addresses or by registered mail, setting a time limit for submission of written explanations, which shall not be shorter than 20 days from the date of sending the application.

### 535. pants

Determination of Application for Issuance of Writ of Execution for Forced Enforcement of Permanent Arbitration Award

(1)	A decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award or a decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall be adopted by the judge on the basis of the submitted documents, without summoning the participants in the case, within 20 days from the date when the explanations have been sent to the other participants in the case, or within 20 days from the date when the time limit for providing explanations has expired. When adopting a decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award, the judge shall also decide the question of whether the state fee for issuance of such writ of execution is to be reimbursed and whether the expenses related to the examination of the case are to be reimbursed. The decision shall be sent to the parties within three days. A decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall be sent to the permanent arbitration to the e-mail address indicated on its website.  

(2)	The court may request from the permanent arbitration the case file or other information if it is necessary for adoption of the decision referred to in Paragraph one of this Section.  

(3)	A decision on issuance of a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall not be subject to appeal.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against a decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award within 10 days from the date of receipt of the decision.  

(5)	A decision on refusal to issue a writ of execution for forced enforcement of a permanent arbitration award shall enter into force after the time limit for lodging an appeal has expired and an appeal has not been lodged.

### 541. Article. Preparation of a writ of execution

(1)	A writ of execution is prepared by the court of first instance or the court of appeal after the judgment or decision has entered into legal force, but in cases where the judgment or decision is immediately enforceable — immediately after the pronouncement of the judgment or the adoption of the decision.

(2)	If a time limit for voluntary execution has been set for the enforcement of a court judgment and the judgment has not been executed, the writ of execution is available in the online system for compulsory enforcement after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary execution.

(3)	(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.)

(31)	In the case referred to in point 4 of the second part of Article 539 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by the Riga City Court.

(32)	In the cases referred to in Articles 544.1 and 544.2 of this Law, the writ of execution is prepared by the district (city) court according to the place of execution of the decision or according to the declared place of residence of the debtor — natural person, but if there is none — according to the debtor's place of residence or the legal address of the legal person.

(33)	If several writs of execution are to be prepared for one judgment or a writ of execution is necessary in a case in which a settlement has been concluded, then the writ of execution, on the basis of a written request of the creditor, is prepared by the court that adopted the decision.

### 542. Article. Preparation of several writs of execution for one judgment

(1)	One writ of execution is prepared for each judgment, except in the cases specified in the second part of this Article.

(2)	Several writs of execution are prepared for one judgment if:

1)	the execution of the judgment is to be carried out in different places;

2)	the judgment is immediately enforceable in any part thereof;

3)	the judgment is made in favour of several applicants or is directed against several defendants;

4)	a different enforcement procedure is provided for by law for the execution of the claim satisfied or partially satisfied by the judgment.

(3)	When preparing several writs of execution, each of them precisely indicates the place of execution or the part of the judgment which is enforceable under this writ of execution, as well as the creditor in whose favour and the debtor against whom recovery is to be directed under this writ of execution.  
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 544.pants. Izpildu raksta dublikāta izsniegšana

(1)	Ja izpildu raksts nozaudēts, nozagts vai iznīcināts, tiesa, kas pieņēmusi nolēmumu, pēc piedzinēja pieteikuma, bet, ja tas noticis sprieduma izpildes procesā, — pēc tiesu izpildītāja pieteikuma var izsniegt izpildu raksta dublikātu. (2)	Pieteikumu par dublikāta izsniegšanu izskata tiesas sēdē, iepriekš par to paziņojot piedzinējam un parādniekam. Šo personu neierašanās nav šķērslis pieteikuma izskatīšanai par izpildu raksta dublikāta izsniegšanu.  

(3)	Pieņemot lēmumu par izpildu raksta dublikāta izsniegšanu, tiesa vienlaikus pasludina nozaudēto, nozagto vai iznīcināto izpildu rakstu par spēku zaudējušu un atbrīvo piedzinēju no valsts nodevas samaksas, ja nav konstatēta viņa vaina izpildu raksta nozaudēšanā, iznīcināšanā vai nozagšanā.  

(4)	Par tiesas lēmumu var iesniegt blakus sūdzību.  

(5)	Izpildu raksta dublikāts izsniedzams piedzinējam pēc lēmuma stāšanās spēkā un valsts nodevas samaksas, ja piedzinējs nav no tās atbrīvots.

### 543.pants. Content of the writ of execution

(1)	The writ of execution shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court that issued the writ of execution;  

2)	the case in which the writ of execution was issued;  

3)	the time of making the decision;  

4)	the operative part of the decision or a part thereof;  

5)	the time when the decision enters into legal force, or an indication that the decision is to be executed immediately;  

6)	(deleted by the law of 11.11.2021.);  

7)	information about the creditor and debtor: for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number, declared place of residence, additional address(es) indicated in the declaration and place of residence if it differs, and for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number;  

8)	information about the child — name, surname, personal identity number and location — in cases where a decision on the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence or a decision in a case arising from custody or contact rights is to be executed;  

9)	information about the contact person in whose presence contact rights are to be exercised (for natural persons — name, surname, personal identity number and address, for legal persons — name, legal address and registration number), if the decision in a case arising from contact rights has designated a contact person in whose presence contact is to be exercised, and the said person is not a representative of the orphan's court or a person authorised by the orphan's court;  

10)	information about the place where contact rights are to be exercised, if the decision in a case arising from contact rights has designated a place for the exercise of contact that is not the premises of the orphan's court;  

11)	information about the forced opening of premises — the address and the time period when the premises are to be opened — if the court has determined in the decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights that the premises are to be opened by force (eleventh paragraph of Section 244.13 of this Law).  

(2)	The writ of execution shall be signed by the judge.  

(3)	The content of other enforcement documents shall be determined by the respective laws.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 04.08.2011., 29.11.2012., 29.10.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

543.1 pants. Correction of errors in European Union enforcement documents

(1)	The court that made the judgment or adopted the decision may, upon application of a party to the case or, if provided for in European Union legal norms, also on its own initiative, correct errors:

1)	in the European Enforcement Order, based on Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council;  

2)	in the certificate referred to in Article 41(1) or Article 42(1) of Council Regulation No 2201/2003, based on Council Regulation No 2201/2003;  

3)	in the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, based on point (a) of Article 9(1) of Council Regulation No 606/2013;  

4)	in the certificate referred to in Article 36 or 47 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, based on Article 37 or 48 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.  

(2)	When submitting an application for the correction of a European Enforcement Order, the form referred to in Article 10(3) of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council shall be used.  

(3)	The question of correction of errors shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the parties to the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the question.  

(4)	Errors in the enforcement documents referred to in paragraph one of this Section shall be corrected by a court decision.  

(5)	An appeal may be lodged against the court decision to make a correction of errors in enforcement documents.  
(In the wording of the law of 07.09.2006. with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014. and 16.06.2022., which enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of paragraph one enters into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision 177)

### 544.pants. Issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution

(1)	If a writ of execution has been lost, stolen or destroyed, the court that adopted the decision may, upon application of the creditor, or, if it occurred during the enforcement proceedings, upon application of the bailiff, issue a duplicate of the writ of execution. The application shall indicate the circumstances in which the writ of execution was lost, stolen or destroyed.  

(2)	The application for the issuance of a duplicate shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the creditor and debtor. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application for the issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution.  

(3)	When adopting a decision on the issuance of a duplicate of the writ of execution, the court shall simultaneously declare the lost, stolen or destroyed writ of execution invalid and release the creditor from payment of the state fee if his or her fault in the loss, destruction or theft of the writ of execution has not been established.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the court decision.  

(5)	A duplicate of the writ of execution shall be issued to the creditor after the decision enters into force and payment of the state fee, if the creditor has not been released from it.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

544.1 Enforcement of a decision of a labour dispute commission

(1)	The decision of the labour dispute commission shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.  

(2)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the decision of the labour dispute commission attached to it within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.  

(3)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.  

(5)	The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it establishes that, in accordance with the law, the specific dispute may only be resolved in court.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 05.02.2009. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

544.2 pants. Enforcement of a regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement

(1)	The regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement shall be attached to the application submitted to the court for the issuance of a writ of execution.  

(2)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution or a reasoned refusal to issue it shall be adopted by the judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the regulator's decision on the examination of a dispute or disagreement attached to it within three days from the date of submission of the application, without summoning the parties.  

(3)	The decision on the issuance of a writ of execution shall enter into force immediately.  

(4)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision to refuse to issue a writ of execution within 10 days from the date when the decision was issued to the claimant.  

(5)	The court shall refuse to issue a writ of execution if it establishes that, in accordance with the law, the specific dispute or disagreement may only be resolved in court.  
(In the wording of the law of 08.09.2011. with amendments made by the laws of 22.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 545.pants. Liability for the preservation of an enforcement document

(Repealed by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

545.1 pants. Withdrawal of European Union enforcement documents

(1)	The court which has delivered the judgment or adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case, using the form referred to in Article 10(3) of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may withdraw the European Enforcement Order on the basis of Article 10 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council.  

(11)	The court which has adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case or on its own initiative, using the certificate referred to in Article 14 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, may withdraw the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the basis of point (b) of Article 9(1) of Council Regulation No 606/2013.  

(12)	The court which has delivered the judgment or adopted the decision, upon receipt of an application from a party to the case or on its own initiative, using the certificate referred to in Article 49 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, shall withdraw the certificate referred to in point (a) or (b) of Article 47(1) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 on the basis of Article 48(2) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.  

(2)	An application for the withdrawal of a European Enforcement Order, the withdrawal of the certificate referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council, or the withdrawal of the certificate referred to in point (a) or (b) of Article 47(1) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 shall be examined at a court hearing, after prior notification to the parties to the case. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the matter.  

(3)	An appeal may be lodged against the decision of the court.  
(As worded by the law of 07.09.2006 with amendments made by the laws of 30.10.2014 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of the title of the Section, Paragraph 1.2 and the amendment to Paragraph 2 enter into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision 177)

### 546.pants. Time limits within which enforcement documents must be submitted for enforcement

(1)	An enforcement document may be submitted for compulsory enforcement within 10 years from the date of entry into force of the court or judge's decision, unless other limitation periods are provided for by law.  

(2)	If periodic payments are recovered pursuant to a court judgment, the enforcement document shall retain its validity for the entire period for which the payments have been awarded, but the running of the time limit provided for in Paragraph 1 of this Section shall commence from the date of expiry of each payment.  

(3)	The time limits within which other enforcement documents referred to in Section 540 of this Law must be submitted for enforcement shall be determined by the respective laws.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002, which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 547.pants. Interruption of the limitation period for submission of an enforcement document

(1)	The limitation period shall be interrupted by submitting the enforcement document for enforcement. The limitation period shall also be interrupted by partial voluntary execution of the decision.  

(2)	After the interruption, the running of the time limit shall recommence, without counting the time that has elapsed before. If full recovery has not been made pursuant to the enforcement document and it has been returned to the creditor, the new time limit for submission of the document shall be counted from the day on which it was issued to the creditor.

### 550. pants. Recusal or rejection of a bailiff

(1)	A bailiff is prohibited from performing enforcement actions in cases where one of the parties is the bailiff himself or herself, his or her spouse, including former spouse, a relative of his or hers or of his or her spouse in direct line in all degrees, in collateral line — up to the fourth degree and in affinity relations — up to the third degree, a person under the guardianship or curatorship of his or hers or of his or her spouse, or adoptive parents or adopted children of his or hers or of his or her spouse, as well as when there are other circumstances under the influence of which the bailiff justifiably cannot maintain objectivity and neutrality.

(2)	A rejection of a bailiff may be declared by the creditor or debtor by submitting a written application to him or her if there are circumstances that give rise to justified doubts about the bailiff's objectivity. The bailiff shall decide on the application immediately. A decision by which the application is left without satisfaction may be appealed to the district (city) court according to the bailiff's place of office. The filing of a complaint does not suspend enforcement actions.

(3)	An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding a court decision to refuse the rejection of a bailiff.

(4)	If a bailiff has recused himself or herself or has been rejected, he or she shall transfer the enforcement document for further execution to another bailiff in the procedure established by the Council of Sworn Bailiffs of Latvia.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 05.02.2009. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 01.03.2009.)

### 551. pants. Obligation of bailiff's demands or orders

(1)	A bailiff's demands and orders in executing court judgments and other decisions are obligatory for natural and legal persons throughout the entire territory of the state. State institutions shall provide information necessary for ensuring the execution of judgments and other decisions to a sworn bailiff free of charge.

(2)	If a bailiff's demands or orders are not executed, the bailiff shall draw up a report thereof and submit it to the court for it to decide the question of liability. The court may impose a fine on the guilty persons: on a natural person up to 360 euros, but on an official — up to 750 euros. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(3)	The court may impose a fine of up to 150 euros on a person (employer) who, pursuant to a court decision, was required to withhold maintenance for a child or parent and who has not notified the bailiff and the recipient of maintenance within the time period specified by law of the release of the maintenance payer from work, as well as of his or her new place of work or residence, if it is known to that person. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(4)	If resistance is shown in executing a judgment, the bailiff, in the presence of invited persons, but if it is not possible to invite persons — unilaterally, shall draw up a report thereof and, in order to remove obstacles, shall seek assistance from the police. The report shall be submitted to the court for it to decide the question of liability of those persons who resisted the execution of the judgment.

(5)	If the creditor or debtor refuses to sign a report drawn up by the bailiff, a note thereof shall be made in the drawn-up report, indicating the reasons for refusal. Refusal to sign a report drawn up by the bailiff does not affect the validity of the report.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 09.06.2011., 23.05.2013., 12.09.2013. un 09.06.2016.  
likumu, kas stājas spēkā 13.07.2016.)

### 552. pants. Debtor's obligations and consequences of their non-performance

(1)	The debtor shall appear before the bailiff upon summons and provide explanations regarding his or her financial situation and place of work, at the same time informing of amounts on which enforcement may not be levied (Section 596).

(2)	The debtor shall notify the bailiff of a change of place of work or declared place of residence, additional address indicated in the declaration or place of residence during the execution of the decision, as well as of additional sources of income.

(3)	If the debtor does not appear before the bailiff upon summons, refuses to provide explanations or does not provide the information specified by law, the bailiff may apply to the court for it to decide the question of liability of that person. The court may adopt a decision on the compulsory bringing of the debtor, as well as impose a fine on him or her: on a natural person up to 80 euros, but on an official — up to 360 euros. An ancillary complaint may be submitted regarding the court decision.

(4)	If it is established that the debtor has provided false information, the bailiff shall send a submission to the prosecutor.

(Ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 12.09.2013., 29.10.2015. un
09.06.2016. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 13.07.2016.)

General provisions of enforcement proceedings

552.1 pants. Opening of an enforcement case

(1)	A bailiff shall open a separate enforcement case for each received enforcement document.

(2)	If an enforcement document is not executed in the procedure established by law or the documents necessary in accordance with international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia or European Union legal norms are not attached to it, the state fee or other expenses of execution of the judgment have not been paid, the bailiff shall set a time period for remedying the deficiencies, which may not be less than 10 days.

(3)	If the deficiencies are remedied within the set time period, an enforcement case shall be opened and the enforcement document shall be deemed submitted on the day when it was first submitted to the bailiff.

(4)	If the creditor does not remedy the deficiencies within the set time period, the enforcement document shall be deemed not submitted and shall be returned to the creditor.

(5)	The return of an enforcement document to the creditor is not an obstacle to its repeated submission to the bailiff, observing the procedure for submission of enforcement documents established by law.

(6)	If the bailiff establishes that insolvency proceedings have been declared for the debtor, or a sworn notary has accepted an application for the release of a natural person from debt obligations, which includes debt obligations for which the received enforcement document has been issued, an enforcement case shall not be opened and the enforcement document shall be returned to the submitter, except in cases where the enforcement document has been issued in claims the execution of which is not related to levying enforcement on the debtor's property or funds. An enforcement case shall also not be opened for the voluntary sale of immovable property at auction or the transfer of movable property.

(7)	If the bailiff establishes that sanctions apply to the creditor in accordance with the International and National Sanctions Law of the Republic of Latvia (hereinafter — sanctions), including such sanctions established by a member state of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization that have been applied to the creditor, which, in accordance with the regulations of the Bank of Latvia, significantly affect the interests of financial market participants or the financial market, an enforcement case shall not be opened and the enforcement document shall be returned to the submitter, except in cases where the execution of a specific decision would not result in a violation, circumvention or evasion of the requirements established by sanctions for that person.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā ar grozījumiem, kas izdarīti ar 30.09.2010., 18.04.2013., 30.10.2014., 11.11.2021.,
15.06.2021. un 16.03.2023. likumu, kas stājas spēkā 29.03.2023.)

### 553.pants. Clarification of an enforceable court decision

If an enforceable court decision is not clear, the bailiff is entitled to request the court that adopted the decision to clarify it. Clarification of a decision shall take place in the procedure established in Section 202 or 437 of this Law.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

### 554.pants

Postponement of execution of a judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method and procedure of execution

(1)	If there are circumstances that make the execution of a court judgment difficult or make it impossible, the bailiff is entitled to submit to the court that rendered the judgment in the case a proposal for postponement of execution of the judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method or procedure of execution.

(2)	The court shall examine the bailiff's application for postponement of execution of a judgment, division into instalments, amendment of its method or procedure of execution in the procedure established in Section 206 or 438 of this Law.

(31.10.2002. likuma redakcijā, kas stājas spēkā 01.01.2003.)

### 558. pants. Parādnieka telpu apskate

### 555th Section. Notice of Obligation to Execute Decision

(1)	Upon commencing execution, the bailiff notifies the debtor, by sending or issuing a notice, of the obligation to execute the decision within 10 days. If the decision is to be executed immediately, the time limit for execution shall be set at no less than three days. In cases concerning the execution of confiscation of property and the execution of a decision on securing a claim or applying interim protection that does not impose a prohibition or obligation on the defendant to perform certain actions, a notice of the obligation to execute the decision shall not be sent.

(11) Upon commencing execution of the writ of execution referred to in point 17 of Section 540 of this law, except in cases where the writ of execution provides for the execution of a measure for securing a claim or interim protection, or execution of the writ of execution referred to in point
20 of Section 540 of this law, the bailiff, together with the notice, sends or issues the writ of execution to the debtor. If it is not evident from the documents submitted to the bailiff that the enforceable court decision, public act or settlement has been issued to the debtor, the enforceable court decision, public act or settlement shall also be attached to the writ of execution.

(2)	If the debtor is a natural person, the bailiff sends the notice to the debtor at the official electronic address, but if this is not possible, by registered mail to his or her last known place of residence or issues it to the debtor personally against signature. If the bailiff does not find the debtor at his or her place of residence, he or she issues the notice to one of the adult family members living together with the debtor.

(3)	If the debtor — a natural person — does not have an official electronic address and his or her place of residence is not known, the notice of the obligation to execute the decision shall be published in the official publication "Latvijas Vēstnesis".

(4)	If the debtor is a legal person, the bailiff sends the notice to the official electronic address, but if this is not possible, by registered mail to the debtor's legal address or issues it personally against signature to a representative of the debtor's executive body.

(5)	If the debtor or a representative of the debtor's executive body refuses to accept or sign the notice, the bailiff or the deliverer of the proposal shall draw up a record thereof. Refusal to accept or sign the notice shall not be an obstacle to the enforcement of the decision.

(6)	If the notice (in the case referred to in paragraph 1.1 of this Section — also the specified documents) has been delivered in the manner prescribed in this Section, it shall be deemed that the debtor has been notified of the decision and its execution time limit.

(7)	The bailiff may at any stage of the enforcement proceedings:

1)	request that the debtor declare his or her financial situation and changes therein during the last year, warning the debtor of criminal liability;

2)	attach the debtor's property, including attaching funds and deposits at a credit institution or with other payment service providers, funds due from other persons, or property held by other persons;

3)	submit a request for confirmation to the district (city) court for the entry of a recovery note in the land register or send an order to another public register for the entry of a prohibition on alienation or other actions.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003, 05.02.2009, 08.09.2011, 04.08.2011,
29.11.2012, 30.10.2014, 29.10.2015, 23.11.2016, 22.06.2017, 25.10.2018, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which
enters into force on 07.07.2022. The new wording of the first sentence of paragraph 1.1 enters into force on 01.08.2022. See transitional provision
point 177)

Section 555.1 Sending of Documents

Documents drawn up by the bailiff and other documents related to the execution of the decision provided for in this law shall be sent electronically to the addressee's official electronic address or to the electronic mail address indicated by the addressee, if he or she has notified the bailiff that he or she agrees to use electronic mail for communication with the bailiff. If it is not possible to send documents electronically, they shall be sent by ordinary mail, but the documents to be sent specified in the fourth paragraph of Section 581, the first paragraph of Section 583.1, the third paragraph of Section 584, the first and third paragraphs of Section 600, the second paragraph of Section 604, the fifth paragraph of Section 606, the first and third paragraphs of Section 618.2, the first paragraph of Section 618.6 and the fourth paragraph of Section 644.33 of this law — by registered mail. If it is not possible to send electronically the notice specified in point 1 of the first paragraph of Section 620.14 and point 1 of the first paragraph of Section 620.28 of this law, it shall be issued to the creditor against signature or sent by registered mail, or forwarded through the Ministry of Justice.
(In the wording of the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### Section 556. Enforcement of Court Judgment

(Deleted by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011.)

### Section 557. Means of Enforcement

Means of enforcement are:

1)	recovery against the debtor's movable property, including property held by other persons, and intangible things, by selling them;

2)	recovery against money due to the debtor from other persons (wages, payments equivalent thereto, other income of the debtor, deposits at credit institutions or with other payment service providers);

3)	recovery against the debtor's immovable property, by selling it;

31) recovery against the debtor's building rights, by selling them;

4)	transfer of property awarded by the court to the creditor and performance of actions imposed by the court judgment;

5)	eviction of persons and property specified in the judgment from premises;

6)	introduction into possession;

61) return of a child to the country where he or she has his or her place of residence;

7)	other means specified in the judgment.
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002 with amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 23.11.2016 and 01.03.2018, which enters into force on 01.07.2018.)

### Section 558. Inspection of Debtor's Premises

(1)	The bailiff is entitled, if necessary for making recovery, to carry out an inspection of the debtor's premises and his or her storage facilities. If the debtor does not participate in the inspection of premises and storage facilities, it shall be carried out in the presence of invited persons.

(2)	If the debtor refuses to admit the bailiff to premises which he or she occupies, or to the location of property, or refuses to open storage facilities, the bailiff shall invite a police representative, in whose presence the premises or storage facilities shall be opened and their inspection carried out.

(3)	If the manager of immovable property belonging to the debtor evades or refuses to admit the bailiff to the immovable property during enforcement of the decision and the manager has been notified in writing of the time of inspection of the immovable property at least five days in advance, the bailiff may carry out the inspection of the immovable property in the presence of a police representative without the participation of the manager.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002 and 19.06.2003, which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 567. pants. Sprieduma izpildes izdevumu maksāšanas kārtība izpildes procesā

(1)	Piedzinējs, iesniedzot izpildu dokumentu izpildei, norāda piespiedu izpildes līdzekli, ievērojot šā likuma 570. un 572.panta noteikumus, samaksā valsts nodevu un sedz citus sprieduma izpildes izdevumus tādā apmērā, kāds nepieciešams izpildes uzsākšanai piedzinēja norādītajā veidā. 5)	gadījumos, kad persona no tiesas izdevumu samaksas atbrīvota ar tiesas lēmumu, — pilnībā vai daļēji atbilstoši tiesas lēmumam;  

6)	gadījumos, kad piedziņa izdarāma atbilstoši vienotajam instrumentam, kas atļauj izpildi pieprasījuma saņēmējā dalībvalstī, izņemot gadījumus, kad Valsts ieņēmumu dienests ir vienojies ar dalībvalsts iestādi, kura lūgusi savstarpēju palīdzību prasījumu piedziņā, par izpildes izmaksu īpašu atlīdzināšanas kārtību;  

7)	kas ir trauksmes cēlēji un viņu radinieki vai saistītās personas ar šādu statusu celtajās prasībās, arī pieteikumos par prasības nodrošināšanu vai pagaidu aizsardzību.  

(3)	Gadījumos, kad piedzinējs ir atbrīvots no sprieduma izpildes izdevumu samaksas, zvērinātam tiesu izpildītājam no valsts budžeta līdzekļiem tiek izmaksāta kompensācija ar izpildu darbību veikšanu saistīto izdevumu segšanai.  

(4)	Izpildu darbību veikšanai nepieciešamo izdevumu apmēru un to maksāšanas kārtību, kā arī kompensācijas apmēra noteikšanas un izmaksas kārtību gadījumos, kad piedzinējs ir atbrīvots no sprieduma izpildes izdevumu samaksas, nosaka Ministru kabinets.

### 568. pants. Sprieduma izpildes izdevumu piedziņa

likuma 567. panta otrās daļas 1., 2., 2.1, 3. un 5. punktā minētajām lietām.  

(12)	Ja izpildu lietvedība ir izbeidzama, izņemot šā likuma 563. panta pirmās daļas 4. un 11. punktā noteiktos gadījumus, kā arī gadījumos, kad izpildu dokumentu izsniedz piedzinējam, pamatojoties uz šā likuma 565. panta pirmās daļas 2. vai 7. punktu, sprieduma izpildes izdevumus, ciktāl tie nav piedzīti no parādnieka, sedz piedzinējs, ja tas saskaņā ar šo likumu nav atbrīvots no to samaksas tiesu izpildītājam.  

(13)	Ja izpildu lietvedība izbeigta saskaņā ar šā likuma 563. panta pirmās daļas 14. punktu, sprieduma izpildes izdevumus, ciktāl tie nav piedzīti no parādnieka, sedz piedzinējs, ja tas saskaņā ar šo likumu no sprieduma izpildes izdevumu samaksas tiesu izpildītājam nav atbrīvots.  

(2)	Tiesu izpildītājs par sprieduma izpildes izdevumiem sastāda aprēķinu un nosūta parādniekam un piedzinējam. Aprēķinu var pārsūdzēt šā likuma 632.pantā noteiktajā kārtībā.  

(3)	Aprēķinā tiek norādīts, kādā apmērā sprieduma izpildes izdevumi atlīdzināmi tiesu izpildītājam (amata atlīdzība), piedzinējam (viņa samaksātā valsts nodeva un citi sprieduma izpildes izdevumi) vai ieskaitāmi valsts ienākumos.  

(4)	Ja nav iespējams sprieduma izpildes izdevumus piedzīt no parādnieka vai šā panta 1.1, 1.2 un sestajā daļā norādītajos gadījumos tos nav sedzis piedzinējs, tiesu izpildītājs uz sastādītā aprēķina pamata izraksta rēķinu un nodod to piespiedu izpildei.  

(5)	Rēķinu piespiedu izpildei nodod pēc tam, kad izbeidzies tiesu izpildītāja sastādītā sprieduma izpildes izdevumu aprēķina pārsūdzēšanas termiņš, bet, ja tas ir pārsūdzēts, — pēc tiesas nolēmuma stāšanās likumīgā spēkā.  

(6)	Izdevumus, kas saistīti ar tiesas lēmumu par prasības nodrošināšanu, pagaidu aizsardzības līdzekļa noteikšanu vai Eiropas kontu apķīlāšanas rīkojuma izpildi, sedz prasītājs.  

(61) Ja izpildu lietvedība izbeigta saskaņā ar šā likuma 563. panta pirmās daļas 4. punktu un sprieduma izpildes izdevumi nav piedzīti no parādnieka, izpildu lietvedību izbeidz daļā par nolēmuma izpildi, bet turpina daļā par sprieduma izpildes izdevumu piedziņu.  

(7)	Ja izpildu lietvedība izbeigta saskaņā ar šā likuma 563.panta pirmās daļas 11.punktu un palīdzības pieprasījuma atsaukšanas iemesls ir piedzenamā prasījuma vai tā izpildei izdotā dokumenta atcelšana, tiesu izpildītājs iesniedz Valsts ieņēmumu dienestam izpildes izdevumu aprēķinu un lūdz, lai tas vienojas ar dalībvalsts iestādi, kura lūgusi savstarpēju palīdzību prasījumu piedziņā, par izpildes izmaksu atlīdzināšanu.

### 567. pants. Procedure for Payment of Judgment Enforcement Costs in Enforcement Proceedings

(1)	When submitting an enforcement document for execution, the creditor shall indicate the means of compulsory enforcement, observing the provisions of Sections 570 and 572 of this Law, pay the state fee and cover other judgment enforcement costs in the amount necessary to commence enforcement in the manner indicated by the creditor. During judgment enforcement, the creditor shall pay in additional judgment enforcement costs as necessary upon instruction of the bailiff. In cases specified by law, during judgment enforcement the judgment enforcement costs for individual procedural actions shall be paid by the debtor.

(11) A creditor — natural person — in a claim for recovery of compensation for harm in a criminal case is released from the obligation to indicate the means of compulsory enforcement. The applicable means of compulsory enforcement, observing the provisions of Section 570 of this Law, shall be determined by the bailiff.

(2)	The following creditors are released from payment of judgment enforcement costs to the bailiff:

1)	in claims for recovery of wages and other claims of employees and persons in service that arise from or are related to employment or service legal relations;

2)	in claims arising from personal injuries that have caused mutilation or other health damage or resulted in death of a person;

21) in cases where recovery is made in favour of an injured party — natural person — in connection with a satisfied claim for compensation for harm in a criminal case;

3)	in claims for recovery of maintenance for a child or parent;

4)	in cases where recovery is made into state revenues;

5)	in cases where a person has been released from payment of court costs by a court decision — in full or in part in accordance with the court decision;

6)	in cases where recovery is made in accordance with a uniform instrument permitting enforcement in the requested Member State, except in cases where the State Revenue Service has agreed with the authority of the Member State that has requested mutual assistance in the recovery of claims on a special procedure for reimbursement of enforcement costs;

7)	who are whistleblowers and their relatives or related persons in claims brought with such status, including in applications for securing a claim or interim protection.

(3)	In cases where the creditor is released from payment of judgment enforcement costs, compensation shall be paid to the sworn bailiff from state budget funds to cover costs related to the performance of enforcement actions.

(4)	The amount of costs necessary for the performance of enforcement actions and the procedure for their payment, as well as the procedure for determining and paying compensation in cases where the creditor is released from payment of judgment enforcement costs, shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(41) If, when recovering compensation for harm in the case referred to in point 2.1 of the second paragraph of this Section, the amount recovered from the debtor is insufficient to cover the judgment enforcement costs in full, the remuneration in the amount of the fee and the costs necessary for the performance of enforcement actions in the uncovered part shall be covered to the bailiff from state budget funds in the procedure determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

### 570th Article. Enforcement Against the Property of a Natural Person

(1)	Enforcement shall be directed against the property of a natural person, including this person's share in co-ownership and in the joint property of spouses, as well as in cases provided by law — against the community of property of spouses.  

(2)	Enforcement against the debtor's property shall not be directed if the debtor works or receives a pension or scholarship and the amount of enforcement does not exceed the portion of monthly income against which enforcement may be directed by law.  

(3)	Enforcement against the debtor's immovable property is permissible if, by applying other enforcement measures, it is not possible to satisfy the creditor's claim within a reasonable time. This procedure does not apply to the recovery of debts secured by pledging the respective immovable property.  
(With amendments made by the law of 22.05.2014., which enters into force on 05.06.2014.)

### 571st Article. Property Against Which Enforcement May Not Be Directed

When executing judgments, enforcement may not be directed against the property referred to in Annex 1 of this law, except for the recovery of debts secured by pledging the respective items.  
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 572nd Article. Enforcement Against a Legal Person

(1)	Pursuant to enforcement documents, the bailiff shall first direct enforcement against the legal person's monetary funds held at credit institutions or with other payment service providers.  

(2)	If, by directing enforcement against the legal person's monetary funds at credit institutions or with other payment service providers, the creditor's claim is not satisfied, enforcement shall be directed against the legal person's property.  
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the law of 23.11.2016., which enters into force on 01.01.2017.

(1)	If the creditor has expressed a corresponding request, as well as a request to apply all the enforcement measures specified in points 1, 2 and 3 of Article 557 of this law, and if the debtor has not paid the amount specified in the notice into the bailiff's deposit account within the time limit set in the notice of the obligation to execute the decision, the bailiff shall notify the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration that the decision on the recovery of maintenance or the notarial deed containing an agreement on periodic maintenance payments and enforceable in the manner of execution of court judgments is not being fulfilled.  

(2)	If the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration, on the basis of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Law, has been substituted for the creditor in a maintenance recovery case in the part concerning the recovery from the debtor of maintenance paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, it shall have all the rights and obligations of the creditor provided for in this law.  

(3)	The enforcement order of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration for the recovery from the applicant of the amount of maintenance paid without justification shall not be returned to the creditor. If the bailiff, at the request of the creditor, has provided the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration with the information specified in the first paragraph of this article, the enforcement document shall be issued to the creditor only after a confirmation of the non-existence of the claim has been received from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration.

(5)	Viena veida priekšmetus tiesu izpildītājs var sasaiņot pakās, mantas aprakstes aktā norādot sasaiņoto priekšmetu kopējo nosaukumu. Atsevišķus priekšmetus var sasaiņot pakās, uz iesaiņojuma norādot aprakstīto priekšmetu nosaukumus.

### 574. Section. General provisions for seizure of debtor's movable property

(1) The bailiff shall seize the debtor's movable property in such quantity as is necessary to satisfy the amount to be recovered and to cover the costs of enforcement of the judgment. The bailiff shall not seize accessories of principal things separately from the principal thing.

(2) The bailiff may seize the debtor's movable property whose value exceeds the amount awarded to the creditor and the costs of enforcement of the judgment, if the debtor has no other property subject to seizure or the value of such property does not cover the amount to be recovered and the costs of enforcement of the judgment.

(3) After seizure of movable property, the bailiff shall request information from movable property registers regarding ownership of such things by the debtor, and shall also ascertain in the commercial pledge register whether the movable property belonging to the debtor has been pledged. If the bailiff establishes that the seized property belongs to third parties, he or she shall immediately release it from seizure. If a commercial pledge in favour of third parties is registered in the commercial pledge register on the debtor's movable property, the bailiff shall request that the debtor and the pledgee notify of the remaining amount of the debt.

(4) The bailiff may enforce against movable things pledged as a commercial pledge or possessory pledge to secure claims of third parties with the consent of the respective pledgee, and may also enforce against the surplus of money in the event of sale of the pledge. If the pledgee does not consent to the sale and himself or herself delays selling the pledged thing without justifiable reason, the bailiff shall explain to the creditor that he or she may request the court to set a time for sale of the pledged things in order to be able to enforce against the surplus of money, and shall also explain the right to establish a commercial pledge.

(5) If the bailiff establishes that the movable property has already been seized for another enforcement, he or she shall compare the property with the property inventory act drawn up in the previous seizure and shall seize only those items which are not entered in the earlier inventory act, but if he or she has already carried out the seizure — shall immediately release the items seized for the second time from seizure.

(6) If the debtor is absent or evades enforcement of the judgment, the movable property shall be seized by the bailiff with the participation of a representative of the municipality or the police.

(7) During seizure of the debtor's movable property, the debtor and the creditor have the right to invite no more than two witnesses. Non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend the seizure of property.

(8) During seizure of movable property, the debtor has the right to notify the bailiff as to which items enforcement should be directed first. The bailiff shall satisfy such application if it does not contradict the provisions of this law and does not hinder enforcement of the judgment.

(9) (Deleted by law of 05.02.2009.)

(10) (Deleted by law of 01.03.2018.)

(11) (Deleted by law of 01.03.2018.)
(In the wording of the law of 31.10.2002. with amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006., 05.02.2009. and 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 575. Section

Seizure of debtor's movable property if the property is with another person

(1) If there is evidence that the debtor's property is with another person, the bailiff shall seize this property in the general procedure. If the person refuses to admit the bailiff to the location of the movable property, the bailiff shall invite a police representative to ensure public order, in whose presence he or she shall open the premises or storage facility and carry out the seizure. Locked premises or storage facilities regarding which there is evidence that they contain the debtor's property, and which no person opens, may be opened by force in the presence of a police representative, or the bailiff, having assessed the specific circumstances, shall adopt a decision to postpone the seizure.

(2) If no adult person is found in the premises or other storage facilities after their opening, the bailiff shall, after forced opening of the premises, ensure their secure closure and sealing. The bailiff shall leave at the respective premises or storage facility a notice with an invitation to appear at the bailiff's place of practice to receive the keys to the premises.

(3) Things located in premises or storage facilities opened in the procedure specified in this section, which the bailiff does not seize, shall not be indicated in the property inventory act.

(4) If the debtor's property is with another person pursuant to a mutually concluded contract, the bailiff shall seize this property, but the question of preservation of the other person's rights arising from the contract shall be decided by the court in claim proceedings.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 576. Section. Inventory of corporeal things

(1) When inventorying corporeal things, their individual characteristics and quantity shall be precisely indicated, and photographic recording of the things shall be carried out.

(2) When inventorying corporeal things, new items shall be distinguished from used ones.

(3) When inventorying precious metals, the fineness (assay) shall be indicated if it is known. If things decorated with precious stones are inventoried, the number and colour of these stones shall be indicated, as well as the size and name if they are known.

(4) When inventorying goods, as well as products and materials in goods packaging, the numbers or marks on the packaging and the name and description of the goods stored in such packaging shall be indicated.

(5) The bailiff may package items of one type in bundles, indicating in the property inventory act the general name of the packaged items. Individual items may be packaged in bundles, indicating on the packaging the names of the inventoried items.
(In the wording of the law of 01.03.2018., which comes into force on 01.07.2018.)

### 580. pants. Parādniekam izņemtās naudas un vērtslietu glabāšana

(1)	Aprakstītos zelta un sudraba izstrādājumus un citas vērtslietas tiesu izpildītājs izņem un, ja nevar nodrošināt to saglabāšanu, nodod glabāšanā kredītiestādē.
