## (Chapter 31

Edition of law 10.2002, which enters into force 01.01.2003.)

Article 620.5 Notice of obligation to execute decision

(1) The notice of obligation to execute a court decision, together with family members and other persons to vacate the immovable property and transfer it to the acquirer, shall be sent by the bailiff to the debtor in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law.

(2) In the notice, the bailiff shall also indicate the date on which the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property will take place if the debtor fails to fulfil the obligation.

(3) Introduction into possession shall also take place if the acquirer has not yet registered the property rights in the Land Register.

(4) If introduction into possession of such immovable property is to be carried out which the bailiff has alienated as heirless property, the bailiff shall prepare a notice of the date and time of the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property and issue it to the person encountered on the immovable property. If no adult person is encountered on the immovable property, the bailiff shall leave the notice at the respective immovable property.
(With amendments made by the laws of 08.09.2011 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.6 Introduction into possession of immovable property in the presence of the debtor

(1) The introduction into possession of immovable property shall be carried out by the bailiff in the presence of the acquirer of the immovable property and the debtor or another adult person living together with him or her on the immovable property. These persons have the right to each invite no more than two witnesses. The bailiff shall verify the identity of the witnesses and indicate these persons in the record. Non-appearance of witnesses shall not suspend enforcement.

(2) The bailiff shall invite the debtor to vacate the immovable property of property belonging to him or her and to leave the immovable property together with family members and other persons.

(3) If the bailiff's invitation is not complied with, all persons in the premises shall be removed, but the property shall be described and valued by the bailiff in accordance with the provisions of Articles 577 and 578 of this law, and a custodian of the property shall be appointed, the property shall be removed and transferred to the custody of the custodian of the property according to the description record. Movable things belonging to the immovable property shall not be included in this description record and shall not be removed. Introduction into possession shall not affect the rights of other persons to use the premises if the rights to use the premises arise from registration in the Land Register.

(4) The bailiff shall issue one copy of the record to the debtor or the person in whose presence the introduction of the acquirer into possession of the immovable property was carried out.

(5) At the request of the debtor or the acquirer, the bailiff shall draw up a separate record of the immovable property to be transferred to the acquirer, which shall indicate the condition of the immovable property and the movable things belonging to it which are transferred to the acquirer.

(6) If things that spoil quickly have been described and removed, the bailiff shall sell them in accordance with the provisions of the second part of Article 581 of this law. The money received shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus of money shall be paid to the debtor.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.7 Introduction into possession of immovable property in the absence of the debtor

(1) If at the time appointed for introduction into possession of the immovable property neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living together with the debtor on the immovable property appears and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance or they have not appeared for a justifiable reason, the bailiff shall postpone the introduction into possession.

(2) If neither the debtor nor any of the other adult persons living together with the debtor on the immovable property appears at the time repeatedly appointed for introduction into possession of the immovable property and there is no information about the reason for their non-appearance or they have not appeared for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the premises shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of the forced opening of the premises.

(3) Introduction into possession of the immovable property shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of Article 620.6 of this law.

(4) The debtor is entitled to receive one copy of the property description record.

(5) Introduction into possession of such immovable property which the bailiff has alienated as heirless property shall be carried out in the presence of a police representative and the acquirer of the immovable property. If persons are encountered on the immovable property, the bailiff shall act in the procedure specified in Article 620.6 of this law.
(Edition of law 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.8 Disputes and complaints in connection with introduction into possession of immovable property
(Deleted by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Article 620.9 Handling of property transferred to custody

(1) The debtor has the right within one month to receive the property transferred to custody by paying the costs of execution of the judgment.

(2) If the debtor refuses to pay the costs of execution of the judgment, the bailiff shall seize the debtor's property in such value as is necessary to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but shall transfer the remaining property to the debtor.

(3) The seized property shall be sold by the bailiff in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(4) The money received from the sale of the property shall be credited to cover the costs of execution of the judgment, but any surplus of money shall be paid to the debtor. The bailiff shall notify the debtor of the sale of the property if he or she has information about the debtor's official electronic address, e-mail address or place of residence.

(5) If the debtor does not appear within one month to receive the property transferred to custody, the bailiff shall sell it in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 71 of this law.

(6) Property which has no market value or which cannot be sold and which the debtor has not appeared to receive within the time limit and procedure specified in the first paragraph of this Article shall be destroyed by the bailiff in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a record thereof.

(7) Property which has been described on immovable property alienated as heirless property and which has no market value shall be destroyed by the bailiff in the presence of witnesses, drawing up a record thereof, but the property description record in the part concerning property which has market value shall be sent by the bailiff to the notary who made the notarial deed on termination of the inheritance matter for amendments to be made therein.
(Edition of law 08.09.2011 with amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 74.3
Return of a child to the country of his or her place of residence

(3)	Bērna nodošana piedzinējam vai bāriņtiesas pārstāvim veicama pēc iespējas ātrāk.  

(4)	Bērna nodošanā piedalās tiesu izpildītājs, bāriņtiesas un policijas pārstāvji, kā arī psihologs, ja bāriņtiesa to ir pieaicinājusi. Par darbībām, kas saistītas ar telpu piespiedu atvēršanu, tiesu izpildītājs izdara atzīmi aktā.  

(6)	Ja bērns tiek nodots piedzinējam, tiesu izpildītājs par bērna nodošanu izdara atzīmi aktā, norādot, ka nolēmums ir izpildīts.

Pēc tam, kad saņemts bāriņtiesas paziņojums, ka bērns nogādāts atpakaļ uz valsti, kurā ir viņa dzīvesvieta, tiesu izpildītājs sastāda aktu par to, ka nolēmums ir izpildīts.

620.15 pants. Tiesu izpildītāja rīcība, ja bērnu nav iespējams nodot piedzinējam vai bāriņtiesas pārstāvim

## (Chapter 04

Edition of 08.2011 law, which enters into force on 01.10.2011.)

620.10 Article. Costs of enforcement of a decision and the procedure for their payment

(1) The creditor, when submitting an enforcement document for enforcement, shall pay the state fee and cover the costs of enforcement of the decision in accordance with the first part of Article 567 of this law.

(2) The creditor who does not participate in the enforcement of the decision shall, at the request of the bailiff, in addition to the costs of enforcement of the decision referred to in the first part of this Article, pay a sum of money to cover the costs associated with the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence (including costs associated with the child's stay in a crisis centre or other safe conditions, travel costs, costs for interpreter and psychologist services and other costs). The amount of these costs and the procedure for payment shall be determined by the Cabinet of Ministers.

(3) After the child has been handed over to the representative of the orphan's court, the bailiff shall immediately transfer the costs referred to in the second part of this Article to the account specified by the orphan's court.

(4) When issuing an enforcement document to the creditor (points 7 and 8 of the first part of Article 565 and the third part of Article 620.13), the bailiff or the orphan's court shall refund to the creditor the costs referred to in the second part of this Article that have not been used for the enforcement of the decision.

(5) The bailiff shall recover the costs of enforcement of the decision from the debtor.
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

620.10A Article. Time limit within which an enforcement document must be submitted for enforcement

An enforcement document for the return of a child to the country of his or her habitual residence, including a relevant European Union enforcement document, may be submitted for compulsory enforcement within one year from the date of entry into force of the court or foreign court decision.
(Edition of 16.06.2022 law, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.11 Article. Notice of the obligation to enforce the decision

(1) The bailiff, when commencing enforcement in the procedure established in Article 555 of this law, shall notify the debtor of the obligation to enforce the decision within 10 days. If the creditor submits the enforcement document for enforcement repeatedly after the bailiff has issued it to him or her in accordance with the third part of Article 620.13 of this law, the notice shall not be sent.

(2) Upon receiving for enforcement a European Union enforcement document which does not specify a time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision, the bailiff shall, in the procedure established in Article 555 of this law, send to the debtor a notice of the obligation to enforce

the decision within 30 days. In the notice, the bailiff shall warn the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that will occur if the decision is not enforced.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.12 Article. Consequences arising if the debtor does not enforce the decision voluntarily

(1) The bailiff shall send information that the debtor has not voluntarily enforced the decision to:

1) the district (city) court which adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence — upon receiving the said decision for enforcement;

2) the district (city) court in whose territory of operation the foreign court decision is to be enforced — after the expiry of the time limit for voluntary enforcement of the decision specified in the enforcement document or in accordance with Article 620.11 of this law.

(2) The court, upon receipt of the information referred to in the first part of this Article, shall impose a fine of 750 euros on the debtor.

(3) The issue of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The court decision on the imposition of a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision on the imposition of a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine shall not release the debtor from the obligation to enforce the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 12.09.2013, 09.06.2016, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

620.13 Article. Ascertaining the child's daily routine

(1) Simultaneously with the sending of the information referred to in the first part of Article 620.12 of this law, the bailiff, if necessary for the enforcement of the decision, shall give an order to the orphan's court according to the child's location to ascertain the child's daily routine within 15 days from the date of receipt of the order and to inform the bailiff thereof.

(2) The orphan's court shall immediately inform the bailiff of information relating to the child and the child's location which it has obtained in executing the order specified in the first part of this Article. If it is not possible to obtain the said information, the orphan's court shall inform the bailiff thereof. The bailiff, upon receiving information that the child's location is not known, shall, in accordance with Article 569 of this law, request the judge to adopt a decision on the search for the child or the child and the debtor with the assistance of the police and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

(3) The bailiff, having received from the orphan's court or the police information about the child's location which is in the territory of operation of the regional court to which this bailiff does not belong, shall make a note thereof in the enforcement document, indicating information about the child's location, and shall immediately issue the enforcement document to the creditor, explaining to him or her the right to submit the enforcement document for enforcement in accordance with the provisions of Article 549 of this law.

(4) (Deleted by the law of 29.10.2015)
(With amendments made by the law of 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

620.14 Article. Handing over of the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court

(1) Upon receiving the information referred to in the first part of Article 620.13 of this law, the bailiff shall determine the times and places when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement, and shall notify thereof:

1) the creditor, informing him or her of the creditor's right to be present at enforcement actions;

2) the orphan's court and the police according to the child's location, giving an order to their representatives to participate in compulsory enforcement. The orphan's court shall, at its discretion, invite a psychologist to participate in the compulsory enforcement of the decision.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the times and places when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement.

(3) The handing over of the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court shall be carried out as soon as possible.

(4) The handing over of the child shall be attended by the bailiff, representatives of the orphan's court and the police, as well as a psychologist if the orphan's court has invited one. At the time and place specified in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court, in cooperation with the psychologist if one has been invited, shall conduct conversations with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court if the creditor does not participate in the enforcement, as well as to prepare the child for return to the country of his or her habitual residence. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's order.

(5) If the bailiff is not allowed into premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, they shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after the forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave at the relevant immovable property or premises a notice with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(6) If the child is handed over to the creditor, the bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child, indicating that the decision has been enforced.

(7) If the child is handed over to the representative of the orphan's court for further actions to be taken to return the child to the country of his or her habitual residence, the bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child. A copy of the record shall be issued to the representative of the orphan's court. After receiving a notice from the orphan's court that the child has been returned to the country of his or her habitual residence, the bailiff shall draw up a record that the decision has been enforced.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

620.15 Article. Actions of the bailiff if it is not possible to hand over the child to the creditor or the representative of the orphan's court

If it is not possible for the orphan's court to obtain the information referred to in Article 620.13 of this law or the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence is not possible because the child has not been found at the times and places determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send this record to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide on the initiation of criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of enforcement of the decision, and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

620.16 Article. Refusal or postponement of enforcement of the decision

(1) The debtor may submit to the district (city) court which adopted the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence a proposal for postponement of enforcement of the decision or refusal of enforcement of the decision if a substantial change of circumstances has occurred.

(2) A substantial change of circumstances within the meaning of this Article shall include:

1) the fact that the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence is not possible due to the child's health or psychological condition, as evidenced by a hospital or psychiatrist's certificate;

2) the child's objections to his or her return to the country of his or her habitual residence, as evidenced by the opinion of a psychologist appointed by the orphan's court;

3) the fact that the creditor shows no interest in restoring contact with the child.

(3) The proposal referred to in the first part of this Article may be submitted if more than one year has passed since the decision on the return of the child to the country of his or her habitual residence (Article 644.20), except in the case referred to in point 1 of the second part of this Article.

(4) The application shall be examined at a court hearing, having previously notified the parties and the orphan's court thereof. The failure of these persons to appear shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(5) In the decision on postponement of enforcement of the decision, the court shall indicate the obligations of the debtor and the creditor during the time while enforcement of the decision is postponed and, if necessary, also the procedure for restoring contact between the child and the creditor.

(6) The decision shall be enforceable immediately. An appeal may be lodged against the court decision. The lodging of an appeal shall not suspend the enforcement of the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 29.10.2015 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force on 07.07.2022.)

Enforcement of decisions in matters arising from custody rights

620.17 Article. Notice of obligation to execute decision

The bailiff shall send or issue to the debtor a notice of the obligation to hand over the child to the creditor within 15 days in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law. In the notice, the bailiff warns the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that will arise if the decision is not executed.

620.18 Article. Civil procedural consequences arising if the debtor does not execute the decision

(1) If the debtor has not executed the decision within the time limit specified in the bailiff's notice, the bailiff shall send information about it to the district (city) court which adopted the decision in a case arising from custody rights, or in whose territory of operation a foreign decision is to be executed.

(2) The judge, upon receipt of the information referred to in paragraph one of this Article, shall impose a fine on the debtor of up to 1500 euros.

(3) The question of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The judge's decision on imposing a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision on imposing a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine does not release the debtor from the obligation to execute the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

620.19 Article. Ascertainment of child's daily routine

(1) If it is necessary for the execution of the decision, the bailiff shall issue an order to the orphan's court according to the child's location to ascertain the child's daily routine within 15 days from the date of receipt of the order and to inform the bailiff thereof.

(2) The orphan's court shall immediately inform the bailiff of information relating to the child and his or her location which it has obtained in executing the order specified in paragraph one of this Article. If it is not possible to obtain the said information, the orphan's court shall inform the bailiff thereof.

(3) The bailiff, having received information that the child's location is not known, in accordance with Article 569 of this law shall request the judge to adopt a decision on the search for the child or the child and the debtor with the assistance of the police and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

(4) The bailiff, having received from the orphan's court or the police information about the child's location, which is in the territory of operation of the regional court to which this bailiff does not belong, shall make a note thereof in the enforcement document, indicating information about the child's location, and shall immediately issue the enforcement document to the creditor, explaining to him or her the right to submit the enforcement document for execution in accordance with the provisions of Article 549 of this law.

620.20 Article. Handing over of child to creditor

(1) Having received the information referred to in paragraph one of Article 620.19 of this law, the bailiff shall determine the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor, and shall notify the creditor, the orphan's court and the police according to the child's location thereof, issuing an order to their representatives to participate in the forced execution. The orphan's court at its discretion shall invite a psychologist to participate in the forced execution of the decision.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor.

(3) The child shall be handed over to the creditor as soon as possible.

(4) If the creditor does not appear at the time and place determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall postpone the handing over of the child. If the creditor also does not appear repeatedly at the determined time and has not notified the reason for non-appearance or has not appeared for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the enforcement document shall be issued back to the creditor without execution.

(5) The bailiff, representatives of the orphan's court and the police, as well as a psychologist, if the orphan's court has invited one, shall participate in the handing over of the child. At the place and time determined in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court in cooperation with the psychologist, if one has been invited, shall conduct conversations with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located, in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor, as well as to prepare the child for handing over to the creditor. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's orders.

(6) If the bailiff is not allowed into premises about which there is information that the child is located therein, they shall be opened by force in the presence of a police representative. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after the forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave a notice at the relevant immovable property or premises with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the record of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(7) The bailiff shall make a note in the record of the handing over of the child to the creditor, indicating that the decision has been executed.

620.21 Article. Bailiff's action if it is not possible to hand over the child to the creditor

If it is not possible for the orphan's court to obtain the information referred to in Article 620.19 of this law or the handing over of the child to the creditor does not take place because the child is not found at the place and time determined by the bailiff, the bailiff shall draw up a record thereof and send it to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of execution of the decision, and shall also send the record to the orphan's court for evaluation of the debtor's conduct and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

## (Chapter 29

620.23 Article. Notice of obligation to execute decision

(1) If the decision (including a foreign court decision and a court decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights adopted in the procedure specified in Article 244.13 of this law, if the court has not ordered the forced opening of premises) specifies the procedure, time and place for the creditor's exercise of contact rights, the bailiff shall send to the debtor, in the procedure specified in Article 555 of this law, a notice of the obligation to execute the decision in the procedure, time and place specified therein. If the time and place are not specified in the decision, the bailiff shall determine the place of execution and the time of execution within a reasonable period, but not later than two weeks, unless otherwise follows from the decision. In the notice, the bailiff warns the debtor of the consequences provided for in this chapter that arise in the event of non-execution of the decision.

(2) If the decision specifies that contact rights are to be exercised at a specified place or in the presence of a contact person or a representative of the orphan's court, or a person authorised by the orphan's court, or at a specified place and in the presence of a contact person or a representative of the orphan's court, or a person authorised by the orphan's court, the bailiff shall also notify the contact person, the orphan's court and the user of the premises of the specified place of the time and place of execution of the decision, giving an order to the contact person or the representative of the orphan's court, or the person authorised by the orphan's court to participate in the execution and an order to the user of the premises of the specified place to ensure access to the specified place.
(With amendments made by the law of 16.06.2022, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

620.24 Article. Act on execution or non-execution of decision

(1) If, at the time and place determined by the bailiff, the debtor ensures the creditor's contact with the child in accordance with the procedure for exercising contact rights specified in the decision, the bailiff shall draw up an act that the decision is being executed. If, at the time and place indicated by the bailiff, the child is not found and the debtor has not notified the reason why the child is not found, or has notified a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, or the debtor refuses to execute the decision for a reason which the bailiff does not recognise as justifiable, the bailiff shall draw up an act on non-execution of the decision.

(2) If, at the time and place indicated by the bailiff, the child is not found, but the debtor has notified the reason why the child is not found, and the bailiff recognises this reason as justifiable, or the debtor refuses to execute the decision for a reason which the bailiff recognises as justifiable, the bailiff shall draw up an act on non-execution of the decision for justifiable reasons and shall determine a new time and place for execution of the decision.

620.25 Article. Civil procedural consequences arising if debtor does not execute decision

(1) The bailiff shall send the act on non-execution of the decision to the district (city) court which adopted the decision in the case arising from contact rights, or in whose territory of operation the foreign court decision is to be executed.

(2) The judge, upon receipt of the act referred to in paragraph one of this Article, shall impose a fine on the debtor of up to 1500 euros.

(3) The question of imposing a fine shall be examined in written proceedings.

(4) The judge's decision on imposing a fine shall be sent to the debtor.

(5) An appeal may be lodged against the court decision on imposing a fine.

(6) The fine shall be recovered from the debtor to state revenues.

(7) Payment of the fine shall not release the debtor from the obligation to execute the decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 09.06.2016 and 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which enters into force 07.07.2022.)

620.26 Article. Bailiff's action if it is not possible to hand over child to creditor

If, after the question of imposing a fine has been examined (Article 620.25), the debtor does not execute the order repeatedly given by the bailiff in accordance with the procedure specified in Article 620.23 of this law regarding the obligation to execute the decision and an act on non-execution of the decision has been repeatedly drawn up in accordance with paragraph one of Article 620.24 of this law, the bailiff shall send the said act to the prosecutor's office so that it may decide the question of initiating criminal proceedings against the debtor in connection with his or her malicious evasion of execution of the decision, and shall also send the act to the orphan's court for evaluation of the debtor's conduct and shall suspend enforcement proceedings.

620.27 Article. Issuance of enforcement document to creditor

If, after resumption of enforcement proceedings, the debtor continues not to execute the decision or there are other circumstances that make execution of the decision difficult or impossible, the bailiff shall return the enforcement document to the creditor, informing him or her of his or her rights under Article 244.13 of this law to request the court to review the procedure for exercising contact rights.

620.28 Article. Procedure for executing decision on review of time and place of exercise of contact rights if court has ordered forced opening of premises

(1) The bailiff, upon commencing execution of the court decision on the review of the time and place of exercise of contact rights adopted in the procedure specified in Article 244.13 of this law, taking into account the address indicated in the decision and the time period during which the premises may be opened by force, shall determine the time and place when and where the child will be handed over to the creditor for the exercise of contact, and shall notify:

1) the creditor, informing him or her of the creditor's obligation to be present at the enforcement actions;

2) the contact person in whose presence, in accordance with what is specified in the decision, contact rights are to be exercised, giving an order to this person to participate in the execution;

3) the orphan's court at the child's place of location, giving an order to its representative to participate in the forced execution. The orphan's court, at its discretion, shall involve a psychologist in the forced execution of the decision;

4) the police at the child's place of location, giving an order to its representative to participate in the forced execution.

(2) The bailiff shall not inform the debtor of the place and time where and when the child will be handed over to the creditor for the exercise of contact.

(3) At the place and time specified in the bailiff's order, the representative of the orphan's court, in cooperation with a psychologist, if one has been involved, shall conduct discussions with the debtor or other persons with whom the child is located, in order to persuade them to hand over the child to the creditor for the exercise of contact. Police representatives shall ensure public order and compliance with the bailiff's orders.

(4) If the bailiff is not admitted to the premises indicated in the court decision, they shall be opened by force. If no person older than seven years is found in the premises, the bailiff, after forced opening of the premises, without describing the property in the premises, shall ensure the secure closing and sealing of these premises. The bailiff shall leave a notice at the relevant immovable property or premises with an invitation to come to the bailiff's office to receive the keys to the premises. The bailiff shall make a note in the act of actions related to the forced opening of premises.

(5) If the child is handed over to the creditor, the bailiff shall draw up an act on execution of the decision.

(6) If contact rights are to be exercised at a specified place or in the presence of a contact person at another place that is not the place of execution, the child shall be handed over to the representative of the orphan's court or the contact person so that he or she, together with the creditor, may take the child to the specified place for the exercise of contact. The bailiff shall draw up an act on execution of the decision, indicating the person to whom the child has been handed over.

(7) If, when performing the actions specified in this Article, it was not possible to hand over the child to the creditor, the bailiff shall close the enforcement case without execution and shall inform the creditor of his or her rights under Article 244.13 of this law to request the court to review the procedure for exercising contact rights.
(With amendments made by the law of 11.11.2021, which enters into force 01.12.2021.)

### 621. Section. Issuance of Recovered Amounts to Creditors

(1)	From the amount that the bailiff has recovered from the debtor, enforcement costs are covered first, and from the remaining amount the claims of creditors that are substantiated by enforcement documents in the possession of this bailiff are satisfied. The amount that remains after satisfaction of all claims is returned to the debtor.  

(2)	Amounts that have been recovered from the debtor and are to be transferred to creditors are deposited into the bailiff's deposit account, and thereafter issued or transferred in the prescribed manner.  

(3)	Amounts that are to be credited to state revenues are paid by the bailiff into the State Treasury budget account.  

(4)	Amounts that have been recovered in favour of a person residing abroad are transferred to the creditor in the prescribed manner.  

(5)	Persons who have enforcement documents in other cases may join the enforcement by submitting the enforcement document to the bailiff who is organising the auction no later than seven days before the auction closing date indicated in the auction notice or until the date when the property has been handed over to a trading company for sale under commission terms.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009. and 28.05.2015., which enter into force on 02.07.2015.)

### 622. Section. Order of Satisfaction of Creditors' Claims

(1)	If the amount recovered from the debtor is insufficient to satisfy all claims under enforcement documents, this amount shall be divided among the creditors in the order specified in this law, unless a separate law establishes priorities for certain creditors.  

(2)	Claims of each subsequent priority are satisfied after complete satisfaction of claims of the previous priority.  

(3)	If the recovered amount is insufficient to fully satisfy all claims of one priority, these claims shall be satisfied proportionally to the amount due to each creditor.  

(4)	If there are several enforcement cases in the bailiff's proceedings that have been initiated for the claims referred to in the first paragraph of Section 623 of this law, and among them is an enforcement case in which the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration has been substituted for the creditor in part for the recovery from the debtor of maintenance payments that have been paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, and the recovered amount is insufficient to fully satisfy all claims, the recovered amount shall be divided proportionally to the calculated debt amount in the enforcement cases or the total amount of debts if there are several creditors in the case.  
(With amendments made by the law of 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017.)

### 623. Section. First Priority Enforcement

(1)	The following shall be satisfied first:

1)	claims for recovery of maintenance for a child or parent or claims of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration for recovery of maintenance debt;  

2)	claims for recovery of wages;  

3)	claims for personal injuries resulting in mutilation or other health damage or death of a person;  

4)	claims for compensation for harm satisfied in favour of a natural person in a criminal case.  

(2)	If maintenance is paid in accordance with a decision of the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration and the recovered maintenance amount:

1)	does not cover the amount of maintenance paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, the recovered maintenance is credited to the Maintenance Guarantee Fund;  

2)	covers the amount of maintenance paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, but does not cover the minimum amount of maintenance as determined by the Cabinet of Ministers on the basis of the fifth paragraph of Section 179 of the Civil Law, the recovered maintenance is paid to the applicant;  

3)	covers the minimum amount of maintenance as determined by the Cabinet of Ministers on the basis of the fifth paragraph of Section 179 of the Civil Law, then the maintenance in the amount specified by the Cabinet of Ministers is paid to the applicant, and the remaining amount is credited to the Maintenance Guarantee Fund until complete repayment of the debt.  

(3)	If the bailiff's proceedings include an enforcement case for recovery of maintenance for a child and a case in which the Maintenance Guarantee Fund Administration has been substituted for the same creditor in part for the recovery from the debtor of maintenance that has been paid from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund, but the payment of maintenance to the creditor from the Maintenance Guarantee Fund has been terminated because the debtor's obligation to provide monthly maintenance to his or her child has ended, the recovered maintenance is credited to the Maintenance Guarantee Fund until complete repayment of the debt.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 17.06.2004., 09.06.2011., 08.12.2016., 22.06.2017., 21.01.2021. and 25.03.2021.  
which enters into force on 20.04.2021.)

### 624. Section. Second Priority Enforcement

In the second priority, claims for taxes and non-tax payments to the budget shall be satisfied.

### 625. Section. Third Priority Enforcement

In the third priority, the following shall be satisfied:

1)	claims of natural persons for compensation for damage caused to their property by a criminal offence, if compensation for damage has been determined on the basis of a court judgment in a civil case or administrative violation;  

2)	claims for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management expenses), for payments for services necessary for the maintenance of the building (utility services) and payments to the apartment owners' association reserve fund (reserves), which are payable for this immovable property.  
(In the wording of the law of 21.01.2021., which enters into force on 01.03.2021. See transitional provision 162)

### 626. Section. Fourth Priority Enforcement

In the fourth priority, all other claims shall be satisfied.

### 627. Section

Distribution of Money Received from the Sale of Movable Property Encumbered by a Pledge

From the money received for the sale of movable property encumbered by a pledge, enforcement costs are covered first, then claims are satisfied in the following order:

1)	the claim secured by the pledge;  

2)	other claims in the order specified in this law.

### 628. Section

Distribution of money received from the sale of mortgaged immovable property

(1) From the money received for the sale of mortgaged immovable property, first the costs of enforcement of the judgment related to the sale of the immovable property shall be covered, then claims shall be satisfied in the following order:

1) claims of those employees for payment of wages who are related to the maintenance of the immovable property, and social insurance payments related to their wages;

2) claims for tax payments payable for this immovable property;

21) claims for payments for management activities in a multi-apartment residential building (management expenses), for payments for services necessary for the maintenance of the building (utility services) and payments to the accumulation fund of the apartment owners' association (accumulations) payable for this immovable property;

3) real burdens registered in the Land Register for which the payment term has arrived;

4) claims secured by the mortgage of this immovable property according to their priority;

5) other claims in the order specified in this law, including the claims specified in point 2.1 of this paragraph in their unsatisfied part.

(11) When satisfying claims in the order specified in point 2.1 of the first paragraph of this section, they shall be covered in an amount that in total does not exceed 5 percent of the money received for this immovable property.

(2) When satisfying mortgage claims according to their priority, their ancillary claims shall also be satisfied simultaneously — interest for the last three years until the day of conclusion of the auction, awarded court costs and costs related to the conduct of the case, not exceeding the mortgage sum registered in the Land Register. In the remaining part not secured by the mortgage (hypothec) of the immovable property, the claim shall be satisfied in the order specified in Section 622 of this law.

(21) If the mortgage creditor has not joined the enforcement (fifth paragraph of Section 621), the money in the amount of the mortgage sum indicated in the Land Register or in the amount indicated in the mortgage creditor's notice, if such has been received (fourth paragraph of Section 600), taking into account the priority of the respective mortgage claim, shall be deposited in the deposit account of the bailiff who conducted the auction and kept until receipt of the enforcement documents.

(3) If immovable property has been sold at auction in respect of which a note of pledge right is registered in the Land Register, the money in the amount of the claim according to the priority of the claim shall be deposited in the bailiff's deposit account and kept until the secured claim is examined in court.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 05.02.2009., 28.05.2015. and 21.01.2021., which enter into force on 01.03.2021. See transitional provision point 161)

### 629. Section. Distribution of money received from the sale of a ship

From the money received for the sale of a ship, the costs of enforcement of the judgment shall be covered and other claims satisfied, taking into account the second paragraph of Section 56 of the Maritime Code.
(In the wording of the law of 19.06.2003., which enters into force on 24.07.2003.)

### 630. Section

Order of enforcement in cases where the debtor's property has been confiscated by a judgment in a criminal case

(1) When executing a judgment in a criminal case on confiscation of property, the bailiff shall pay the funds obtained by executing the judgment on confiscation of property into the State Treasury budget account after all claims submitted to the debtor that arose before the convicted person's property was seized or pledged by the preliminary investigation authorities or the court have been satisfied.

(2) Claims for maintenance and claims for personal injury resulting in mutilation or other health damage or death of a person shall be satisfied even if they arose after the seizure or pledging of the convicted person's property.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002. and 22.06.2017., which enters into force on 01.08.2017.)

### 631. Section. Calculation prepared by the bailiff

(1) If the court has recognized the claimant's right to receive interest on the awarded sum until the execution of the judgment (the day of conclusion of the auction) or if the obligation to pay interest is specified in another law, the bailiff shall prepare a calculation of the total sum to be paid to the claimant.

(2) If there are several claimants and if the sum recovered from the debtor is insufficient to fully satisfy all claims, the bailiff shall prepare a calculation for the distribution of money among the claimants and issue it to the claimants and the debtor.

(3) If the auction of immovable property has been declared not to have taken place and the creditor, co-owner or last outbid bidder has expressed a wish to retain the immovable property for themselves, the bailiff shall prepare a calculation to determine the sum due from this person.

(4) The calculation prepared by the bailiff may be appealed to the district (city) court according to the bailiff's place of office. An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 19.06.2003., 17.06.2004., 05.02.2009., 28.05.2015. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

Chapter 76
Protection of the rights of the claimant, debtor and other persons when executing a court judgment

### 632. Section. Appeal of the bailiff's actions

(1) The bailiff's actions in the execution of a judgment or their refusal to perform such actions, except for the case specified in Section 617 of this law, may be appealed by the claimant or debtor by submitting a reasoned complaint to the district (city) court according to the bailiff's place of office within 10 days from the day of performance of the appealed action or the day when the complainant, who has not been notified of the time and place of the action to be performed, became aware of it.

(2) The complaint shall be examined in a court session within 15 days. The debtor and the claimant, as well as the bailiff, shall be notified of the court session. The non-appearance of these persons is not an obstacle to the examination of the matter.

(3) At the reasoned request of the complainant, the judge may adopt a decision in the procedure specified in Section 140 of this law to postpone the enforcement action, to prohibit the bailiff from transferring money or property to the claimant or debtor, or to suspend the sale of property. The decision shall be executed immediately after its adoption.

(4) An appeal may be submitted against the court's decision.
(With amendments made by the laws of 31.10.2002., 19.06.2003. and 05.02.2009., which enters into force on 01.03.2009.)

### 633. Section. Protection of the rights of other persons when executing a decision

(1) A person who believes that they have any rights to the described movable property or immovable property against which enforcement is directed, or a part thereof, shall bring an action in court according to general jurisdiction.

(2) An action for exclusion of property from the description act, deletion of the enforcement note in the Land Register or another action shall be brought against the debtor and the claimant. If property has been described on the basis of a judgment in a criminal case in the part on confiscation of property, the convicted person and the financial institution shall be summoned as defendants.

(3) If the property has already been sold, the action shall also be submitted against the persons to whom the property has been transferred. If the court satisfies the action in respect of immovable property, the entry in the Land Register on the transfer of ownership rights to its acquirer shall be declared invalid.

(4) Disputes between the acquirer, claimant and debtor, if an action for the return of sold property in kind has been satisfied, shall be examined by the court in action proceedings.
(With amendments made by the law of 31.10.2002., which enters into force on 01.01.2003.)

### 634. Section. Reversal of execution of judgment

(1) If an executed judgment is revoked and after a new examination of the case a judgment is made to reject the claim or a decision is adopted to terminate the proceedings in the case or to leave the case without examination, the defendant shall return everything that was recovered from them in favour of the plaintiff according to the revoked judgment (reversal of execution of judgment).

(2) If it is not possible to return the property in kind, the judgment or decision of the court shall provide for compensation of the value of this property.

### 635. Section. Decision on reversal of judgment enforcement

(1) The court to which the case has been referred for a new hearing shall, on its own initiative, examine the question of reversal of judgment enforcement and decide it in the new judgment or decision by which the proceedings in the case are concluded.

(2) If the court hearing the case anew has not decided the question of reversal of enforcement of the annulled judgment, the defendant is entitled to submit to that court an application for reversal of judgment enforcement. This application shall be examined at a court hearing, having notified the parties to the case in advance. The non-appearance of these persons shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.

(3) The court of cassation, if it amends the appealed (protested) judgment by its judgment, annuls it and terminates the proceedings in the case or leaves the application without examination, shall decide the question of reversal of judgment enforcement or refer its decision to the court whose judgment was appealed.

(4) If the court of appeal rejects the claim in a case in which the court of first instance, in accordance with Section 205 of this law, has allowed immediate enforcement of the judgment, or terminates the proceedings in such a case or leaves the claim without examination, it shall simultaneously decide the question of reversal of judgment enforcement.

(5) If the judgment is annulled due to newly discovered circumstances or due to review of the decision in cases provided for in European Union legal norms, the question of reversal of judgment enforcement shall be decided by the court which, after annulment of the judgment, hears the case anew.

(6) In cases concerning recovery of maintenance, recovery of wages, recovery of damages in connection with personal injuries resulting in mutilation or other health damage or death of a person, reversal of judgment enforcement is permissible if the annulled judgment was based on false information provided by the claimant or on forged documents submitted by him or her.

(7) An appeal may be lodged against the court's decision on the question of reversal of judgment enforcement.
(With amendments made by the law of 08.09.2011, which enters into force on 30.09.2011. Part six, insofar as it relates to reversal of judgment enforcement in cases concerning recovery of wages, has been declared invalid from 01.11.2015 by the judgment of the Constitutional Court of 16.04.2015, which enters into force on 20.04.2015.)

Part F International Civil Procedure
(Part in the wording of the law of 07.04.2004, which enters into force on 01.05.2004.)

Section Fifteen International Civil Procedural Cooperation

Chapter 77
Recognition and enforcement of foreign court decisions

### 636. Section. Foreign court decision

(1) A foreign court decision within the meaning of this chapter is a judgment adopted by a foreign court by which a dispute between the parties has been decided on the merits, as well as a settlement approved by a foreign court.

(2) A foreign court decision within the meaning of this chapter is also a decision of a foreign competent authority that is enforceable in the country of its adoption, if the recognition and enforcement of the decision follows from directly applicable European Union legal norms or international agreements binding on the Republic of Latvia.
(In the wording of the law of 07.09.2006, which enters into force on 11.10.2006.)

### 637. Section. Recognition of a foreign court decision

(1) A foreign court decision shall be recognised in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, observing the general provisions of this law.

(2) A foreign court decision shall not be recognised only if one of the following grounds for non-recognition exists:

1) the foreign court which adopted the decision was not competent, in accordance with Latvian law, to hear the respective dispute or such a dispute is subject to exclusive jurisdiction of a Latvian court;

2) the foreign court decision has not entered into legal force;

3) the defendant has been denied the opportunity to defend his or her rights, in particular if the defendant who has not participated in the hearing of the case has not been notified in a timely and proper manner of the appearance in court, except if the defendant has not appealed this decision, although he or she has had such an opportunity;

4) the foreign court decision is incompatible with a court decision already adopted in Latvia and having entered into legal force in the same dispute between the same parties or with proceedings already initiated in a Latvian court between the same parties;

5) the foreign court decision is incompatible with a decision of another foreign court already adopted and having entered into legal force in the same dispute between the same parties, which is recognisable or has already been recognised in Latvia;

6) recognition of the foreign court decision is contrary to the public order of Latvia;

7) when adopting the foreign court decision, the law of the country that should have been applied in accordance with the conflict of laws norms of Latvian private international law has not been applied.

(3) A foreign court decision in cases arising from guardianship, trusteeship or contact rights shall not be recognised only if at least one of the grounds for non-recognition referred to in points 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 of part two of this section exists or one of the following grounds for non-recognition exists:

1) the foreign court decision is incompatible with a court decision later adopted in Latvia and having entered into legal force in the same dispute between the same parties or with proceedings later initiated in a Latvian court between the same parties;

2) the foreign court decision is incompatible with a decision of another foreign court later adopted and having entered into legal force in the same dispute between the same parties, which is recognisable or has already been recognised in Latvia.

(31) A foreign court decision in cases concerning recovery of maintenance, which amends a decision on recovery of maintenance already adopted earlier, on the basis that circumstances have changed, shall not be considered an incompatible judgment within the meaning of points 4 and 5 of part two of this section.

(4) When deciding the question of whether a foreign court decision is recognisable in accordance with part two of this section, the judge or court shall be guided by the circumstances established by the foreign court decision.

(5) If several claims combined in one claim have been satisfied by a foreign court decision and this decision is not recognisable in full, the foreign court decision may be recognised in respect of one or more satisfied claims.
(With amendments made by the laws of 07.09.2006 and 29.10.2015, which enters into force on 03.12.2015.)

### 638. Section. Submission of Application

(1)	An application for recognition or recognition and enforcement of a foreign court judgment shall be submitted for examination to the district (city) court according to the place of enforcement of the judgment or according to the respondent's declared place of residence, but if there is none — according to the respondent's place of residence or registered address.

(2)	The application shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the application is submitted;

11)	the applicant's name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none — other identification data) and address for communication with the court; for a legal person — its name, registration number and registered address. If the applicant agrees to electronic communication with the court, an email address shall also be indicated and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;

12)	the respondent's name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, then other identification data), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there is none — place of residence; for a legal person — its name, registration number and registered address;

2)	(deleted by law of 29.11.2012.);

3)	the subject matter of the application and the circumstances on which the application is based;

4)	the applicant's request to recognize or recognize and enforce the foreign court judgment in full or in part;

5)	the representative's email address and, if registered in the online system for communication with the court, also a reference to the registration, if the application is submitted by a representative whose address for communication with the court is in Latvia and he or she agrees to electronic communication with the court. If the applicant's representative's address is outside Latvia, an email address shall additionally be indicated or notification of registration of participation in the online system shall be given;

6)	a list of attached documents;

7)	the time of preparation of the application.

(21) An application in a case concerning recognition or declaration of enforceability of a foreign court judgment on maintenance in cases provided for in European Union and international treaties, using the forms specified in the relevant legal acts, may be submitted or transmitted through the intermediary of the Latvian central authorities appointed to ensure cooperation.

(3)	The following shall be attached to the application:

1)	the foreign court judgment with confirmation that the judgment has entered into legal force;

2)	a document issued by the foreign court certifying that the respondent who did not participate in the examination of the case was notified in due time and in proper manner of the time and place of examination of the case;

3)	a document issued by the foreign court or competent institution concerning the enforcement of the judgment, if the foreign court judgment has already been partially enforced;

4)	a document issued by the foreign court certifying that the foreign court judgment is enforceable in the country of its adoption, if the applicant requests recognition and enforcement of the foreign court judgment;

5)	a translation into the official language of the application and the documents referred to in points 1, 2 and 3 of this paragraph certified in the prescribed manner;

6)	a document confirming payment of the state fee in the manner and amount prescribed by law, except where the application has been submitted and payment made in the online system".

(4)	The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative. If the application is signed by a representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court with the application shall be attached to the application.

(5)	An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.

(6)	The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authority to apply to the court with this application is not attached. The decision is not subject to appeal.
(With amendments made by laws of 02.09.2004., 07.09.2006., 09.06.2011., 08.09.2011., 29.11.2012., 23.04.2015.,
29.10.2015., 23.11.2016., 01.06.2017. and 11.11.2021., which enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 639. Section. Leaving Application Without Movement

If the application does not comply with the requirements of the second and third paragraphs of Section 638 of this Law or if the power of attorney or other document attached to the application does not show the authority of the representative to apply to the court with this application, the judge shall leave the application without movement and the consequences provided for in Section 133 of this Law shall occur.
(In the wording of law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 640. Section. Determination of Application

A decision on recognition and enforcement of a foreign court judgment or a decision to reject the application shall be adopted by the judge individually on the basis of the submitted application and the documents attached thereto within 10 days after initiation of the case, without summoning the parties.
(With amendments made by law of 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 641. Section

Appeal of Entry into Force of Decision of First Instance Court and Appellate Court

(1)	An appeal may be submitted to the regional court against a decision of the first instance court in a case of recognition of a foreign court judgment, and a decision of the regional court on an appeal may be appealed to the Supreme Court by submitting an appeal.

(2)	A party to the case whose declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence or registered address is in Latvia may submit the appeal referred to in the first paragraph of this Section within 30 days from the date of issue of the decision, but a party to the case

whose declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence or registered address is not in Latvia — within 60 days from the date of issue of the decision.

(21) In cases provided for in Council Regulation No 4/2009, a party to the case whose declared place of residence, but if there is none — place of residence or registered address is not in Latvia may submit the appeal referred to in the first paragraph of this Section within 45 days from the date of issue of the decision.

(3)	The decision of the first instance court and the decision of the appellate court shall enter into legal force after the time limit for appeal thereof has expired, counting from the later date of issue of the decision, and no appeal has been submitted.

(4)	If in the case referred to in the third paragraph of this Section the relevant confirmation of issue of the decision has not been received, the decision shall enter into legal force six months after its pronouncement.
(With amendments made by laws of 05.02.2009., 09.06.2011., 29.11.2012., 30.10.2014. and 11.11.2021., which
enters into force on 01.12.2021.)

### 642. Section. Competence of Regional Court

(1)	The regional court, when examining an appeal, shall have the right to:

1)	leave the decision unchanged and reject the appeal;

2)	annul the decision in full or in part and decide the question of recognition of the foreign court judgment;

3)	amend the decision.

(2)	The court may request explanations from the parties or additional information from the foreign court that adopted the judgment.

(21) When applying Council Regulation No 4/2009, the appeal shall be examined within the time limits set out in Article 34 of Council Regulation No 4/2009.

(3)	The court, at the request of the respondent, may suspend proceedings if the foreign court judgment has been appealed in the relevant foreign country in the general procedure or the time limit for such appeal has not expired. In the second case, the court may set a time limit within which an appeal must be submitted for appeal of the foreign court judgment in the relevant foreign country.
(With amendments made by laws of 09.06.2011., 30.10.2014. and 23.04.2015., which enters into force on 26.05.2015.)

### 643. Section. Securing Enforcement of Foreign Court Judgment

(1)	Upon application of the applicant, the judge or court in the decision by which the foreign court judgment is recognized may determine the measures provided for in Section 138 or Chapter 77.3 of this Law for securing enforcement of the foreign court judgment.

(2)	Submission of the appeal referred to in the first paragraph of Section 641 of this Law shall not suspend execution of the decision of the judge or court in the part concerning securing enforcement of the foreign court judgment. Submission of an appeal against such a decision in a case of recognition of a foreign court judgment by which the securing of enforcement of the foreign court judgment has been cancelled or the security measure has been changed shall suspend execution of the decision in this part.
(With amendments made by laws of 07.09.2006. and 08.12.2016., which enters into force on 04.01.2017. Amendments to the Section in connection with the European Account Preservation Order enter into force on 18.01.2017. See transitional provision point 121)

(1)	A foreign court judgment that is enforceable in the country of its adoption shall be enforced, after its recognition, in the procedure specified in this Law.

(2)	With regard to the procedure for declaring a judgment enforceable as provided for in the Lugano Convention of 30 October 2007 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, Council Regulation No 2201/2003, Council Regulation No 4/2009 and Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 4 July 2012 on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and acceptance and enforcement of authentic instruments in matters of succession and on the creation of a European Certificate of Succession (hereinafter – Regulation No 650/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council), the provisions of Chapter 77 of this Law on the recognition of foreign court judgments shall apply insofar as the provisions of the relevant conventions and regulations permit.

(3)	In the cases provided for in Council Regulation No 2201/2003, Regulation (EC) No 805/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Regulation (EC) No 861/2007 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Council Regulation No 4/2009, Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 of the European Parliament and of the Council, Regulation (EU) No 655/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111, foreign court judgments shall be enforceable in the procedure specified in this Law without requiring recognition of the foreign court judgment or a declaration of enforceability of the foreign court judgment.

644.1 pants. Deferral of enforcement of a foreign court judgment, division of enforcement into instalments, change of the method or procedure of enforcement

(1)	The court that has adopted a decision on the recognition and enforcement of a foreign court judgment may, upon application by a party to the case, defer the enforcement of the foreign court judgment, divide the enforcement into instalments, or change the method or procedure of enforcement.

(11) The district (city) court in whose territory of operation a foreign court judgment is to be enforced, in respect of which a certificate referred to in point (b) or (c) of Article 36(1) or point (a) or (b) of Article 47(1) of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111 has been issued, may, upon receipt of an application by the debtor, on the basis of Article 56(4) of that Regulation, defer the enforcement of the foreign court judgment.

(3)	A decision on deferral of enforcement of a foreign court judgment, division into instalments, or change of the method and procedure of enforcement shall be enforceable immediately. 644.6 Article. Procedure for Examining Cases

Cases concerning the provision of an opinion to a foreign court regarding the lawfulness of the cross-border removal to a foreign country or retention in a foreign country of a child whose habitual residence is in Latvia shall be examined in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, observing the general provisions of this law.  
(As amended by the law of 14.12.2017, which entered into force on 15.01.2018.)

644.7 Article. Application for the Provision of an Opinion to a Foreign Court in a Case Concerning the Lawfulness of a Child's Cross-Border Removal to a Foreign Country or Retention in a Foreign Country

(1)	If a foreign court is examining a case concerning the return to Latvia of a child wrongfully removed to or retained in that foreign country, at the request of that court, a person whose rights to exercise custody or guardianship have been infringed, as well as an orphan's court or a prosecutor, may submit to the court an application for the provision of an opinion to the foreign court regarding the lawfulness of the child's removal from Latvia across the border to a foreign country or retention in a foreign country. The application referred to in this paragraph may be submitted if the relevant foreign country whose court is examining the case concerning the return to Latvia of a child wrongfully removed to or retained in that foreign country is a contracting state to the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction or the Hague Convention of 19 October 1996 on Jurisdiction, Applicable Law, Recognition, Enforcement and Co-operation in Respect of Parental Responsibility and Measures for the Protection of Children.  

(11) The application referred to in paragraph one of this Article may also be submitted to the court by a person whose rights to exercise custody or guardianship have been infringed, as well as by an orphan's court or a prosecutor, even if no request from a foreign court has been received, but the said person, orphan's court or prosecutor considers that the provision of such an opinion to the foreign court is expedient.  

(2)	Cases concerning the provision of an opinion to a foreign court in a case concerning the wrongful cross-border removal of a child to a foreign country or retention in a foreign country, if the child's habitual residence is in Latvia, shall be examined by the Riga City Court.  

(21) (Deleted by the law of 30.10.2014)

(3)	The application shall indicate:

1)	the name of the court to which the application is submitted;  

2)	the applicant's given name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none — other identification data), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, but if there are none — place of residence, as well as an address in Latvia for communication with the court in order to receive court documents. If the applicant agrees to electronic communication with the court, an e-mail address shall also be indicated and, if he or she has registered in the online system for communication with the court, a reference to the registration shall also be included;  

3)	the given name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, date of birth) of the wrongfully removed or retained child and other information about the child, as well as information about the child's possible location and the identity of the person with whom the child might be;  

4)	the respondent's given name, surname, personal identity number (if there is none, other identification data), declared place of residence and additional address indicated in the declaration, as well as place of residence if it differs from the declared place of residence and the additional address indicated in the declaration, or information about his or her location;  

5)	circumstances confirming the applicant's custody or guardianship rights;  

6)	circumstances confirming the fact of the child's wrongful removal or retention and the civil law aspects;  

7)	the applicant's request;  

8)	a list of attached documents;  

9)	the time of preparation of the application.  

(4)	Documents on which it is based and the request of the foreign court, if any, shall be attached to the application.  

(5)	The application shall be signed by the applicant or his or her representative. If the application is submitted by the applicant's representative, a power of attorney or other document certifying the authorisation to apply to the court with this application shall be attached to the application. If the address of the applicant's representative is outside Latvia, an e-mail address shall additionally be indicated or notification shall be given of the registration of his or her participation in the online system.  

(6)	An unsigned application shall be considered as not submitted and shall be sent back to the submitter.  

(7)	The judge shall adopt a decision to refuse to accept the application if a power of attorney or other document certifying the representative's authorisation to apply to the court with this application is not attached to it. The decision is not subject to appeal.  
(With amendments made by the laws of 04.08.2011, 29.11.2012, 30.10.2014, 23.04.2015, 23.11.2016, 01.06.2017,
14.12.2017, 11.11.2021 and 16.06.2022, which entered into force on 01.08.2022.)

644.8 Article. Leaving the Application Without Progress

If the application does not comply with the requirements of paragraphs three and four of Article 644.7 of this law or if the authorisation for the representative to apply to the court with this application does not follow from the power of attorney or other document attached to the application, the court shall leave the application without progress and the consequences provided for in Article 133 of this law shall ensue.  
(As amended by the law of 23.04.2015, which entered into force on 26.05.2015.)

644.9 Article. Examination of the Application

(1)	The application shall be examined at a court hearing within 15 days after the initiation of the case, with the participation of the submitter of the application and a representative of the relevant orphan's court. The orphan's court shall have the rights of a participant in the case as provided for in paragraph two of Article 88 of this law.  

(2)	The respondent shall be notified of the court hearing. The non-appearance of this person shall not be an obstacle to the examination of the application.  

(3)	The court shall adopt a decision by which it provides an opinion to the foreign court regarding the lawfulness of the child's removal from Latvia across the border to a foreign country or retention in a foreign country.  

(4)	If the court establishes that the child is in Latvia, it shall adopt a decision to leave the application without examination.  

(5)	When examining the application, the court shall request evidence on its own initiative.  

(6)	(Deleted by the law of 14.12.2017)

(7)	The court's decision shall enter into force immediately and is not subject to appeal.  
(As amended by the law of 04.08.2011 with amendments made by the laws of 29.11.2012, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

644.10 Article. Competence of the Regional Court
(Deleted by the law of 14.12.2017, which entered into force on 15.01.2018.)

644.11 Article. Action After Adoption of the Decision

(1)	The court shall submit the adopted decision by which an opinion has been provided to the foreign court regarding the lawfulness of the child's removal from Latvia across the border to a foreign country or retention in a foreign country to the Ministry of Justice if the request for the return of the child to Latvia has been submitted to the foreign country through the intermediary of the Ministry of Justice.  

(2)	(Deleted by the law of 12.06.2009)

(3)	The court on its own initiative or the Ministry of Justice shall attach to the court documents information about the provisions of Latvian regulatory enactments.  

(With amendments made by the laws of 12.06.2009, 14.12.2017 and 11.11.2021, which entered into force on 01.12.2021.)

644.12 Article. Consequences of a Decision Adopted by a Foreign Court or Competent Authority Regarding the Non-Return of a Child

(1)	A decision of a foreign court or competent authority and other documents regarding the non-return of a child to Latvia, which have been adopted on the basis of Article 13 of the Hague Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, may be submitted to the court in Latvia through the intermediary of the Ministry of Justice in accordance with point 3 of Article 29 of Council Regulation (EU) 2019/1111.  

(2)	The Ministry of Justice, having received the documents referred to in paragraph one of this Article, shall send them to the court in whose proceedings the case is for examination on the merits, informing the relevant orphan's court of the decision of the foreign court or competent authority.  

(3)	(Deleted from 01.08.2022 by the law of 16.06.2022. See transitional provision 177)
